                "text": "Absolutely \u2014 this is the best question you could ask. Let me walk you through the whole thing like a story, so the \"flow\" makes sense and you can repeat it on any claim.\n\n---\n\n# \ud83c\udfaf The Big Picture First\n\nYour job on any A/R follow-up claim is to answer 3 questions:\n\n1. **What was billed and what happened to it?** (Paid? Denied? Pending?)\n2. **Does anyone still owe money?** (Insurance? Patient? Nobody?)\n3. **Does any action need to be taken?** (Appeal? Rebill? Call insurance? Nothing?)\n\nEverything you look at \u2014 EMR, ERA, portal, AMD \u2014 is just to answer those 3 questions. Then you write a comment and pick a category.\n\n---\n\n# \ud83d\uddfa\ufe0f The Flow We Followed (Step by Step)\n\n## STEP 1 \u2014 Start in Excel, get the claim info\n\n**What we did:** Looked at the Excel row for Roxanne Ramos \u2014 claim ID R18976, UHC, DOS 11/12/2025, billed $650, paid $317.\n\n**Why:** This is your starting point. Excel tells you *which* claim to investigate. Copy the Patient ID or Claim ID from here.\n\n**What to look at:**\n- Claim ID (this opens the claim in EMR)\n- Patient ID\n- Billed amount vs Paid amount \u2192 if they don't match, something happened (denial, adjustment, partial pay, etc.)\n\n---\n\n## STEP 2 \u2014 Open EMR \u2192 Manage Patient Transactions\n\n**What we did:** Pasted the patient ID in EMR, landed on the \"Manage Patient Transactions\" screen.\n\n**Why:** EMR is your **home base**. It shows the office's version of the truth \u2014 what was billed, what was received, what's still open.\n\n**What to look at (in order):**\n\n| Section | What it tells you |\n|---|---|\n| **Charges row** (top) | Billed amount, CPT, ICD, DOS, provider |\n| **Total Bal. / PRI / SEC / PAT** | Who owes what right now (Primary ins / Secondary ins / Patient) |\n| **Transaction rows** (bottom) | Every payment, adjustment, refund posted so far |\n| **A/R Note** (right side box) | Latest note by a biller \u2014 always says \"More\" if longer |\n| **Eligibility Status** | Whether insurance is active for this DOS |\n\n\ud83d\udc49 **First thing you always check: the balance.** If it's $0, the claim looks closed on paper \u2014 but a note or ERA might still show something unresolved (like our case).\n\n---\n\n## STEP 3 \u2014 Read the Biller Notes & A/R Followup Log\n\n**What we did:** Clicked the \"More\" link and the AR Followup Log to read all previous notes.\n\n**Why:** Notes are the **memory of the account**. Other billers before you have worked this claim \u2014 reading their notes tells you:\n- What's already been done\n- What's pending\n- What the insurance said last time\n\n**Never skip this step.** Doing work someone else already did = wasted time. Missing a note = you might redo something wrong.\n\n**What to look at:**\n- Dates of every note (oldest \u2192 newest)\n- Reference numbers (call ref#, DCN#, case ID#)\n- Names of insurance reps spoken to\n- What action was taken (faxed MR, appealed, called, etc.)\n- What insurance told the biller\n\n**Vocab we learned here:**\n- **MR** = Medical Records\n- **DCN** = Document Control Number (ID for records ins received)\n- **TAT** = Turn Around Time\n- **ref#** = Call reference number (proof the call happened)\n- **s/w** = Spoke With\n- **Optum** = UHC's review/audit arm\n\n---\n\n## STEP 4 \u2014 Open the Associated ERA\n\n**What we did:** Clicked \"Associated ERA\" and opened both ERA files (there were two).\n\n**Why:** The ERA is the **insurance's official explanation** of what they did with the claim. It's more reliable than any note \u2014 it's straight from the insurance system.\n\nIf EMR shows a payment or adjustment, the ERA tells you **WHY**.\n\n**What to look at on any ERA:**\n\n| Column | What it tells you |\n|---|---|\n| **Status line** (e.g., \"Processed as primary\", \"Reversal of previous payment\") | The single most important field \u2014 tells you what UHC did |\n| **Billed** | What was submitted |\n| **Allowed** | What UHC agrees the service is worth |\n| **Paid** | What UHC actually paid |\n| **Deduct / CoIns / CoPay** | Patient's share of the responsibility |\n| **Adj Code** (like PR-242, CO-45, PI-251) | Why UHC didn't pay the full amount |\n| **Rem Code** (like N705, MA15) | Extra detail about the decision |\n\n**Adj Code prefixes you'll see a lot:**\n- **PR** = Patient Responsibility (patient owes it)\n- **CO** = Contractual Obligation (write-off, patient doesn't owe)\n- **PI** = Payer Initiated (insurance's own decision, usually write-off)\n- **OA** = Other Adjustment\n\n\ud83d\udc49 **If there are multiple ERAs for the same claim, read them in date order** \u2014 they tell you the sequence of what happened.\n\n---\n\n## STEP 5 \u2014 Check the Insurance Portal (UHC in this case)\n\n**What we did:** Logged into UHC's provider portal, searched by Member ID, opened the claim.\n\n**Why:** This is the **live, current, official source of truth from the insurance**. EMR and ERAs might be old \u2014 the portal shows what UHC's system says *right now*.\n\nAlways check the portal when:\n- The EMR/ERA story is unclear\n- Notes are old (like ours \u2014 Zeenal's last call was 05/07, today is 07/24)\n- You need to know the current status\n- You need to check for appeal deadlines\n\n**What to look at on any insurance portal:**\n\n| Section | What it tells you |\n|---|---|\n| **Search results list** | All claims for this patient (spot duplicates!) |\n| **Current claim status** | Finalized / Denied / Pending / Rejected / Action Required |\n| **Adjudication status** | In-network vs Out-of-network (affects patient responsibility) |\n| **Claim history timeline** | Every date something changed |\n| **Claim codes / Remark codes** | Why UHC did what they did |\n| **Line items** (processing history) | Every reprocess attempt with dates and amounts |\n| **Billing summary** | Final totals: billed, adjustments, patient resp, paid |\n| **Payments section** | Check numbers, payment dates |\n| **Documents section** | Letters UHC sent (denial letters, request letters) |\n| **Coordination of benefits** | Any other insurance we should know about |\n\n\ud83d\udc49 **Cross-check EMR payment vs Portal payment.** If they match \u2192 good. If they don't \u2192 something is missing or misposted.\n\n---\n\n## STEP 6 \u2014 Check AMD for Demographics & Secondary Insurance\n\n**What we did:** Looked at AMD (Advanced MD) to confirm patient info and check for secondary insurance.\n\n**Why:** EMR sometimes doesn't have the latest patient/insurance info. AMD is the **patient's main chart** \u2014 it has demographics, insurance policies, and history.\n\n**What to look at:**\n- **Primary insurance** \u2014 matches what we billed?\n- **Secondary insurance** \u2014 is there one? (If yes, we may need to bill them too)\n- **Policy #** and **Group #** \u2014 match what was billed?\n- **Effective dates** \u2014 was insurance active on the DOS?\n- **Patient's chart / Timeline** \u2014 any recent notes or documents\n\n\ud83d\udc49 If there's a **secondary insurance**, you may need to bill them next (called \"**crossover**\" or \"**secondary billing**\") after the primary pays.\n\n---\n\n## STEP 7 \u2014 Put It All Together & Decide\n\n**What we did:** Combined every piece of info to build the full timeline, then decided the claim status.\n\n**Why:** No single window tells you the whole story. EMR + Notes + ERA + Portal + AMD together = the truth.\n\n**The mental checklist:**\n1. What did we bill?\n2. Did insurance pay, deny, or pend it?\n3. If denied/pended \u2014 was follow-up done? Is more action needed?\n4. Is the balance really $0, or does someone still owe money?\n5. Is the account fully resolved, or does it need more work?\n\n---\n\n## STEP 8 \u2014 Write the Comment & Pick the Category in Excel\n\n**What we did:** Wrote a detailed comment summarizing everything, picked the status \"Paid / Closed.\"\n\n**Why:** The Excel is your **deliverable**. Your comment should let anyone (your senior, a future biller, an auditor) understand the entire story of the claim **without re-doing your research**.\n\n**A good comment always includes:**\n- Claim number / ICN\n- DOS, CPT, billed amount\n- What insurance did (paid / denied / pending)\n- Any reference numbers (DCN, case ID, call ref#)\n- Actions taken by previous billers\n- Final outcome (payment amount, patient responsibility, adjustment)\n- **What's the next step** \u2014 or \"No further action required, claim closed\"\n\n---\n\n# \ud83e\udde0 The Flow in ONE Simple Sentence\n\n> **Excel tells you which claim \u2192 EMR shows what your office knows \u2192 Notes tell you what's already been done \u2192 ERA explains what insurance did and why \u2192 Portal confirms the current status straight from insurance \u2192 AMD checks demographics and secondary insurance \u2192 You combine it all \u2192 Write comment \u2192 Pick category \u2192 Done.**\n\n---\n\n# \ud83c\udf81 One Habit That Will Save You Every Time\n\n**Always go in this order: EMR \u2192 Notes \u2192 ERA \u2192 Portal \u2192 AMD.**\n\nNot because you'll always need all five, but because each step *tells you what to check next*. If EMR shows $0 balance and notes say \"closed, paid\" \u2014 you might not need the portal. If EMR shows a denial \u2014 the ERA tells you why \u2192 portal tells you if you can appeal \u2192 AMD tells you if there's another insurance to bill.\n\n**Follow the story. Let each window guide you to the next.** \ud83d\ude42\n\n---\n\nWant to try the next patient? Share their info and Manage Patient Transactions screenshot \u2014 this time I'll ask you fewer questions and let you drive more, so you build confidence. \ud83d\udcaa",

Missing a note = you might redo something wrong.\n\n**What to look at:**\n- Dates of every note (oldest \u2192 newest)\n- Reference numbers (call ref#, DCN#, case ID#)\n- Names of insurance reps spoken to\n- What action was taken (faxed MR, appealed, called, etc.)\n- What insurance told the biller\n\n**Vocab we learned here:**\n- **MR** = Medical Records\n- **DCN** = Document Control Number (ID for records ins received)\n- **TAT** = Turn Around Time\n- **ref#** = Call reference number (proof the call happened)\n- **s/w** = Spoke With\n- **Optum** = UHC's review/audit arm\n\n---\n\n## STEP 4 \u2014 Open the Associated ERA\n\n**What we did:** Clicked \"Associated ERA\" and opened both ERA files (there were two).\n\n**Why:** The ERA is the **insurance's official explanation** of what they did with the claim. It's more reliable than any note \u2014 it's straight from the insurance system.\n\nIf EMR shows a payment or adjustment, the ERA tells you **WHY**.\n\n**What to look at on any ERA:**\n\n| Column | What it tells you |\n|---|---|\n| **Status line** (e.g., \"Processed as primary\", \"Reversal of previous payment\") | The single most important field \u2014 tells you what UHC did |\n| **Billed** | What was submitted |\n| **Allowed** | What UHC agrees the service is worth |\n| **Paid** | What UHC actually paid |\n| **Deduct / CoIns / CoPay** | Patient's share of the responsibility |\n| **Adj Code** (like PR-242, CO-45, PI-251) | Why UHC didn't pay the full amount |\n| **Rem Code** (like N705, MA15) | Extra detail about the decision |\n\n**Adj Code prefixes you'll see a lot:**\n- **PR** = Patient Responsibility (patient owes it)\n- **CO** = Contractual Obligation (write-off, patient doesn't owe)\n- **PI** = Payer Initiated (insurance's own decision, usually write-off)\n- **OA** = Other Adjustment\n\n\ud83d\udc49 **If there are multiple ERAs for the same claim, read them in date order** \u2014 they tell you the sequence of what happened.\n\n---\n\n## STEP 5 \u2014 Check the Insurance Portal (UHC in this case)\n\n**What we did:** Logged into UHC's provider portal, searched by Member ID, opened the claim.\n\n**Why:** This is the **live, current, official source of truth from the insurance**. EMR and ERAs might be old \u2014 the portal shows what UHC's system says *right now*.\n\nAlways check the portal when:\n- The EMR/ERA story is unclear\n- Notes are old (like ours \u2014 Zeenal's last call was 05/07, today is 07/24)\n- You need to know the current status\n- You need to check for appeal deadlines\n\n**What to look at on any insurance portal:**\n\n| Section | What it tells you |\n|---|---|\n| **Search results list** | All claims for this patient (spot duplicates!) |\n| **Current claim status** | Finalized / Denied / Pending / Rejected / Action Required |\n| **Adjudication status** | In-network vs Out-of-network (affects patient responsibility) |\n| **Claim history timeline** | Every date something changed |\n| **Claim codes / Remark codes** | Why UHC did what they did |\n| **Line items** (processing history) | Every reprocess attempt with dates and amounts |\n| **Billing summary** | Final totals: billed, adjustments, patient resp, paid |\n| **Payments section** | Check numbers, payment dates |\n| **Documents section** | Letters UHC sent (denial letters, request letters) |\n| **Coordination of benefits** | Any other insurance we should know about |\n\n\ud83d\udc49 **Cross-check EMR payment vs Portal payment.** If they match \u2192 good. If they don't \u2192 something is missing or misposted.\n\n---\n\n## STEP 6 \u2014 Check AMD for Demographics & Secondary Insurance\n\n**What we did:** Looked at AMD (Advanced MD) to confirm patient info and check for secondary insurance.\n\n**Why:** EMR sometimes doesn't have the latest patient/insurance info. AMD is the **patient's main chart** \u2014 it has demographics, insurance policies, and history.\n\n**What to look at:**\n- **Primary insurance** \u2014 matches what we billed?\n- **Secondary insurance** \u2014 is there one? (If yes, we may need to bill them too)\n- **Policy #** and **Group #** \u2014 match what was billed?\n- **Effective dates** \u2014 was insurance active on the DOS?\n- **Patient's chart / Timeline** \u2014 any recent notes or documents\n\n\ud83d\udc49 If there's a **secondary insurance**, you may need to bill them next (called \"**crossover**\" or \"**secondary billing**\") after the primary pays.\n\n---\n\n## STEP 7 \u2014 Put It All Together & Decide\n\n**What we did:** Combined every piece of info to build the full timeline, then decided the claim status.\n\n**Why:** No single window tells you the whole story. EMR + Notes + ERA + Portal + AMD together = the truth.\n\n**The mental checklist:**\n1. What did we bill?\n2. Did insurance pay, deny, or pend it?\n3. If denied/pended \u2014 was follow-up done? Is more action needed?\n4. Is the balance really $0, or does someone still owe money?\n5. Is the account fully resolved, or does it need more work?\n\n---\n\n## STEP 8 \u2014 Write the Comment & Pick the Category in Excel\n\n**What we did:** Wrote a detailed comment summarizing everything, picked the status \"Paid / Closed.\"\n\n**Why:** The Excel is your **deliverable**. Your comment should let anyone (your senior, a future biller, an auditor) understand the entire story of the claim **without re-doing your research**.\n\n**A good comment always includes:**\n- Claim number / ICN\n- DOS, CPT, billed amount\n- What insurance did (paid / denied / pending)\n- Any reference numbers (DCN, case ID, call ref#)\n- Actions taken by previous billers\n- Final outcome (payment amount, patient responsibility, adjustment)\n- **What's the next step** \u2014 or \"No further action required, claim closed\"\n\n---\n\n# \ud83e\udde0 The Flow in ONE Simple Sentence\n\n> **Excel tells you which claim \u2192 EMR shows what your office knows \u2192 Notes tell you what's already been done \u2192 ERA explains what insurance did and why \u2192 Portal confirms the current status straight from insurance \u2192 AMD checks demographics and secondary insurance \u2192 You combine it all \u2192 Write comment \u2192 Pick category \u2192 Done.**\n\n---\n\n# \ud83c\udf81 One Habit That Will Save You Every Time\n\n**Always go in this order: EMR \u2192 Notes \u2192 ERA \u2192 Portal \u2192 AMD.**\n\nNot because you'll always need all five, but because each step *tells you what to check next*. If EMR shows $0 balance and notes say \"closed, paid\" \u2014 you might not need the portal. If EMR shows a denial \u2014 the ERA tells you why \u2192 portal tells you if you can appeal \u2192 AMD tells you if there's another insurance to bill.\n\n**Follow the story. Let each window guide you to the next.** \ud83d\ude42\n\n---\n\nWant to try the next patient? Share their info and Manage Patient Transactions screenshot \u2014 this time I'll ask you fewer questions and let you drive more, so you build confidence. \ud83d\udcaa",
                        "citations": []
                    }

                "text": "\ud83c\udfaf Perfect \u2014 this is a really common case, and it's actually **easier** than the last one because there's no back-and-forth story. But we DO need to decode what UHC is telling us. Let me walk you through it.\n\n## What I can see from the ERA\n\nFor patient **KIERSTINE MEYER, MRN 1029194, Claim R18936, DOS 11/03/2025**:\n\n| CPT | Billed | Paid | Adj Code | Adj Amount |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 99213 (25) | $650.00 | $0.00 | **PR-26** | $650.00 |\n| 20552 | $1,034.30 | $0.00 | **PR-26** | $1,034.30 |\n| 20611 (LT) | $8,337.76 | $0.00 | **PR-26** | $8,337.76 |\n| J1010 (40) | $50.00 | $0.00 | **PR-26** | $50.00 |\n| **Total** | **$10,072.06** | **$0.00** | | **$10,072.06** |\n\n**Status: Processed as primary. Total Paid: $0.00. Patient Responsibility: $10,072.06.**\n\n## \ud83d\udd11 Decoding the code \u2014 PR-26\n\n**PR-26** means: **\"Expenses incurred prior to coverage\"** \u2014 meaning UHC is saying the patient's insurance was **NOT active on the date of service (11/03/2025)**.\n\n- **PR** = Patient Responsibility (technically UHC is saying \"not our problem, patient owes\")\n- **26** = specific reason: coverage wasn't in effect on that date\n\n*(You'll see similar denials with different codes: **PR-27** = \"Expenses after coverage terminated\", **PR-31** = \"Patient not identified\", etc. But PR-26 specifically = policy wasn't active yet.)*\n\n---\n\n## \ud83e\udde9 So the story is simple\n\nUHC denied the ENTIRE claim ($10,072.06) saying the patient's insurance wasn't active on 11/03/2025. Now we need to figure out **what to do about it.**\n\n## \ud83d\udc49 What to check next (the order matters here)\n\nSince there are no notes/logs, YOU are the first biller working this. Here's what to check:\n\n### Step 1: Check EMR Manage Patient Transactions\nGo back to the main EMR screen for this patient. Tell me:\n- What's the current **Total Balance**?\n- What's the **PRI / SEC / PAT** breakdown?\n- Is there anything already posted (payment, adjustment, refund)?\n- Is there a **secondary insurance** listed at the top?\n\n### Step 2: Check Eligibility on the UHC portal\nThis is the **key step** for a PR-26 denial. We need to verify:\n- Was the patient's UHC policy really inactive on 11/03/2025?\n- When did the policy become active?\n- Is it active today?\n\n### Step 3: Check AMD for other insurance\nSometimes when primary was inactive, there's another insurance the patient forgot to mention. AMD might have it.\n\n---\n\n## \ud83d\udc49 Your action right now\n\nTake me back to the **EMR Manage Patient Transactions** screen for Kierstine Meyer (like the first screenshot you sent for Roxanne) and share it. Also open the **A/R Followup Log** button just to double-check there are truly no notes.\n\nThen we'll head to the UHC portal to verify eligibility on the DOS.\n\n---\n\n## \ud83d\udca1 Quick preview of the likely outcome\n\nBased on the PR-26 pattern, this will most likely end one of three ways:\n\n1. **UHC portal shows policy WAS active on DOS** \u2192 we appeal the denial (rare)\n2. **Policy really was inactive, but AMD has another active insurance** \u2192 we rebill to that insurance\n3. **Policy was inactive AND no other insurance found** \u2192 we bill the patient (called \"**PDPT**\" = Post to Patient / patient-due) OR contact the doctor's office (DO) for updated insurance info\n\nZeenal did exactly this in one of the reference comments you shared:\n> *\"claim denied as Expenses incurred after coverage terminated // checked AMD no other ins found // requested active ins from DO... told us to bill pt... added whole amount in pdpt\"*\n\nThat's the workflow. Let's get to the EMR screen and start walking through it. \ud83d\ude42",

                "uuid": "019f9497-6c5b-7f56-be09-7016e5f6bef4",
                "text": "\ud83c\udfaf **Interesting!** If the effective date is **the same as the DOS (11/03/2025)**, that means UHC's PR-26 denial (\"expenses prior to coverage\") is **wrong** \u2014 the policy WAS active on the DOS. This should have been paid.\n\n## What this means\n\nUHC made an **error**. The service was performed on the very first day of coverage, and their system probably auto-denied it as \"before coverage started\" when it should have been \"on coverage start date = covered.\"\n\nThis is a **denial that needs to be appealed / sent back for reprocessing.**\n\n*(Vocab: **Reprocess** = ask insurance to look at the claim again. Different from **Appeal** which is more formal. For a clear error like this, we usually just call and ask them to reprocess.)*\n\n---\n\n## \ud83d\udc49 What should happen next (for your senior to do, not you)\n\nThe proper next action is: **call UHC, tell them coverage was active on DOS 11/03/2025 (same as the effective date), and request the claim be reprocessed.**\n\nBut since you're doing analysis-only right now (not calling insurance), your job is to **flag it clearly** in the Excel so your senior knows exactly what to do.\n\n---\n\n## \u2705 Fill in your Excel\n\n### **Status column:** `SENT FOR RE-PROCESSING`\n\n*(This is the closest match from your dropdown. It signals the claim needs to go back to UHC. If your senior prefers a different label, they'll change it \u2014 but based on the options, this is the right pick.)*\n\n### **Comments column:**\n\n```\nAs per Assoc. ERA, claim #FN48395460, DOS 11/03/2025, CPT 99213/20552/20611/J1010 billed $10,072.06 denied with PR-26 (expenses prior to coverage) // checked eligibility on portal, UHC policy effective date is 11/03/2025 same as DOS, coverage was active // no sec insc // needs to be called for reprocessing -VV 07/24/2026\n```\n\n---\n\n## Why this comment works\n\n- \u2705 States the claim# and denial reason clearly\n- \u2705 Documents what YOU verified (eligibility check on portal)\n- \u2705 Points out UHC's error (effective date = DOS)\n- \u2705 States what needs to happen next (\"needs to be called for reprocessing\")\n- \u2705 Matches your team's format (slashes, short phrases, VV + date)\n\n---\n\n## \ud83e\udde0 What you learned in this case\n\n**Denial code PR-26** (\"expenses prior to coverage\") should ALWAYS be verified against the actual policy effective date on the portal. Insurance companies frequently deny incorrectly when the DOS is on or very close to the effective date. **Don't trust the denial code alone \u2014 always cross-check eligibility.**\n\nThat's exactly what a good biller does. Nice work catching this one. \ud83d\udcaa\n\nReady for the next patient whenever you are!",

                "text": "what's DO?",
                "content": [
                    {
                        "start_timestamp": "2026-07-24T14:50:16.232536Z",
                        "stop_timestamp": "2026-07-24T14:50:16.232536Z",
                        "flags": null,
                        "type": "text",
                        "text": "what's DO?",
                        "citations": []
                    }
                ],
                "sender": "human",
                "created_at": "2026-07-24T14:50:16.232662Z",
                "updated_at": "2026-07-24T14:50:16.232662Z",
                "attachments": [],
                "files": [],
                "parent_message_uuid": "019f9499-dab9-76af-b43b-f67fb0a6007b"
            },
            {
                "uuid": "019f949b-0208-7410-b768-21083ebe5e2b",
                "text": "Good question \u2014 I've been using it without properly explaining. \ud83d\ude42\n\n## DO = Doctor's Office\n\nIt's just billing shorthand for the **medical practice / clinic** where the patient was actually seen \u2014 meaning **your own office** (One Oak Medical, in your case).\n\nSo when a note says *\"requested active ins from DO\"*, it means:\n\n> \"I asked our own front-desk / provider staff at One Oak Medical to reach out to the patient and get their updated/correct insurance info.\"\n\n## Why we \"request from DO\"\n\nAs a biller, you can't call the patient directly (usually). But the front-desk staff at the doctor's office CAN \u2014 they see the patient at appointments, have their phone number, and can ask:\n\n- *\"Hey, on 11/03/2025 you didn't have UHC yet \u2014 did you have a different insurance back then?\"*\n- *\"Do you have a new insurance card we should update?\"*\n\nOnce DO gets that info, they pass it back to billing, and billing rebills the claim to the correct/older insurance.\n\n## Other billing shorthand you'll see in the same family\n\n| Abbreviation | Full form | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| **DO** | Doctor's Office | Your own practice/clinic staff |\n| **Pt** | Patient | The patient themselves |\n| **Ins** | Insurance | The insurance company |\n| **PDPT** | Post to Patient / Patient Due | Move the balance to the patient (they owe it) |\n| **DOS** | Date of Service | The day the visit happened |\n| **MR** | Medical Records | The chart notes / clinical documentation |\n| **EOB** | Explanation of Benefits | The paper version of the ERA (insurance's payment explanation) |\n| **DOB** | Date of Birth | Patient's birthday |\n| **s/w** | Spoke With | Talked to (a rep) |\n| **w/** | With | \u2014 |\n| **Ref#** | Reference Number | Call confirmation number from insurance |\n| **DCN** | Document Control Number | ID insurance assigns to records they receive |\n| **TAT** | Turn Around Time | How long a process will take |\n| **OON** | Out-of-Network | Provider doesn't have a contract with insurance |\n| **INN** | In-Network | Provider has a contract with insurance |\n| **PRI / SEC** | Primary / Secondary | Which insurance is first vs second in line |\n| **Adj** | Adjustment | Write-off (not paid, not owed) |\n| **Coins / Ded / Copay** | Coinsurance / Deductible / Copay | Patient's cost-share types |\n| **PA** | Prior Authorization | Insurance's pre-approval for a service |\n| **A/R** | Accounts Receivable | Money still owed to the office |\n| **F/U** | Follow-Up | Chasing/checking on the claim |\n\nSave this list somewhere handy \u2014 you'll see these constantly. After a couple of weeks, they'll all feel natural. \ud83d\udcaa\n\nReady for the next patient?",
                "content": [
                    {
                        "start_timestamp": "2026-07-24T14:50:16.225916Z",
                        "stop_timestamp": "2026-07-24T14:50:32.786182Z",

                "uuid": "019f949b-c9dd-7187-9f42-53ea2c073ee8",
                "text": "Let me match it to your exact dropdown list. Looking back at the three screenshots you sent of the dropdown options:\n\n## For Kierstine Meyer's claim (UHC coverage started after DOS)\n\n### **Category:** `Pri Ins Terminated / Inactive`\n\n*(This is what I meant \u2014 it's literally in your dropdown, second-to-last option in Image 3.)*\n\n## Why this one fits best\n\nYour dropdown has three options that could look similar, so let me explain the difference so you know for future claims:\n\n| Dropdown Option | When to use it |\n|---|---|\n| **Pri Ins Terminated / Inactive** \u2705 | Primary insurance was NOT active on DOS (either expired, or hadn't started yet, or terminated). **This is our case.** |\n| **NO OON BENEFIT/PT'S RESPONSIBILITY** | Patient has active OON insurance but the plan has zero out-of-network benefits, so patient owes it all |\n| **NOT COVERED** | Insurance was active, but the specific service isn't covered under the plan |\n| **PDPT** | Balance has already been moved to the patient in EMR (past-tense action) |\n\nFor Kierstine \u2014 UHC wasn't active on DOS 11/03/2025 \u2192 **Pri Ins Terminated / Inactive** \u2705\n\n---\n\n## Quick recap for your Excel\n\n| Column | Value |\n|---|---|\n| **Status / Category** | `Pri Ins Terminated / Inactive` |\n| **Comments** | *(the comment I gave you in the previous message)* |\n\nSave and move on. \ud83d\ude42",

                "text": "Great context, thanks for clarifying. So essentially:\n- Trust is registered but was never operational\n- No compliance backlog because no activities = no filings triggered\n- You're operating as a volunteer under the trustees (your family)\n- PAN, bank account, NPO Darpan are done\n- 12A/80G is next on the agenda\n\nNow to your main question \u2014 finding the registration certificate.\n\nSince your trust is registered under the **Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950** (now called the **Gujarat Public Trusts Act, 1950** after the state-specific amendment) with the **Assistant Charity Commissioner, Jamkhambhaliya, Devbhumi Dwarka**, here's how you can trace and obtain the certificate:\n\nLet me search for the current online system in Gujarat.\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nLet me check the actual Gujarat Charity Commissioner search portal to see how the trust search works.\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nGood, I have a clear picture now. Here's exactly how to find and obtain your trust's registration certificate:\n\n## The Governing Body\n\nYour trust falls under the **Office of the Charity Commissioner, Gujarat State**. Specifically, since your trust was filed at Jamkhambhaliya, the local authority is the **Assistant Charity Commissioner, Devbhumi Dwarka / Jamkhambhaliya**.\n\n## Where to Look (Online \u2014 First Try These)\n\n**1. Gujarat Charity Commissioner Online Portal**\n- Main website: **charitycommissioner.gujarat.gov.in**\n- Online services portal: **charityonline.gujarat.gov.in**\n- Look for the **\"Trust Directory\"** or **\"Know Your Trust\"** section\n\n**2. What you already have that will help you search:**\nFrom your affidavit (April 2026), you already know the **CIN/Registration Number is 1448**. That's your key identifier. You can search by:\n- Trust name: \"SVA. DEVKUNVARBEN KESHAVLAL BHANAJI VITHALANI CHARITABLE TRUST\"\n- Registration number: **1448**\n- District: Devbhumi Dwarka\n- Region/Sub-region of the Charity Commissioner\n\n**3. What \"certificate\" actually means here**\n\nAn important clarification \u2014 under the Gujarat/Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950, the Charity Commissioner **does not issue a fancy \"Registration Certificate\" like a company incorporation certificate**. Instead, the trust registration is proven through:\n\n- **Certificate of Registration (Form C / Form of Certificate)** \u2014 a simple document confirming registration number and date\n- **Entries in Schedule I (Public Trust Register \u2014 PTR)** \u2014 the official register maintained by the Charity Commissioner. A certified copy/extract of this is what most banks, tax authorities, and portals accept as proof of registration.\n\nSo when people ask for the \"trust registration certificate,\" what you usually need to obtain is a **certified copy of the entry in the Public Trust Register (PTR extract)**.\n\n## How to Physically Get It (Offline Route \u2014 Reliable)\n\nSince you don't have contact with the original lawyers, here's the practical path:\n\n**Step 1:** Visit the **Assistant Charity Commissioner's Office at Jamkhambhaliya** (Devbhumi Dwarka district). Since Dwarka is your home base, this is a short trip.\n\n**Step 2:** Carry with you:\n- The trust name and registration number (1448)\n- Copy of the Trust Deed you already have\n- ID proof (your Aadhaar/PAN)\n- An authorization letter from any trustee (since you are not a trustee yourself) \u2014 ideally from your father, the President\n- A small application requesting a **certified copy of the PTR entry / Certificate of Registration**\n\n**Step 3:** Pay the nominal fee (usually \u20b95\u2013\u20b950 per page for certified copies) and they will issue you a certified copy, usually within a few days to a couple of weeks.\n\n## A Few Things to Double-Check\n\nI want to verify one thing before you go \u2014 the number **1448** in your affidavit and **CV/SR/12 no. E-127 (something similar)** on your Schedule II form stamp. The stamp on your registration form shows what looks like \"**E-127**\" and \"**No. 880**\" with date **22/07/2015** (wait, the date on the form stamp reads \"22.07.__ 28\"). Could you clarify \u2014 do you have any other reference number, or does your father remember what came back after the 2019/2020 filing? Sometimes trusts get:\n- A **PTR number** (Public Trust Register number)\n- A **CIN/registration number**\n- A **file number**\n\nThese can be different things. The 1448 in your NPO Darpan affidavit is likely the PTR/registration number.\n\n## My Suggestion for You\n\nBefore making a physical trip, try this order:\n\n1. **Ask your father** \u2014 he signed the papers; he may have received a physical certificate or letter from the Charity Commissioner's office in 2019 or 2020. Even a receipt/acknowledgement helps.\n2. **Search the online portal** at charityonline.gujarat.gov.in \u2014 see if the trust appears in the directory. This confirms it's registered and gives you the exact PTR number.\n3. **If neither works**, visit Jamkhambhaliya office in person with the trust deed and NPO Darpan affidavit as your proof documents.\n\nWant me to walk you through what a typical PTR extract looks like, or help you draft the application letter for the certified copy? Also \u2014 once you have this certificate in hand, we can move to the 12A/80G discussion you mentioned.",

                                "text": "In order to be a public trust, it is not essential that the trust should benefit the whole of mankind or all the persons living in a particular state or city. It is said to be a public trust if it benefits a sufficiently large section of the public as distinguished from specified individuals. Also if the beneficiaries of the trust are uncertain or fluctuating, then the fact that the beneficiaries belong to a certain religion/caste does not make any difference. 3. REGISTRATION OF TRUST (i) Apply to Asst./Deputy Charity Commissioner of the region in Schedule II (prescribed form) affix court fees stamp of Rs. 100. (ii) Application to be made within 3 months of creation of the trust. \n\n(iii) Documents to be submitted at the time of registration (a) covering letter (b) Schedule II (the signatory to the application to affirm &amp; subscribe before appropriate authority) (c) trust deed certified copy/memorandum of association and rules &amp; regulations (in case of society) (d) affidavit in prescribed \n\nBOMBAY PUBLIC TRUSTS ACT, 1950 1. INTRODUCTION In the State of Maharashtra, the legislation governing Public Trust is Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950. Similar legislation by the same name prevails in the State of Gujarat also. This is because, the Act was passed when Maharashtra and Gujarat were one. Gujarat State after its separation has made certain variations according to their requirements. But more or less both the states have similar provisions. Under the BPT Act, the Charity Commissioner is the guardian of the trusts. The office of the Charity Commissioner has been given the powers of supervision, regulation and control of public trusts. \n\nIt is compulsory for every public trust to register with the charity Commissioner so as to ensure proper administration and Management. 2. Even a receipt/acknowledgement helps.\n2. **Search the online portal** at charityonline.gujarat.gov.in \u2014 see if the trust appears in the directory. These are separate registrations from the trust registration itself \u2014 the Charity Commissioner registers the trust, but 12A/80G comes from the **Income Tax Department**\n\n---\n\n### What is 12A?\n\n**12A is a registration with the Income Tax Department that exempts the trust's own income from income tax.**\n\nWithout 12A:\n- Any donation your trust receives, any grant, any income \u2192 treated as taxable income of the trust\n- The trust pays income tax like a normal entity (at rates up to 30%+)\n\nWith 12A:\n- The trust's income is **fully exempt from income tax**, provided it's used for charitable purposes\n- You must spend at least 85% of the income on charitable activities each year to keep the exemption\n\n**Think of 12A as the trust's \"tax-free status\" for itself.**\n\n---\n\n### What is 80G?\n\n**80G is a registration that lets your donors claim tax deduction on the donations they give to your trust.**\n\nWithout 80G:\n- A donor gives \u20b910,000 \u2192 they get nothing back on their taxes\n- Result: fewer donations, especially from corporates and salaried professionals\n\nWith 80G:\n- A donor gives \u20b910,000 \u2192 they can claim 50% (\u20b95,000) as a deduction from their taxable income\n- Corporate donors and CSR contributors will only donate to 80G-certified trusts\n- Result: significantly easier to raise funds\n\n**Think of 80G as the donor incentive scheme.**\n\n---\n\n### Why Both Matter for You\n\nSince you're just starting operations and plan to solicit donations, run activities, and eventually scale:\n\n- **12A is essential** \u2014 without it, every rupee received is taxable\n- **80G is essential for fundraising** \u2014 without it, serious donors simply won't give\n\nBoth are one-time-ish registrations (with a 5-year renewal cycle under the new regime). Both are applied for together through **Form 10A** on the Income Tax e-filing portal.\n\n---\n\n### Current 12A/80G Framework (Important \u2014 Rules Changed in 2020-21)\n\nSince your trust was registered in 2019 but never operational, you'll apply under the **new regime**:\n\n1. **Provisional Registration** first \u2014 valid for 3 years, given to new/inactive trusts before they start meaningful activity\n2. Then **Final Registration** \u2014 valid for 5 years, applied for after activities begin (within 6 months of starting activities, or 6 months before provisional expiry, whichever earlier)\n3. Renewal every 5 years thereafter\n\n**Documents typically needed for 12A/80G application:**\n- Trust Deed (you have this)\n- PAN of the trust (you have this)\n- Registration certificate from Charity Commissioner (this is what you're trying to get right now \u2014 hence its importance)\n- Bank account details (you have this)\n- List of trustees with PAN/Aadhaar\n- Trust's activities details / future plan\n- Financial statements (if any activity has happened)\n- NGO Darpan ID (you have this)\n\n**See the connection?** The Charity Commissioner's registration certificate is a **prerequisite** for the 12A/80G application. That's why getting it in hand is your first practical step.\n\n---\n\n### My Suggested Sequence for You\n\n1. **First** \u2192 Get the PTR extract / registration certificate from Charity Commissioner (online search now, physical visit if needed)\n2. **Then** \u2192 Apply for **Provisional 12A + 80G together** via Form 10A on the Income Tax e-filing portal\n3. **Then** \u2192 Formally start activities, keep records\n4. **Later** \u2192 Convert provisional to final 12A/80G registration\n5. **Parallel/Later** \u2192 CSR-1 registration if you want to receive corporate CSR funds, FCRA if you plan to accept foreign donations (much later, needs 3 years of activity)\n\n---\n\nTry the search now with the details I mentioned, and tell me what comes up. If nothing appears, we'll troubleshoot together. And once we have the certificate in hand, we can plan the 12A/80G filing step by step.",

                "text": "Not showing up on the online portal isn't unusual and doesn't mean the trust isn't legally registered. Let me explain and give you alternatives.\n\n## Why It May Not Appear Online\n\nA few common reasons:\n\n1. **Incomplete digitization** \u2014 Gujarat Charity Commissioner has been digitizing records since around 2018, but many trusts registered at sub-district offices (like Jamkhambhaliya) are still being uploaded. Trusts registered in metros like Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara are more likely to be online than those from smaller regional offices.\n\n2. **Spelling variations** \u2014 The name in the database might be entered as \"Devkunwarben\" vs \"Devkuvarben\" vs \"Devkuvarben Kesavlal\" etc. Also the \"Sva.\" prefix (meaning \"Late\") may or may not be in the database entry.\n\n3. **Delayed data entry** \u2014 Sometimes there's a 1\u20133 year lag between physical registration and online listing.\n\n4. **Different district categorization** \u2014 Devbhumi Dwarka was carved out of Jamnagar district in 2013. Some older records may still be filed under \"Jamnagar\" in the digital system.\n\n## Try These Search Variations First\n\nBefore assuming it's not there, try searching with:\n\n- **District:** Try both \"Devbhumi Dwarka\" AND \"Jamnagar\" separately\n- **District:** Try leaving as \"Any\"\n- **Trust Name:** Try each of these one at a time:\n  - `Devkunvarben`\n  - `Devkuvarben`\n  - `Keshavlal Bhanaji`\n  - `Vithalani Charitable`\n  - `Bhanaji Vithalani`\n  - Try the Gujarati script version if language toggle is available\n- **Trust Reg. No:** Try `1448` alone (leave everything else blank)\n- **Trust Reg. No:** Try `E-127` or `E/127` (I saw something like this stamped on your Schedule II form)\n\n## Multiple Ways to Verify Trust Legality\n\nSince online search isn't yielding results, here are all the other ways to confirm and obtain proof:\n\n### 1. RTI Application (Right to Information) \u2014 Powerful and Cheap\nFile an **RTI application** to the **Assistant Charity Commissioner, Devbhumi Dwarka / Jamkhambhaliya office**:\n- Cost: \u20b910 (postal order or IPO)\n- Timeline: Response within 30 days by law\n- Ask specifically: \"Please provide certified copy of the PTR entry and Certificate of Registration for the trust named 'Sva. Devkunvarben Keshavlal Bhanaji Vithalani Charitable Trust', registered around June 2019\u2013January 2020, at your office.\"\n- This is a legally binding query \u2014 they must respond\n\n### 2. Physical Visit to the Jamkhambhaliya Office\nThe most direct route. Carry:\n- Trust deed copy\n- NPO Darpan affidavit (mentions Reg. No. 1448)\n- Your ID + authorization letter from your father (President)\n- \u20b95\u201350 per page as certified copy fee\n\nAsk at the counter for the **\"Public Trust Register nakal\" (PTR extract)** or **\"registration nu praman patra\"**. They will search by name, trustee names, or approximate date of filing.\n\n### 3. Cross-Verify Legality Through What You Already Have\n\nHere's the good news \u2014 **you already have multiple pieces of proof that the trust legally exists.** The registration process isn't just the certificate; the fact that these government-connected systems have accepted the trust is itself proof:\n\n**Documents/systems that already confirm legality:**\n\n| Proof | What it confirms |\n|---|---|\n| **PAN Card of the Trust** | Income Tax Department has recognized the trust as a legal entity |\n| **Bank Account** | The bank verified trust registration documents before opening |\n| **NGO Darpan / NPO Darpan Registration** | NITI Aayog has verified and issued CIN **1448** \u2014 this itself is strong proof |\n| **Signed Trust Deed with witness/notary** | Legal document that creates the trust |\n| **Schedule II form with office stamp** | Physical proof of filing with Charity Commissioner |\n\nIf PAN was issued to the trust, it means the Income Tax Department already accepted the Charity Commissioner's registration. Same with the bank \u2014 no Indian bank opens a trust account without seeing the registration certificate.\n\n**So somewhere in your father's records, there IS a certificate.** It came in, was used for PAN, was used for the bank account, and then got filed away.\n\n### 4. Check With These People/Places for the Original Certificate\n\nBefore spending time on RTI or a physical trip, quickly check:\n\n- **Your father's document files/lockers** \u2014 the certificate was almost certainly given to him\n- **The bank** where the trust account is held \u2014 banks retain a copy of the registration certificate in their KYC file. You can request a photocopy from the bank branch.\n- **The Chartered Accountant who filed the PAN** \u2014 CAs keep client files for years; they'll have a copy\n- **The advocates who registered the trust (Vijay M. Vithalani, Manisha R. Godani)** \u2014 you said you don't have contact, but their office was at Krishna Shopping Center, M.G. Road, Dwarka per your Vakalatnama. That's a physical address \u2014 worth visiting. Advocates are required to maintain case files for years.\n\n### 5. Contact the Charity Commissioner Directly\n\n- **Head Office phone/email** \u2014 Charity Commissioner, Gujarat, Ahmedabad (contact details on charitycommissioner.gujarat.gov.in/contact-us)\n- Email them with the trust name, approximate registration date, and district. They can search internal records and confirm.\n\n## My Practical Recommendation\n\nGiven your situation, I'd do this in order:\n\n1. **First (today)** \u2014 Ask your father to check his files at home. Then check the bank's KYC copy. This solves 80% of such cases.\n2. **This week** \u2014 Visit the advocate's old office at Krishna Shopping Center, Dwarka. Old advocates often continue at the same location, or their staff can retrieve the file.\n3. **If both fail** \u2014 Visit the Jamkhambhaliya Charity Commissioner office in person. Dwarka to Jamkhambhaliya is about 40\u201350 km; a day trip.\n4. **Final fallback** \u2014 File an RTI.\n\n## One Important Legal Note\n\nEven without holding the physical certificate in hand right now, **your trust IS legally valid** if:\n- The trust deed was properly executed (yours was, in June 2019, on stamp paper with signatures)\n- It was filed with the Charity Commissioner (yours was, per the stamped Schedule II)\n- PAN and bank account exist (they do)\n- NPO Darpan CIN was issued (1448 \u2014 it was)\n\nThe certificate is proof, but the legal existence is already established. That said, you'll definitely need the physical certificate for 12A/80G application.\n\nWhich of these routes do you want to try first? Also, before I forget \u2014 can you check with your father whether he remembers receiving any brown envelope, letter, or certificate from the Charity Commissioner's office in late 2019 or early 2020?",

Some older records may still be filed under \"Jamnagar\" in the digital system.\n\n## Try These Search Variations First\n\nBefore assuming it's not there, try searching with:\n\n- **District:** Try both \"Devbhumi Dwarka\" AND \"Jamnagar\" separately\n- **District:** Try leaving as \"Any\"\n- **Trust Name:** Try each of these one at a time:\n  - `Devkunvarben`\n  - `Devkuvarben`\n  - `Keshavlal Bhanaji`\n  - `Vithalani Charitable`\n  - `Bhanaji Vithalani`\n  - Try the Gujarati script version if language toggle is available\n- **Trust Reg. No:** Try `1448` alone (leave everything else blank)\n- **Trust Reg. No:** Try `E-127` or `E/127` (I saw something like this stamped on your Schedule II form)\n\n## Multiple Ways to Verify Trust Legality\n\nSince online search isn't yielding results, here are all the other ways to confirm and obtain proof:\n\n### 1. RTI Application (Right to Information) \u2014 Powerful and Cheap\nFile an **RTI application** to the **Assistant Charity Commissioner, Devbhumi Dwarka / Jamkhambhaliya office**:\n- Cost: \u20b910 (postal order or IPO)\n- Timeline: Response within 30 days by law\n- Ask specifically: \"Please provide certified copy of the PTR entry and Certificate of Registration for the trust named 'Sva. Devkunvarben Keshavlal Bhanaji Vithalani Charitable Trust', registered around June 2019\u2013January 2020, at your office.\"\n- This is a legally binding query \u2014 they must respond\n\n### 2. Physical Visit to the Jamkhambhaliya Office\nThe most direct route. Carry:\n- Trust deed copy\n- NPO Darpan affidavit (mentions Reg. No. 1448)\n- Your ID + authorization letter from your father (President)\n- \u20b95\u201350 per page as certified copy fee\n\nAsk at the counter for the **\"Public Trust Register nakal\" (PTR extract)** or **\"registration nu praman patra\"**. They will search by name, trustee names, or approximate date of filing.\n\n### 3. Cross-Verify Legality Through What You Already Have\n\nHere's the good news \u2014 **you already have multiple pieces of proof that the trust legally exists.** The registration process isn't just the certificate; the fact that these government-connected systems have accepted the trust is itself proof:\n\n**Documents/systems that already confirm legality:**\n\n| Proof | What it confirms |\n|---|---|\n| **PAN Card of the Trust** | Income Tax Department has recognized the trust as a legal entity |\n| **Bank Account** | The bank verified trust registration documents before opening |\n| **NGO Darpan / NPO Darpan Registration** | NITI Aayog has verified and issued CIN **1448** \u2014 this itself is strong proof |\n| **Signed Trust Deed with witness/notary** | Legal document that creates the trust |\n| **Schedule II form with office stamp** | Physical proof of filing with Charity Commissioner |\n\nIf PAN was issued to the trust, it means the Income Tax Department already accepted the Charity Commissioner's registration. Same with the bank \u2014 no Indian bank opens a trust account without seeing the registration certificate.\n\n**So somewhere in your father's records, there IS a certificate.** It came in, was used for PAN, was used for the bank account, and then got filed away.\n\n### 4. Check With These People/Places for the Original Certificate\n\nBefore spending time on RTI or a physical trip, quickly check:\n\n- **Your father's document files/lockers** \u2014 the certificate was almost certainly given to him\n- **The bank** where the trust account is held \u2014 banks retain a copy of the registration certificate in their KYC file. You can request a photocopy from the bank branch.\n- **The Chartered Accountant who filed the PAN** \u2014 CAs keep client files for years; they'll have a copy\n- **The advocates who registered the trust (Vijay M. Vithalani, Manisha R. Godani)** \u2014 you said you don't have contact, but their office was at Krishna Shopping Center, M.G. Road, Dwarka per your Vakalatnama. That's a physical address \u2014 worth visiting. Advocates are required to maintain case files for years.\n\n### 5. Contact the Charity Commissioner Directly\n\n- **Head Office phone/email** \u2014 Charity Commissioner, Gujarat, Ahmedabad (contact details on charitycommissioner.gujarat.gov.in/contact-us)\n- Email them with the trust name, approximate registration date, and district. They can search internal records and confirm.\n\n## My Practical Recommendation\n\nGiven your situation, I'd do this in order:\n\n1. **First (today)** \u2014 Ask your father to check his files at home. Then check the bank's KYC copy. This solves 80% of such cases.\n2. **This week** \u2014 Visit the advocate's old office at Krishna Shopping Center, Dwarka. Old advocates often continue at the same location, or their staff can retrieve the file.\n3. **If both fail** \u2014 Visit the Jamkhambhaliya Charity Commissioner office in person. Dwarka to Jamkhambhaliya is about 40\u201350 km; a day trip.\n4. **Final fallback** \u2014 File an RTI.\n\n## One Important Legal Note\n\nEven without holding the physical certificate in hand right now, **your trust IS legally valid** if:\n- The trust deed was properly executed (yours was, in June 2019, on stamp paper with signatures)\n- It was filed with the Charity Commissioner (yours was, per the stamped Schedule II)\n- PAN and bank account exist (they do)\n- NPO Darpan CIN was issued (1448 \u2014 it was)\n\nThe certificate is proof, but the legal existence is already established. That said, you'll definitely need the physical certificate for 12A/80G application.\n\nWhich of these routes do you want to try first? Also, before I forget \u2014 can you check with your father whether he remembers receiving any brown envelope, letter, or certificate from the Charity Commissioner's office in late 2019 or early 2020?",

                        "text": "Great question \u2014 this is important to clarify, because I need to be honest with you here.\n\n## The Honest Answer\n\n**I have gone through every document you shared, and none of them explicitly contain a Charity Commissioner PTR registration number for your trust.**\n\nHere's what's in each document:\n\n| Document | What numbers appear | What they mean |\n|---|---|---|\n| **\u0ab8\u0a82\u0aae\u0aa4\u0abf \u0aaa\u0aa4\u0acd\u0ab0 (Consent Letter)** | No registration number | Only trustee signatures and Aadhaar references |\n| **\u0ab5\u0a95\u0ac0\u0ab2\u0abe\u0aa4\u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae\u0ac1\u0a82 (Vakalatnama)** | Blank spaces for \"\u0a85\u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0(\u0a88\u0aa8\u0acd\u0ab5\u0ab0\u0acd\u0aa1) \u0aa8\u0a82. ...../2019\" and \"\u0aab\u0ac7\u0ab0\u0ac0 \u0aa8\u0a82. ....../2019\" | These were left blank \u2014 meant to be filled after filing |\n| **\u0ab8\u0acb\u0a97\u0a82\u0aa6\u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae\u0ac1\u0a82 (Affidavits)** | No registration number | Just sworn statements |\n| **Trust Registration Form (Schedule II)** | Stamp shows: `No. 880`, something like `\u0aaa\u0ab9\u0acb\u0a82\u0a9a \u0aa8\u0a82. 545/12.4` (unclear), and date `22/07/____28` | These are **inward/receipt numbers** of the Charity Commissioner's office when they received your application \u2014 NOT the final registration number |\n| **\u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0ab8\u0ac2\u0a9a\u0abf 1, 2, 3 (Schedules)** | No registration number | Content only |\n| **TRUST DEED** | No registration number | The deed itself; registration happens after |\n| **AAZTS5070P Affidavit (NPO Darpan, April 2026)** | **CIN: 1448** and **Registered on 21/01/20** | This is the **NITI Aayog NPO Darpan CIN**, NOT the Charity Commissioner registration number |\n\n## Where the PTR Number SHOULD Appear\n\nThe actual Charity Commissioner registration number (format: **G/xxx/Devbhoomi Dwarka**) would appear on:\n\n1. **The Registration Certificate** issued by the Assistant Charity Commissioner \u2014 a separate document you don't have in this file\n2. **The Order Sheet / Registration Order** \u2014 the formal order sheet from the Charity Commissioner approving registration\n3. **PTR Extract** \u2014 the certified extract from the Public Trust Register\n4. **Any Change Report filings** made later (Form Schedule III) \u2014 but since your trust was inactive, none were filed\n5. **Bank account documents** \u2014 banks record the PTR number in the account opening form\n6. **PAN application (Form 49A) filed for the trust** \u2014 the CA/lawyer would have entered the registration number here\n7. **NGO Darpan application** \u2014 actually, this asks for the \"Registration No.\" and it seems it was entered as **1448**, but that could be either the actual PTR number OR a different reference number.\n\n## Wait \u2014 Let Me Reconsider the \"1448\" Number\n\nLooking again at your NPO Darpan affidavit, it says:\n> \"having the statutory registration no./ Incorporation no./ CIN as **1448**\"\n\n**1448 might actually be your Charity Commissioner registration number**, not the NPO Darpan CIN. Here's why:\n- NPO Darpan issues IDs in a format like \"GJ/2020/xxxxxxx\" \u2014 usually longer and with the state prefix\n- 1448 is a simple 4-digit number, which matches the format of older PTR entries in Gujarat\n\nSo when you filled out the NPO Darpan application (which you did yourself), **you must have entered 1448 as the statutory registration number from some source**. Do you remember where you got that number from? Because that source is likely your registration certificate itself.\n\n## Try This Now on the Portal\n\nIn the Trust Registration Management search:\n- District: **Devbhoomi Dwarka**\n- Trust Name: blank\n- **Trust Reg. No: `1448`**\n\nAnd also try:\n- District: **- Any -**\n- Trust Name: blank\n- **Trust Reg. No: `1448`**\n\nAnd also try variations like:\n- `G/1448`\n- `E/1448`\n- `1448/2019`\n- `1448/2020`\n\n## The Most Important Question for You\n\n**Where did you get the number 1448 from when you filed the NPO Darpan application?**\n\n- Was it from a physical certificate you saw?\n- Did your father tell it to you?\n- Did the previous lawyer/CA share it?\n- Or is it a number from somewhere else (like a receipt)?\n\nThe answer to this will tell us exactly where the registration certificate is and what the actual number means. Please check with your father and let me know.",

MCA / CSR Portal\n**URL:** `csr.gov.in`\n\n- Only if the trust has CSR-1 registration (needed to receive corporate CSR funds)\n- If it doesn't appear here, it just means CSR-1 isn't done yet \u2014 not a legality issue\n\n### 4. GST Portal\n**URL:** `gst.gov.in` \u2192 \"Search Taxpayer\"\n\n- Only relevant if the trust has GST registration (unlikely for a new trust, but worth checking)\n\n### 5. Since it was inactive, probably nothing here, but worth a check.\n\n### 6. FCRA Portal\n**URL:** `fcraonline.nic.in`\n\n- Only relevant if applying for foreign contribution registration (needs 3 years of activity, so not applicable yet)\n\n### 7. Gujarat Charity Commissioner \u2014 Multiple Sections\n**URL:** `charityonline.gujarat.gov.in`\n\nYou've already tried the Trust Registration Management. Also try:\n- **\"Know Your Trust\"** (separate section from Trust Registration Management)\n- **Trust Directory** on the main charitycommissioner.gujarat.gov.in\n- **Change Report search** \u2014 sometimes trusts appear here even when not in the main directory\n- **Audit Report / Property Register sections** if visible after login\n\n### 8. Gujarat Revenue / Sub-Registrar Records\n**URL:** `garvi.gujarat.gov.in` (for property/document registration)\n\n- The Trust Deed itself was executed on stamp paper in June 2019. If it was registered with a Sub-Registrar (in addition to Charity Commissioner filing), it would have a **document registration number** searchable here\n- Search by document number, party name, or year\n\n### 9. India Stamp Duty / e-Stamping Records\n**URL:** `shcilestamp.com` (SHCIL \u2014 Stock Holding Corporation of India, e-stamp records)\n\n- If the trust deed was executed on e-stamp paper, you can verify the e-stamp certificate here. Won't give you PTR number, but confirms authenticity of the deed.\n\n### 10. Bank Verification\n- Not a portal, but call the trust's bank branch\n- The KYC file will have the **exact registration number** they verified while opening the account\n- This is often the fastest reliable route\n\n### 11. GuideStar India\n**URL:** `guidestarindia.org`\n\n- Independent NGO transparency platform. Trusts often list here voluntarily. If your trust or family listed it, it'll appear.\n\n### 12. CBDT PAN Database (Indirect)\n- Not a public portal, but if you have the trust's PAN card, the PAN itself confirms IT Department recognition\n- The 4th letter of the PAN indicates entity type \u2014 for trusts it's usually \"T\" (e.g., AAZTS5070P \u2014 the \"T\" here confirms it's a Trust)\n\n### 13. Zauba Corp / Tofler\n**URLs:** `zaubacorp.com`, `tofler.in`\n\n- These aggregate government data on companies and some trusts. Not always accurate for trusts, but worth a quick name search.\n\n### 14. Gujarat Public Trust Filings Portal (Annual Filing Portal)\n**URL:** `charityonline.gujarat.gov.in` (login section)\n\n- If the trust ever filed Schedule VIII / Schedule IX (annual accounts/statements), it would be searchable\n- Since your trust was inactive, no filings would exist here\n\n### 15. Local RTO / Property Records (if the trust owns any asset)\n- Not applicable if the trust doesn't own vehicles or property\n\n---\n\n## My Recommended Order for You\n\nGiven your situation, do it in this order \u2014 fastest to slowest:\n\n1. **Bank branch phone call/visit** \u2014 takes 30 minutes. They have the exact number in their file.\n2. **NGO Darpan search** \u2014 takes 5 minutes. Log in with your credentials, view your organization profile, and see the \"Statutory Registration No.\" field. That's what you entered \u2014 trace back where you got it from.\n3. **Income Tax \"Exempt Institution Search\"** \u2014 takes 5 minutes. Search by trust PAN.\n4. **Garvi Gujarat portal** \u2014 if the trust deed was Sub-Registrar registered, this will show the document number.\n5. **Gujarat CC \"Know Your Trust\"** \u2014 different section from what you searched.\n\n---\n\n## One Reality Check\n\nIf after all these portals the trust doesn't appear **anywhere**, there's a possibility worth considering seriously: **the trust may have been filed but not finally registered by the Charity Commissioner.**\n\nThis happens more often than people realize in India. The lawyer files the papers (as evidenced by the office stamp on your Schedule II form dated 22/07/2019), but then:\n- The Charity Commissioner raises queries or objections\n- The lawyer doesn't respond\n- The application lapses\n- No final registration order is passed\n- No PTR number is assigned\n\nMeanwhile, other things happen based on the \"filing done\" understanding \u2014 PAN gets issued (Income Tax doesn't verify PTR status), a bank account might get opened (depends on the bank; some accept application receipt as proof), and NPO Darpan may accept whatever number is entered.\n\n**The fact that \"1448\" doesn't turn up anywhere in Gujarat's system is a real yellow flag.**\n\nI'm not saying this is definitely the case \u2014 the Jamkhambhaliya sub-office non-digitization theory is still valid. But you should be prepared for the possibility that the registration was never completed.\n\nTry the bank call and NGO Darpan check first. Report back what you find, and then we'll know exactly where you stand \u2014 and either celebrate finding the certificate, or plan the fix if registration is genuinely incomplete.",

Let me give you a clear, fact-based answer.\n\n## Important Reframe First\n\nBefore I explain \"how to get on the list,\" let me be honest with you about what's actually happening in your case, because it matters:\n\n**You're not \"getting yourself on the list from scratch.\"** Based on your documents, an application was filed on **22/07/2019** at the Assistant Charity Commissioner's office at Jamkhambhaliya. The stamped Schedule II proves this. So legally, one of three situations is true:\n\n1. **Registration was granted** but the PTR number was never digitized (paper-only records at the sub-office)\n2. **Registration was granted** but the number is listed differently in the online database (spelling issue)\n3. **Registration was never finalized** \u2014 the application lapsed due to unresolved queries, non-payment of publication fees, or advocate abandonment\n\nYou **cannot file a fresh registration** without first resolving the status of the 2019 application. If registration was already granted, filing again creates a duplicate. If it lapsed, you need to know why before re-filing.\n\n---\n\n## Step 1: Determine Actual Status of the 2019 Application (MUST DO FIRST)\n\nThere is no online way to check this. You must do one of these:\n\n### Option A \u2014 Physical Visit (Fastest & Cheapest)\nVisit the **Assistant Charity Commissioner's Office, Jamkhambhaliya, Devbhumi Dwarka District**.\n\nTake with you:\n- Copies of your Trust Deed\n- Copy of the stamped Schedule II (showing filing on 22/07/2019)\n- Trust PAN card copy\n- Your ID + a signed authorization letter from your father (President)\n- A short written application (in Gujarati) requesting: \"Status inquiry of Schedule II application filed on 22/07/2019 for trust named 'Sva. Devkunvarben Keshavlal Bhanaji Vithalani Charitable Trust' \u2014 please confirm PTR registration number if granted, or advise pending action if not.\"\n\nAsk them to check the **inward register for July 2019** and the **Public Trust Register (Schedule I)** in the paper records. Sub-office staff can usually pull this in an hour.\n\n### Option B \u2014 RTI Application (If Physical Visit Isn't Feasible)\n- Cost: \u20b910 (postal order or IPO)\n- Address: **Public Information Officer, Office of the Assistant Charity Commissioner, Jamkhambhaliya, District Devbhumi Dwarka**\n- Response mandated within 30 days\n- Frame it as a status inquiry with the same details as above\n\n### Option C \u2014 Contact Head Office\n- Office of the Charity Commissioner, Gujarat State, Ahmedabad\n- Contact details on `charitycommissioner.gujarat.gov.in/contact-us`\n- They can direct the sub-office to check records\n\n---\n\n## Step 2: Based on What Step 1 Reveals\n\n### Scenario A: Registration Was Granted\nYou get the PTR number. Ask the office to:\n- Issue a certified PTR extract (Schedule I copy)\n- Confirm whether the entry needs digital upload to the online portal \u2014 request them to update the record if it's missing online\n- Cost: nominal fee per page for certified copies\n\n### Scenario B: Application Is Still Pending\nAsk what step is pending \u2014 usually one of:\n- Publication in newspapers (mandatory under BPT Rules)\n- Payment of publication/registration fee\n- Response to queries raised by the ACC\n- Verification visit\n\nYou (or a lawyer) can revive the application by responding to whatever is pending.\n\n### Scenario C: Application Has Lapsed / Was Rejected\nThis is when you actually need to **file a fresh Schedule II application**. Here's the official process:\n\n---\n\n## The Official Process to Register a Public Trust in Gujarat (If Fresh Filing Is Needed)\n\n### Legal Basis\n- **The Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950** (as applicable in Gujarat)\n- **Section 18** \u2014 mandatory registration\n- **Bombay Public Trusts (Gujarat) Rules, 1961** \u2014 procedure details\n- Governed by the Charity Commissioner, Gujarat\n\n### Where to Apply\nThe **Assistant/Deputy Charity Commissioner** of the region where the trust's registered office is. For you, that's **Devbhumi Dwarka region \u2014 Jamkhambhaliya office**.\n\n### Online vs Offline\nGujarat's `charityonline.gujarat.gov.in` portal supports online submission of several trust-related processes (like change reports, annual filings), but as of my current information, **initial trust registration (Schedule II filing) still primarily requires physical submission** at the regional/sub-regional Charity Commissioner office. The online portal is mainly for post-registration compliance. Please verify this at the office itself \u2014 policies may have changed.\n\n### Application Form and Documents\nFile **Schedule II Application** with:\n\n1. **Form Schedule II** (the same form you already have signed, but fresh if lapsed) \u2014 with \u20b92 court fee stamp\n2. **Trust Deed** \u2014 original + certified true copies\n3. **Consent Letter (\u0ab8\u0a82\u0aae\u0aa4\u0abf \u0aaa\u0aa4\u0acd\u0ab0)** signed by all trustees\n4. **Affidavit (\u0ab8\u0acb\u0a97\u0a82\u0aa6\u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae\u0ac1\u0a82)** by one trustee on stamp paper affirming particulars are true\n5. **Schedule I** \u2014 trustee details\n6. **Schedule II-A** \u2014 memorandum of immovable property (if any)\n7. **List of trustees** with PAN, Aadhaar, address, photos\n8. **Address proof of registered office** (electricity bill / rent agreement / ownership document)\n9. **Vakalatnama** if represented by advocate\n10. **Court fee stamps** and registration fee (based on trust property value \u2014 from the fee slab you have in your instructions document)\n\n### Registration Fee (from your own documents)\nAs per your instruction sheet:\n| Trust property value | Fee |\n|---|---|\n| Less than \u20b92,000 | \u20b920 |\n| \u20b92,001 \u2013 \u20b95,000 | \u20b950 |\n| \u20b95,001 \u2013 \u20b910,000 | \u20b9100 |\n| \u20b910,001 \u2013 \u20b925,000 | \u20b9250 |\n| Above \u20b925,000 | \u20b9500 |\n\n### Statutory Timeline After Filing\n- ACC issues acknowledgement (inward number)\n- ACC holds an inquiry under **Section 19** to verify the trust's existence and public charitable nature\n- If satisfied, ACC passes an order and makes an **entry in the Public Trust Register (Schedule I)** under **Section 21**\n- ACC issues a **Certificate of Registration** signed and sealed, as per **Rule 8 of BPT (Gujarat) Rules, 1961**\n- The certificate states: *\"It is hereby certified that the Public Trust described below has this day been duly registered under the Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950...\"*\n\n**Practical timeline:** 30\u2013100 days depending on office workload.\n\n---\n\n## What to Do Right Now \u2014 Concrete Next Actions\n\nGiven your situation, this is my strong recommendation in order:\n\n1. **This week** \u2014 Ask your father to physically go through every file, folder, envelope, and drawer at home for anything from the Charity Commissioner. Also ask him to phone the previous advocate's office (Vijay M. Vithalani, Krishna Shopping Center, M.G. Road, Dwarka \u2014 from your Vakalatnama). Even if you don't have their personal number, the office location is known.\n\n2. **This week or next** \u2014 Visit the **bank branch** where the trust account is held. Request a copy of the KYC file. The registration certificate is 100% there. Banks cannot open trust accounts without it.\n\n3. **Within 2 weeks** \u2014 Visit the **Jamkhambhaliya Assistant Charity Commissioner office** in person with the documents I listed. This is a day trip from Dwarka. Get definitive answer on whether the trust is registered, pending, or lapsed.\n\n4. **Based on outcome** \u2014 Either obtain the PTR extract, revive the pending application, or file fresh.\n\n---\n\n## One More Thing \u2014 A Cautionary Word\n\nPlease do **not** apply for 12A/80G, or take any donations, until Step 1 is resolved. Both the Income Tax Department and any prospective donor will demand the Charity Commissioner registration certificate. If the trust is legally unregistered, applying for 12A/80G with wrong statutory numbers would create serious legal complications later.\n\nAlso, since your trust's operations are just starting and stakes are getting real (real registrations, real donations, real compliance), it's worth engaging a **local CA or advocate** in Dwarka/Jamnagar for at least the compliance setup phase. It's a one-time cost of \u20b915,000\u2013\u20b930,000 that saves years of headaches. You can then handle ongoing operations, digital presence, activities, and fundraising yourself with your skill set.\n\nWould you like me to help draft the application letter for the sub-office visit, or the RTI application? Or explain the 12A/80G filing sequence once we know the registration status?",

                        "text": "Now I have a very thorough understanding. Let me give you a clear, fact-based answer.\n\n## Important Reframe First\n\nBefore I explain \"how to get on the list,\" let me be honest with you about what's actually happening in your case, because it matters:\n\n**You're not \"getting yourself on the list from scratch.\"** Based on your documents, an application was filed on **22/07/2019** at the Assistant Charity Commissioner's office at Jamkhambhaliya. The stamped Schedule II proves this. So legally, one of three situations is true:\n\n1. **Registration was granted** but the PTR number was never digitized (paper-only records at the sub-office)\n2. **Registration was granted** but the number is listed differently in the online database (spelling issue)\n3. **Registration was never finalized** \u2014 the application lapsed due to unresolved queries, non-payment of publication fees, or advocate abandonment\n\nYou **cannot file a fresh registration** without first resolving the status of the 2019 application. If registration was already granted, filing again creates a duplicate. If it lapsed, you need to know why before re-filing.\n\n---\n\n## Step 1: Determine Actual Status of the 2019 Application (MUST DO FIRST)\n\nThere is no online way to check this. You must do one of these:\n\n### Option A \u2014 Physical Visit (Fastest & Cheapest)\nVisit the **Assistant Charity Commissioner's Office, Jamkhambhaliya, Devbhumi Dwarka District**.\n\nTake with you:\n- Copies of your Trust Deed\n- Copy of the stamped Schedule II (showing filing on 22/07/2019)\n- Trust PAN card copy\n- Your ID + a signed authorization letter from your father (President)\n- A short written application (in Gujarati) requesting: \"Status inquiry of Schedule II application filed on 22/07/2019 for trust named 'Sva. Devkunvarben Keshavlal Bhanaji Vithalani Charitable Trust' \u2014 please confirm PTR registration number if granted, or advise pending action if not.\"\n\nAsk them to check the **inward register for July 2019** and the **Public Trust Register (Schedule I)** in the paper records. Sub-office staff can usually pull this in an hour.\n\n### Option B \u2014 RTI Application (If Physical Visit Isn't Feasible)\n- Cost: \u20b910 (postal order or IPO)\n- Address: **Public Information Officer, Office of the Assistant Charity Commissioner, Jamkhambhaliya, District Devbhumi Dwarka**\n- Response mandated within 30 days\n- Frame it as a status inquiry with the same details as above\n\n### Option C \u2014 Contact Head Office\n- Office of the Charity Commissioner, Gujarat State, Ahmedabad\n- Contact details on `charitycommissioner.gujarat.gov.in/contact-us`\n- They can direct the sub-office to check records\n\n---\n\n## Step 2: Based on What Step 1 Reveals\n\n### Scenario A: Registration Was Granted\nYou get the PTR number. Ask the office to:\n- Issue a certified PTR extract (Schedule I copy)\n- Confirm whether the entry needs digital upload to the online portal \u2014 request them to update the record if it's missing online\n- Cost: nominal fee per page for certified copies\n\n### Scenario B: Application Is Still Pending\nAsk what step is pending \u2014 usually one of:\n- Publication in newspapers (mandatory under BPT Rules)\n- Payment of publication/registration fee\n- Response to queries raised by the ACC\n- Verification visit\n\nYou (or a lawyer) can revive the application by responding to whatever is pending.\n\n### Scenario C: Application Has Lapsed / Was Rejected\nThis is when you actually need to **file a fresh Schedule II application**. Here's the official process:\n\n---\n\n## The Official Process to Register a Public Trust in Gujarat (If Fresh Filing Is Needed)\n\n### Legal Basis\n- **The Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950** (as applicable in Gujarat)\n- **Section 18** \u2014 mandatory registration\n- **Bombay Public Trusts (Gujarat) Rules, 1961** \u2014 procedure details\n- Governed by the Charity Commissioner, Gujarat\n\n### Where to Apply\nThe **Assistant/Deputy Charity Commissioner** of the region where the trust's registered office is. For you, that's **Devbhumi Dwarka region \u2014 Jamkhambhaliya office**.\n\n### Online vs Offline\nGujarat's `charityonline.gujarat.gov.in` portal supports online submission of several trust-related processes (like change reports, annual filings), but as of my current information, **initial trust registration (Schedule II filing) still primarily requires physical submission** at the regional/sub-regional Charity Commissioner office. The online portal is mainly for post-registration compliance. Please verify this at the office itself \u2014 policies may have changed.\n\n### Application Form and Documents\nFile **Schedule II Application** with:\n\n1. **Form Schedule II** (the same form you already have signed, but fresh if lapsed) \u2014 with \u20b92 court fee stamp\n2. **Trust Deed** \u2014 original + certified true copies\n3. **Consent Letter (\u0ab8\u0a82\u0aae\u0aa4\u0abf \u0aaa\u0aa4\u0acd\u0ab0)** signed by all trustees\n4. **Affidavit (\u0ab8\u0acb\u0a97\u0a82\u0aa6\u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae\u0ac1\u0a82)** by one trustee on stamp paper affirming particulars are true\n5. **Schedule I** \u2014 trustee details\n6. **Schedule II-A** \u2014 memorandum of immovable property (if any)\n7. **List of trustees** with PAN, Aadhaar, address, photos\n8. **Address proof of registered office** (electricity bill / rent agreement / ownership document)\n9. **Vakalatnama** if represented by advocate\n10. **Court fee stamps** and registration fee (based on trust property value \u2014 from the fee slab you have in your instructions document)\n\n### Registration Fee (from your own documents)\nAs per your instruction sheet:\n| Trust property value | Fee |\n|---|---|\n| Less than \u20b92,000 | \u20b920 |\n| \u20b92,001 \u2013 \u20b95,000 | \u20b950 |\n| \u20b95,001 \u2013 \u20b910,000 | \u20b9100 |\n| \u20b910,001 \u2013 \u20b925,000 | \u20b9250 |\n| Above \u20b925,000 | \u20b9500 |\n\n### Statutory Timeline After Filing\n- ACC issues acknowledgement (inward number)\n- ACC holds an inquiry under **Section 19** to verify the trust's existence and public charitable nature\n- If satisfied, ACC passes an order and makes an **entry in the Public Trust Register (Schedule I)** under **Section 21**\n- ACC issues a **Certificate of Registration** signed and sealed, as per **Rule 8 of BPT (Gujarat) Rules, 1961**\n- The certificate states: *\"It is hereby certified that the Public Trust described below has this day been duly registered under the Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950...\"*\n\n**Practical timeline:** 30\u2013100 days depending on office workload.\n\n---\n\n## What to Do Right Now \u2014 Concrete Next Actions\n\nGiven your situation, this is my strong recommendation in order:\n\n1. **This week** \u2014 Ask your father to physically go through every file, folder, envelope, and drawer at home for anything from the Charity Commissioner. Also ask him to phone the previous advocate's office (Vijay M. Vithalani, Krishna Shopping Center, M.G. Road, Dwarka \u2014 from your Vakalatnama). Even if you don't have their personal number, the office location is known.\n\n2. **This week or next** \u2014 Visit the **bank branch** where the trust account is held. Request a copy of the KYC file. The registration certificate is 100% there. Banks cannot open trust accounts without it.\n\n3. **Within 2 weeks** \u2014 Visit the **Jamkhambhaliya Assistant Charity Commissioner office** in person with the documents I listed. This is a day trip from Dwarka. Get definitive answer on whether the trust is registered, pending, or lapsed.\n\n4. **Based on outcome** \u2014 Either obtain the PTR extract, revive the pending application, or file fresh.\n\n---\n\n## One More Thing \u2014 A Cautionary Word\n\nPlease do **not** apply for 12A/80G, or take any donations, until Step 1 is resolved. Both the Income Tax Department and any prospective donor will demand the Charity Commissioner registration certificate. If the trust is legally unregistered, applying for 12A/80G with wrong statutory numbers would create serious legal complications later.\n\nAlso, since your trust's operations are just starting and stakes are getting real (real registrations, real donations, real compliance), it's worth engaging a **local CA or advocate** in Dwarka/Jamnagar for at least the compliance setup phase. It's a one-time cost of \u20b915,000\u2013\u20b930,000 that saves years of headaches. You can then handle ongoing operations, digital presence, activities, and fundraising yourself with your skill set.\n\nWould you like me to help draft the application letter for the sub-office visit, or the RTI application? Or explain the 12A/80G filing sequence once we know the registration status?",
