                "text": "Yes, there are several official ways to verify a trust's 12A registration online. Let me walk you through them.\n\n## Primary Official Source \u2014 Income Tax Department\n\n**Portal:** `incometax.gov.in`\n\nThe Income Tax Department maintains an official public search facility called **\"Tax Exemption Institution Search\"** (previously called \"Exempt Institutions\" search).\n\n**Path to reach it:**\n1. Go to `incometax.gov.in`\n2. Do NOT log in \u2014 this is a public utility\n3. Look for the menu: **\"Services\"** \u2192 **\"Know Your...\"** or **\"Tax Services\"**\n4. Find **\"Tax Exemption Institution Search\"** or **\"Search u/s 12A/12AA/12AB\"**\n\n**Search options available:**\n- By **PAN of the trust** (best option \u2014 you have this)\n- By **name of the trust**\n- By **section** under which registered (12A, 12AA, 12AB, 80G, 10(23C), etc.)\n- By **date range**\n\n**What you'll see if registered:**\n- Trust name\n- PAN\n- Registration number under 12A/12AB\n- Section under which registered\n- Date of registration\n- Validity period (for provisional registrations)\n- Assessing officer\n\n**If nothing appears** \u2014 the trust is not registered under 12A. Simple as that.\n\n---\n\n## Secondary Verification Portals\n\n### 1. Reporting Portal (Income Tax)\n`report.insight.gov.in` \u2014 used by CAs for donation reporting under 80G. Requires login but confirms 80G status.\n\n### 2. e-Filing Portal\n`incometax.gov.in` \u2014 if you log in with the trust's PAN credentials, the dashboard will clearly show all active registrations (12A, 80G, 10(23C), etc.) under the \"Profile\" or \"My Registrations\" section.\n\n### 3. NGO Darpan\n`ngodarpan.gov.in` \u2014 the profile you created will show 12A/80G numbers **only if you entered them** during application. Not an independent source of truth, but useful cross-check.\n\n### 4. CSR-1 Portal (MCA)\n`csr.gov.in` \u2014 CSR-1 filing requires 12A/80G, so if the trust is CSR-1 registered, its 12A/80G numbers are on public record here. Searchable by PAN or name.\n\n### 5. Donation Utility Portal (Form 10BD/10BE)\n`incometax.gov.in` \u2014 trusts filing Form 10BD (statement of donations received) must have 12A. If any donor claims deduction citing your trust, it shows up here.\n\n---\n\n## But Here's Where I Need to Push Back Gently\n\nYou said: *\"I am sure that the trust do have a 12A certificate.\"*\n\nVraj, based on everything you've told me and everything in your documents, I want to respectfully suggest that this confidence may be misplaced. Here's why:\n\n1. **The trust was never operational** \u2014 you confirmed this. 12A registration is typically applied for by trusts that intend to operate and receive donations. There was no reason for it to have been applied for.\n\n2. **12A wasn't in the original registration workflow** \u2014 the 2019 lawyers registered the trust under BPT Act. 12A is a completely separate Income Tax filing that requires a separate professional engagement, separate documents, and separate government fees.\n\n3. **You told me the Charity Commissioner registration itself isn't findable online** \u2014 12A comes AFTER the CC registration certificate is in hand. If the base registration is uncertain, 12A on top of it is very unlikely.\n\n4. **Post-2020 rule changes** \u2014 after April 2021, ALL existing 12A/12AA registrations had to be re-registered under **Section 12AB** by filing **Form 10A** on the e-filing portal. This was a mandatory migration. If your trust had 12A pre-2020 and didn't migrate, the old 12A is void.\n\n5. **None of your documents mention any 12A number** \u2014 the affidavit from NPO Darpan (April 2026) which lists statutory registrations only mentions the \"1448\" number. If 12A existed, it would have been listed there prominently.\n\n6. **The financial year mentioned in your trust deed for compliance is April\u2013March**, but there's no indication of ITR-7 filings, audit reports, or any 12A-linked compliance ever being done. 12A without 85% expenditure and ITR-7 filings gets automatically cancelled.\n\n---\n\n## What I Suggest You Do\n\n**Check first, believe later.** Here's the order:\n\n1. Go to `incometax.gov.in` \u2192 Tax Exemption Institution Search\n2. Enter the trust's PAN (which starts with AAZTS from your affidavit \u2014 full PAN is AAZTS5070P based on the file name of your affidavit)\n3. See what comes up\n\n**If it shows 12A/12AB registration** \u2014 great, note the number and validity, and share it with me so we can plan next steps.\n\n**If it shows nothing** \u2014 then the trust does not have 12A registration, and I'd suggest we plan for a fresh Provisional 12A + 80G application together, once the base Charity Commissioner registration is verified.\n\n**One more possibility to consider:** Sometimes people confuse \"having a PAN\" with \"having 12A.\" They're completely different. PAN just identifies the trust as a taxpayer entity. 12A is the exemption from paying tax on that PAN's income. Could this be the confusion?\n\nTry the Income Tax search and let me know what shows up. I'd rather help you plan based on facts than on assumptions \u2014 even if the facts are less convenient than we'd hope.",

Look for the tile: **\"Tax Exemption Institution Search\"** or **\"Trust and Institution\"**\n5. Click it \u2014 you'll land on the search interface\n\n### Alternative Path \u2014 Through Menu\n1. From the top bar: **\"Services\"** (in some views this is inside a hamburger menu)\n2. Under Services, find: **\"Know your...\"** section\n3. Look for **\"Tax Exemption Institution Search\"**\n\n### If You Still Can't Find It\nTry this URL directly in your browser:\n- `https://portal.incometax.gov.in/iec/foservices/#/pre-login/knowYourTaxExemptInstitution`\n\nOr search Google for: **\"income tax exemption institution search\"** \u2014 the first official result will be the direct link.\n\n---\n\n## What the Search Interface Looks Like\n\nOnce you're on the right page, you'll see a form with these fields:\n\n- **PAN** (of the trust)\n- **Name of the Institution**\n- **State**\n- **City**\n- **Section number** (dropdown: 12A, 12AA, 12AB, 80G, 10(23C), etc.)\n- **Date range** (optional)\n\nEnter the **trust PAN (AAZTS5070P** \u2014 based on your affidavit filename**)** and click search. Let me actually research this properly this time before answering.\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nNow I have the correct URL. Let me verify it works.\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nI've now confirmed the correct URL through multiple official sources. Let me give you the definitive answer.\n\n## First \u2014 I Owe You a Correction\n\nI sent you to `incometax.gov.in` (the e-Filing portal, for logged-in taxpayer services). That was the wrong domain for public exemption verification. The correct portal is **`incometaxindia.gov.in`** (the main department website, without the \"e-\" filing part). These are two different websites run by the Income Tax Department, and the public search tool for exempt institutions lives only on the second one.\n\nSorry for the runaround. Here's the correct information now.\n\n---\n\n## The Official Tool \u2014 Tax Exempted Institutions Search\n\n**Direct URL:** `https://incometaxindia.gov.in/Pages/utilities/exempted-institutions.aspx`\n\nAlso linked from: `https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/tax-exempted-institutions`\n\nThis is a public database maintained by the **Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)** listing all institutions that have registration/approval under Sections 12A, 12AA, 12AB, 80G, 10(23C), 35(1)(ii)/(iii), and similar exemption provisions.\n\n### How to Navigate to It (Menu Path)\n\nIf the direct URL gives issues in your browser, navigate manually:\n\n1. Go to **`incometaxindia.gov.in`** (the CBDT main site, NOT `incometax.gov.in`)\n2. On the top navigation, click **\"Tax Information & Services\"**\n3. In the dropdown, look under **\"Tax Utilities\"**\n4. Click **\"Tax Exempted Institutions\"**\n\nOr from the homepage, look for a section called **\"Important Links\"** or **\"Quick Access\"** \u2014 \"Tax Exempted Institutions\" is listed there as one of the utilities.\n\n### How to Search\n\nThe search interface offers multiple fields \u2014 **use PAN of the trust as the primary search key**, because:\n\n- Trust names have spelling variations (Vithalani/Vithlani/Vitthalani)\n- The database is huge (over 2 lakh institutions listed)\n- PAN is unique and exact\n\n**Search fields available:**\n- Name of the institution\n- PAN (recommended)\n- Section (dropdown: 12A, 12AA, 12AB, 80G, 10(23C), 35(1)(ii)/(iii), etc.)\n- Text search\n- Advanced search: date range, approving authority, jurisdiction\n\n**For your trust:** Enter PAN **AAZTS5070P** (from your affidavit filename) and search across all sections.\n\n### Important Caveats About This Tool\n\nBased on official sources and user reports:\n\n1. **The database is imperfect.** The Income Tax Department itself displays a disclaimer that information is subject to change and may not reflect real-time status.\n2. **Sometimes only PAN shows without the name/address** \u2014 this is a known limitation, not an error.\n3. **Post-2020 12AB registrations are supposed to be listed**, but there's known lag in updating.\n4. **There is no user support** \u2014 no button or email to raise queries about missing entries.\n\n---\n\n## Alternative Method \u2014 Login to E-Filing Portal (Most Reliable)\n\nIf the public search shows nothing or partial data, the definitive check is:\n\n1. Go to **`incometax.gov.in`** (the e-Filing portal this time)\n2. Click **\"Login\"** \u2014 top right\n3. Enter the trust's PAN as User ID\n4. If never logged in before, you or a trustee will need to **register** first (create password, link mobile/email)\n5. Once logged in, go to **\"Pending Actions\"** or **\"Services\"** \u2192 **\"View Registrations\"** / **\"My Registrations\"** or under **\"Profile\"**\n6. Any active 12A / 12AB / 80G / 10(23C) registrations will be clearly listed with:\n - Registration number\n - Section\n - Date of order\n - Validity period\n - Order (Form 10AC) downloadable as PDF\n\nThis is the trust's own tax record \u2014 100% authoritative.\n\n---\n\n## Two Other Ways to Confirm 12A Status\n\n### 1. Check the Bank Account for Interest TDS\nIf the trust has a bank account with any deposits, check whether the bank has been deducting **TDS on interest**. If the trust had 12A registration, the trustees would typically have submitted **Form 15G** or a lower/nil TDS certificate to the bank. If the bank has been deducting normal TDS on interest, that's an indirect indicator that no 12A exemption was on record.\n\n### 2. Check the Trust's Form 26AS / AIS\nLog in with the trust's PAN on the e-filing portal \u2192 **\"Services\"** \u2192 **\"Annual Information Statement (AIS)\"** or **\"Form 26AS\"**. This shows all tax-relevant transactions the department knows about. If 12A/80G registration exists, the profile will reflect the exempt entity classification.\n\n---\n\n## Try This Order and Report Back\n\n1. **First** \u2014 Direct URL: `incometaxindia.gov.in/Pages/utilities/exempted-institutions.aspx` \u2014 search by PAN AAZTS5070P\n2. **If that fails** \u2014 Log in to `incometax.gov.in` with the trust's PAN (register if needed)\n3. **Send me a screenshot** of what shows up\n\nOnce we have hard confirmation of whether 12A exists or not, we can plan the actual next steps \u2014 either use the existing registration, or apply fresh via Form 10A. Take your time, and thank you for pushing back when I pointed you to wrong pages. That kind of check helps us get to the truth faster.",

However, there have been cases when the benefits provided to such organisations have been misused and in order to curb this, Government have been trying to bring in changes/ amendments to the way such trusts are subjected to tax. Step-2: Navigate to \u201cIncome Tax Forms\u201d under E-File tab and select Form 10A/ 10AB, as the case may be. Step-3: Select the option \u201cPrepare and Submit online\u201d to fill requisite details in the form.\n\nSimilar amendment in registration/ renewal procedure has also been made in section 10(23C), 80G. Thus, the existing trusts/ institutions will now have to apply for fresh registration under section 10(23C), 80G similar to the same manner as applicable in section 12AB. Such application shall be made through Form No. 10A or 10AB, as the case may be. Also an important change which has been made is that trusts or institutions who are registered u/s 80G shall now have to furnish a statement containing details of donations received during the year in Form No. 10BD in the prescribed manner.                                 "title": "Are you in the list of \u201cTax Exempted institutes\u201d \u2013 KCJM | NGO",

                                    "site_domain": "kcjmngo.com",

                                "is_missing": false,
                                "text": "As a good initiative of governance, Income Tax department has made the list public for all the institutes which are having tax exemption under various sections like 12A, 80G, 10(23c) etc \u00b7 You can search your organisation\u2019s name in this list of exempted institutes by following method\n\nTrust Registration Certificate Sec 12A (New Sec 12AB) Provisionally Approved \u00b7 FCRA \u2013 GAME OVER ? Sale to Foreigner deposited in FC or NonFC Bank? D-407, The First, Bh ITC Narmada, Satellite Road, Ahmedabad Gujarat \u00b7 Mobile \u2013 9825434411 Email \u2013 contact@kcjmngo.com \u00b7 Working Hours 11:00 am \u2013 6:00 pm Monday to Friday \u00b7 12A Registration of NGO online processHow UDIN affects NGO Utilization Certificate?\n\nhttps://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/Pages/utilities/exempted-institutions.aspx \u00b7 There are lots of fields are given for searching NGO in exemption lists, like Name, PAN, Sections, Text even as an advanced search like range, authority, dates etc.. \n\nBut because the database is so huge, it is advisable to use your NGO\u2019s PAN for searching purpose. You may get discrepancies related to your exemption status or not getting your name at all. Like I have experienced that, exemption for 12A is showing for particular organization but not for 80G. Income Tax department has not put any button or email to contact regarding any query related to this utility or database. However, in \u201cContact us\u201d page, toll free numbers are given where one can contact and raise their query. Contact us if you have any further query. ... https://kcjmngo.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/Check-Exemption-Status.jpg 267 382 Jahir Mansuri https://kcjmngo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/Logo-340-x-156-px-2.png Jahir Mansuri2019-02-0",

                                "is_missing": false,
                                "text": "Search Legislation\n\nIncome Tax Act 2007\n\nStatus:\n\nThis is the original version (as it was originally enacted).\n\n518Overview of Part\n\nThis section has no associated Explanatory Notes\n\n(1)This Part makes provision about some gifts and payments made to charitable trusts, including provision imposing charges to income tax and conferring exemptions from those charges (see sections 520 to 523).\n\n(2)This Part also provides for some of the income of charitable trusts and others to be exempt from charges to income tax (see sections 524 to 537).\n\n(3)In the provisions of this Part containing exemptions, references to total income of a charitable trust are to the total income of the trustees of the charitable trust concerned.\n\n(4)See section 538 for provision about making claims for the exemptions under this Part.\n\n(5)In the case of a charitable trust which has a non-exempt amount for a tax year (see section 540), the exemptions under this Part are subject to restrictions (see section 539).",

                                "type": "knowledge",
                                "title": "Tax Payers Information Series \u2013 37",
                                "url": "https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/assessment-charitable-trustsinstitutions/9851331",
                                "metadata": {

                                "is_missing": false,
                                "text": "Tax Payers Information Series \u2013 37\n\n\n\n\n    Assessment of\n       Charitable\n Trusts and Institutions\n\n\n\n\nDirectorate of Income Tax\n          (RSP&Public Relations)\n    Mayur Bhawan, New Delhi \u2013 110 001\n\n\n                    1\nThis booklet should not be construed as an exhaustive statement of\nthe Law. In case of doubt, reference should always be made to the\n           relevant provisions in the Acts and the Rules.\n\n\n\n\n                                2\n3\nPREFACE\n       Creation of two new Directorates of Exemption at Hyderabad and\nBangalore last year points towards the ever increasing work of dealing with\ncharitable trusts and institutions. The issues of registration of charitable trusts\nand institutions, approval u/s 80-G, and approval or notification under different\nclauses of Section 10 are of interest to a large number of NGOs and officers\nworking in the field dealing with such cases. In view of this, the publication of this\n\n\nbooklet is quite timely and it will fill the vacuum, which existed because of lack of\nany material on this topic published by this Directorate.\n\n\n       The booklet has been authored by Shri K.G. Bansal. He has dealt with\nimportant issues of registration of trusts and institutions, approval u/s 80-G,\napprovals under sections 10(17A) and 10(23C), and Notification u/s 35(1)(ii)/(iii).\nVarious forms required to be filled up for such exemptions, notifications etc.,\nhave also been compiled in the booklet.\n       It is hoped that this booklet will be of great help to those who have to deal\nwith provisions contained in Sections 10, 11, 12, and 13 regarding Charitable\nTrusts and Institutions.\n\n       Any suggestion for improvement of this booklet is welcome.\n\n\nNew Delhi,\nDated : 5.12.2002                                            (DEEPA KRISHAN)\n                                                            Director of Income-tax\n\n\n                                                                (RSP & PR)",

                                "text": "the difference in box 7.12.\n\nIncome on which you are claiming exemption\n\nboxes 7.14 to 7.21   The breakdown of income here is either the\nyear ended 5 April 2025 or for the period covered by the accounts \non which the return is based.\n\nPlease indicate in the appropriate box the amount the charity has \nactually received during the period.\n\nDo not include details of income which is not taxable (GASDS \nincome is not taxable).\n\n\u25cf Total turnover from exempt trading activities\n\nbox 7.14   Enter details of the turnover from trades, or fund\nraising events, the profits of which will be exempted by  \nsections 524, 526 and 529 Income Tax Act (ITA) 2007. For \nguidance on the tax treatment of trades carried on by charities, \ngo to www.gov.uk/guidance/charities-and-trading or you can \nphone us for help at HM Revenue and Customs Charities  \non 0300 123 1073.\n\nIf the charity has carried on a trade during the return period which \n\n\nfalls outside the exemption, please fill in the 'Trust and Estate Trade' \npages. Go to www.gov.uk and search for \u2018SA901\u2019. Do not include  \nin the calculation sources of income which are otherwise exempt \nfrom tax.\n\n\u25cf Investment income\n\nbox 7.15   The entry here will include income from:\n\u2022 company dividends\n\u2022 interest on deposits and loans\n\u2022 alternative finance receipts\n\u2022 foreign investments\n\n\u25cf UK land and buildings income\n\nbox 7.16   Include rents received from property owned by the\ncharity. Consideration received for transactions in land which has \nbeen developed is likely to be taxable under either section 5 of the \nIncome Tax (Trading and Other Income) Act (ITTOIA) 2005 or \nsection 755 ITA 2007, include it in the main tax return.\n\n\u25cf Gift Aid\n\nbox 7.17   Enter the total net donations received in the period.\nDo not include GASDS income.\n\n\u25cf Other charities\n\nbox 7.18   Enter the total payments received from other charities.\n\n\u25cf Legacies",

                                "text": "Guidelines to the AOs-29\nRegarding cancellation of registration of trust\nGuidelines to the AOs-29\nRegarding cancellation of registration of trust\nA. Preliminary Verification\n(i) Confirm legal existence of trust/institution: Ensure that the trust is constituted through a registered trust deed, society registration, or statute and that the legal identity is verifiable.\nInvestigation:\ni. Obtain and verify original registration documents.\nCross-check with Registrar of Societies/Charity Commissioner records.\nVerify PAN and GST registrations, if any, to ensure operational authenticity.\n(ii) Examine application completeness: Check that the application under Section 12A/12AB is fully supported by documents such as the founding deed, PAN, prior registrations, activity reports, and financial statements.\nInvestigation:\ni.                                 "is_missing": false,
                                "text": "Taxation of Charitable Trust\nBy\nCA Sweety\nSharma\nSYNOPSIS\n\u2022 Introduction\n\u2022 Application under Sec 12A\n\u2022 Charitable Purpose 2(15)\n\u2022 Exemption u/s 11\n\u2022 Exemption not available u/s11\n\u2022 Returns of Charitable Trust & penalty for non filing\n\u2022 Audit of the Accounts of Charitable Trust\n\u2022 80 G Certificate\n\u2022 Deduction u/s 80G\nIntroduction\n\u2022 Charitable/Religious Trusts have been exempted from Tax under\nITA, 1961 provided that it must be carrying an activity covered\nu/s 2(15) of ITA, 1961.\n\u2022 The Trust is required to make application for grant of exemption\nu/s 12A & 12AA of ITA, 1961.\n\u2022 The exemption is given u/s 11& 12 of the Act provided trust is\nregistered u/s 12 A of the Act. If, it is not registered, no exemption\nwill be allowed.\nApplication under Sec 12A\n\u2022 Application for registration of Charitable Trust has to be made in duplicate in\nForm 10A to the Commissioner/Principal Commissioner along with\nfollowing documents\ni. \n\nform part of the corpus trust i.e. corpus donations is exempted fully.\nSec 11(2) : Where 85% of the income is not applied to charitable purpose but is\naccumulated, such accumulated income will not be included in total income if such\ntrust intimate to AO for which purpose it is being accumulated & for what period it\nis being accumulated that should not exceed 5 years & income so accumulated must\nbe deposited in 11(5) modes\nExemption u/s 11 not available if\n\u2022 Income for private religious purpose which does not ensure benefit of\ngeneral public\n\u2022 Income for benefit of particular religious community\n\u2022 Income for the benefit of specified persons such author/trustee/\nsubstantial contributor/relative etc.\n\u2022 Funds not invested in Specified modes u/s 11(5).\nReturns of Charitable Trust\n\u2022 As per Sec 139(4A) Charitable Trust is required to file the return in Form ITR 7\non or before the due date if total income before giving exemption u/s 11 & 12\n\n\n    SYNOPSIS \u2022 Introduction \u2022 Applicationunder Sec 12A \u2022 Charitable Purpose 2(15)",

                        "text": "I've now confirmed the correct URL through multiple official sources. Let me give you the definitive answer.\n\n## First \u2014 I Owe You a Correction\n\nI sent you to `incometax.gov.in` (the e-Filing portal, for logged-in taxpayer services). That was the wrong domain for public exemption verification. The correct portal is **`incometaxindia.gov.in`** (the main department website, without the \"e-\" filing part). These are two different websites run by the Income Tax Department, and the public search tool for exempt institutions lives only on the second one.\n\nSorry for the runaround. Here's the correct information now.\n\n---\n\n## The Official Tool \u2014 Tax Exempted Institutions Search\n\n**Direct URL:** `https://incometaxindia.gov.in/Pages/utilities/exempted-institutions.aspx`\n\nAlso linked from: `https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/tax-exempted-institutions`\n\nThis is a public database maintained by the **Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)** listing all institutions that have registration/approval under Sections 12A, 12AA, 12AB, 80G, 10(23C), 35(1)(ii)/(iii), and similar exemption provisions.\n\n### How to Navigate to It (Menu Path)\n\nIf the direct URL gives issues in your browser, navigate manually:\n\n1. Go to **`incometaxindia.gov.in`** (the CBDT main site, NOT `incometax.gov.in`)\n2. On the top navigation, click **\"Tax Information & Services\"**\n3. In the dropdown, look under **\"Tax Utilities\"**\n4. Click **\"Tax Exempted Institutions\"**\n\nOr from the homepage, look for a section called **\"Important Links\"** or **\"Quick Access\"** \u2014 \"Tax Exempted Institutions\" is listed there as one of the utilities.\n\n### How to Search\n\nThe search interface offers multiple fields \u2014 **use PAN of the trust as the primary search key**, because:\n\n- Trust names have spelling variations (Vithalani/Vithlani/Vitthalani)\n- The database is huge (over 2 lakh institutions listed)\n- PAN is unique and exact\n\n**Search fields available:**\n- Name of the institution\n- PAN (recommended)\n- Section (dropdown: 12A, 12AA, 12AB, 80G, 10(23C), 35(1)(ii)/(iii), etc.)\n- Text search\n- Advanced search: date range, approving authority, jurisdiction\n\n**For your trust:** Enter PAN **AAZTS5070P** (from your affidavit filename) and search across all sections.\n\n### Important Caveats About This Tool\n\nBased on official sources and user reports:\n\n1. **The database is imperfect.** The Income Tax Department itself displays a disclaimer that information is subject to change and may not reflect real-time status.\n2. **Sometimes only PAN shows without the name/address** \u2014 this is a known limitation, not an error.\n3. **Post-2020 12AB registrations are supposed to be listed**, but there's known lag in updating.\n4. **There is no user support** \u2014 no button or email to raise queries about missing entries.\n\n---\n\n## Alternative Method \u2014 Login to E-Filing Portal (Most Reliable)\n\nIf the public search shows nothing or partial data, the definitive check is:\n\n1. Go to **`incometax.gov.in`** (the e-Filing portal this time)\n2. Click **\"Login\"** \u2014 top right\n3. Enter the trust's PAN as User ID\n4. If never logged in before, you or a trustee will need to **register** first (create password, link mobile/email)\n5. Once logged in, go to **\"Pending Actions\"** or **\"Services\"** \u2192 **\"View Registrations\"** / **\"My Registrations\"** or under **\"Profile\"**\n6. Any active 12A / 12AB / 80G / 10(23C) registrations will be clearly listed with:\n - Registration number\n - Section\n - Date of order\n - Validity period\n - Order (Form 10AC) downloadable as PDF\n\nThis is the trust's own tax record \u2014 100% authoritative.\n\n---\n\n## Two Other Ways to Confirm 12A Status\n\n### 1. Check the Bank Account for Interest TDS\nIf the trust has a bank account with any deposits, check whether the bank has been deducting **TDS on interest**. If the trust had 12A registration, the trustees would typically have submitted **Form 15G** or a lower/nil TDS certificate to the bank. If the bank has been deducting normal TDS on interest, that's an indirect indicator that no 12A exemption was on record.\n\n### 2. Check the Trust's Form 26AS / AIS\nLog in with the trust's PAN on the e-filing portal \u2192 **\"Services\"** \u2192 **\"Annual Information Statement (AIS)\"** or **\"Form 26AS\"**. This shows all tax-relevant transactions the department knows about. If 12A/80G registration exists, the profile will reflect the exempt entity classification.\n\n---\n\n## Try This Order and Report Back\n\n1. **First** \u2014 Direct URL: `incometaxindia.gov.in/Pages/utilities/exempted-institutions.aspx` \u2014 search by PAN AAZTS5070P\n2. **If that fails** \u2014 Log in to `incometax.gov.in` with the trust's PAN (register if needed)\n3. **Send me a screenshot** of what shows up\n\nOnce we have hard confirmation of whether 12A exists or not, we can plan the actual next steps \u2014 either use the existing registration, or apply fresh via Form 10A. Take your time, and thank you for pushing back when I pointed you to wrong pages. That kind of check helps us get to the truth faster.",

                "text": "Perfect, you're on the right page. Here's exactly what to enter.\n\n## What to Fill In\n\nBased on the fields shown, here's the recommended approach:\n\n### Best Approach \u2014 Search by PAN\n\n| Field | What to Enter |\n|---|---|\n|                 "text": "This is a really sharp question, and I want to answer it very carefully \u2014 because your intuition here is only partially correct, and the difference matters a lot for what you do next.\n\n## The Short Answer\n\n**Yes, it matters. A lot. And no \u2014 NPO Darpan approving your registration does NOT prove the trust has 12A/80G, nor does it fully verify Charity Commissioner registration.**\n\nLet me explain why.\n\n---\n\n## What NPO Darpan Actually Verifies\n\nNPO Darpan (NITI Aayog) is essentially a **directory / registry** \u2014 not a legal validator. Its purpose is to give NGOs a Unique ID so government departments can identify them when disbursing grants or CSR funds.\n\nWhen you registered on NPO Darpan, here's what actually happened technically:\n\n1. **PAN verification** \u2014 Darpan checks with the Income Tax Department that the PAN exists and belongs to a trust entity. **This confirms only that a PAN was issued** \u2014 it does NOT confirm 12A, 80G, or even Charity Commissioner registration.\n\n2. **Aadhaar linkage** \u2014 Verifies your and other trustees' Aadhaar.\n\n3. **Self-declaration of registration details** \u2014 You typed in \"1448\" and \"21/01/2020\" and \"Bombay Public Trust Act 1950\" yourself. Darpan **accepted your declaration** \u2014 it did NOT cross-verify this with the Charity Commissioner's database.\n\n4. **Mobile/email OTP** \u2014 Basic contact validation.\n\nThat's it. Darpan is largely a **declaration-based system**. You said the trust is registered, you provided a number, they gave you a Unique ID.\n\n---\n\n## Why PAN Alone Doesn't Prove Registration Status\n\nThis is the critical part most people miss.\n\nThe Income Tax Department issues PAN cards to trusts based on the **Trust Deed alone**. The PAN application (Form 49A) requires:\n- Trust deed\n- Address proof\n- Trustees' ID\n- Application fee\n\n**It does NOT require Charity Commissioner registration certificate.** A PAN can be issued to an unregistered trust \u2014 it just identifies the trust as a taxable entity for the Income Tax Department.\n\n**Having a PAN \u2260 being legally registered**\n**Having a PAN \u2260 having 12A / 80G**\n**Having a PAN \u2260 being tax-exempt**\n\nThe PAN just means \"this entity exists in our records and here's its ID for tax purposes.\"\n\n---\n\n## What This Means For Your Trust \u2014 The Real Picture\n\nLet's put together everything we've learned:\n\n| Registration | Status | Evidence |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Trust Deed executed** | \u2705 Yes | Signed June 2019, on stamp paper |\n| **Application filed with Charity Commissioner** | \u2705 Yes | Stamped Schedule II dated 22/07/2019 |\n| **Charity Commissioner registration completed** | \u2753 Unknown | Not findable on portal, no certificate in your possession |\n| **PAN issued by IT Department** | \u2705 Yes | AAZTS5070P (based on filename) |\n| **Bank account opened** | \u2705 Yes | You confirmed |\n| **12A / 12AB registration** | \u274c Not registered | Confirmed absent from CBDT exempt institutions database |\n| **80G registration** | \u274c Not registered | Same |\n| **NPO Darpan Unique ID** | \u2705 Yes | You obtained this in April 2026 |\n\n**So the trust has legal existence (deed + PAN + bank + Darpan), but its status under the Charity Commissioner is unverified, and it has NO tax exemption.**\n\n---\n\n## Why This \"Matters a Lot\" Practically\n\nHere's what changes based on registration status:\n\n### If Charity Commissioner Registration is Complete but Not Digitized\n- Everything is fine legally\n- You just need to obtain the certified PTR extract from the Jamkhambhaliya office\n- Then apply for Provisional 12A + 80G via Form 10A\n- Full operations can begin\n\n### If Charity Commissioner Registration is Pending / Lapsed\n- Trust operates in a legal grey zone\n- Cannot legally solicit donations from public\n- Cannot get 12A / 80G because those require CC registration proof\n- Any donation received would be taxable as income\n- Any expenditure on \"charitable activities\" cannot claim tax exemption\n\n### If Trust Is Fully Unregistered With CC\n- Technically the trust is a **private trust** or an **unregistered trust**, not a **registered public charitable trust**\n- Under Bombay Public Trusts Act, Section 18, registration is **mandatory** for public trusts in Gujarat within 3 months of creation\n- Failure to register = penalty under Section 66 of the Act\n- Cannot claim to be a \"public charitable trust\" or issue formal donation receipts\n- NPO Darpan ID does not confer any legal legitimacy \u2014 it's just a directory listing\n\n---\n\n## Why NPO Darpan Doesn't \"Fix\" Anything\n\nNPO Darpan is a **destination** for already-legitimate NGOs, not a **source** of legitimacy. It's like:\n\n- A phone directory listing your business doesn't make your business legally registered\n- A LinkedIn profile doesn't make you employed\n- A wedding photo on Instagram doesn't legally register your marriage\n\nNPO Darpan itself has a disclaimer stating that registration on the portal is **NOT a proof of authenticity or legality** of the organization. It's essentially a self-service database.\n\nYou'll notice in your own affidavit for Darpan, you signed a declaration accepting that:\n- Darpan registration is not proof/verification of authenticity/legality of the organisation\n- The Aayog is not liable for anything about the organisation's legality\n- You accept full responsibility\n\nThat's the government explicitly telling you: \"We're not verifying that you're a real registered trust. That's on you.\"\n\n---\n\n## What You Absolutely Need to Do Now\n\n**Priority 1 \u2014 Verify Actual Charity Commissioner Registration Status**\n\nThis isn't optional anymore. Given that:\n- The trust doesn't appear on the CC online portal\n- No 12A/80G exists (meaning no post-registration compliance ever happened)\n- No physical certificate is in your possession\n- The advocates who filed it are no longer in contact\n\n...there's a real possibility that the 2019 application never completed to final registration. You cannot build operations, take donations, or apply for 12A/80G on top of an unverified base.\n\n**Action steps in order:**\n\n1. **This week** \u2014 Ask your father to physically dig through every file, drawer, folder, envelope at home. Also ask him what he remembers about receiving any Charity Commissioner document in 2019-2020.\n\n2. **This week** \u2014 Call/visit the bank branch. Ask for a copy of the trust's KYC file. The registration certificate (if it exists) will be there.\n\n3. **Within 2 weeks** \u2014 Physical visit to Assistant Charity Commissioner office at Jamkhambhaliya. Take Schedule II copy showing 22/07/2019 filing stamp. Ask them to search inward register for that date and check current status.\n\n**Do not proceed with any donations, activities, publicity, or 12A/80G application until this is resolved.**\n\n---\n\n## A Direct, Honest Word\n\nVraj, I understand this is not what you hoped to hear. You've clearly done a lot already \u2014 NPO Darpan, understanding the trust's objectives, planning digital operations. But you're building on an uncertain foundation.\n\nThe good news: this is completely fixable. Either the registration exists and just needs to be located, or it needs to be freshly filed. Neither is a disaster. What would be a disaster is starting real operations, taking real donations, publishing real activities, and then discovering 6 months later that the base registration is invalid \u2014 because then every transaction, every donor, every activity becomes legally messy to unwind.\n\nDo the three action steps above this month. Once we have clarity on CC registration status, we can plan the actual operational launch, 12A/80G filing, website, activities, and fundraising with total confidence. Your skills in digital marketing and development will make this trust genuinely successful \u2014 but only on top of a verified legal foundation.\n\nWant me to help you draft the application letter for the physical visit to the Charity Commissioner office, or an RTI application as a parallel track?",

                "uuid": "019f9b29-847e-7778-be29-526734d56bd2",
                "text": "Good questions. Let me answer each directly and honestly.\n\n## 1. Why Does It Matter That the Trust Doesn't Show on \"Know Your Trust\"?\n\n**Legally \u2014 it doesn't invalidate anything.**\n\nThe online portal is just a digital display of the Charity Commissioner's records. Non-appearance online can mean:\n- Records not digitized yet (very common for sub-district offices like Jamkhambhaliya)\n- Data entry lag or spelling mismatch\n- Or, in some cases, incomplete registration\n\n**Practically \u2014 it creates three real friction points:**\n\n**(a) Donor confidence** \u2014 Serious donors, especially corporates and NRIs, verify trusts online before donating. If they can't find your trust on the Gujarat government portal, they'll hesitate. Your digital marketing skills know this \u2014 trust signals matter.\n\n**(b) 12A/80G application review** \u2014 When your CA files Form 10A, the Income Tax officer reviewing it may cross-check the CC portal. If the trust isn't listed there, they may raise a query asking for additional proof of registration. This delays approval by weeks or months.\n\n**(c) Bank scrutiny for large transactions** \u2014 When your trust starts receiving donations, banks flag large credits and sometimes re-verify registration. Portal non-appearance can trigger a KYC re-verification request.\n\n**None of these are legal disqualifiers.** They're operational friction. As long as you have the physical certificate (or PTR extract) in hand, you can address each of these issues when they arise.\n\n**Bottom line:** Not on portal \u2260 illegal. But get the physical certificate in hand \u2014 that's your armor against all these frictions.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Can You Register for 12A / 12AB / 80G Online Yourself?\n\n**Yes, absolutely.** The entire process is online through the Income Tax e-Filing portal, and given your skills, documents, and backup team, you can definitely handle it yourself.\n\nHere's the process:\n\n### The Form and Path\n- **Form 10A** \u2014 for fresh Provisional Registration (your case)\n- Filed at **`incometax.gov.in`** \u2192 Login with trust PAN \u2192 **e-File** \u2192 **Income Tax Forms** \u2192 **File Income Tax Forms** \u2192 Select **Form 10A**\n\n### What You'll Need Ready\n1. **Trust PAN** (have it)\n2. **Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)** of the authorized trustee \u2014 mandatory for trusts, OR Aadhaar OTP-based e-verification for the authorized signatory\n3. **Trust Deed** \u2014 certified copy, PDF (have it)\n4. **Charity Commissioner Registration Certificate** \u2014 this is the sticking point right now\n5. **NGO Darpan Unique ID** (have it)\n6. **PAN and Aadhaar of all trustees** (have)\n7. **Bank account details** of the trust (have)\n8. **Trust's activities details** \u2014 a note on current and proposed activities\n9. **Financial statements** \u2014 if any activity happened (in your case, none since inactive)\n\n### Two Applications, Filed Together\n- **Section 12AB** \u2014 for tax exemption on trust's own income\n- **Section 80G** \u2014 for donor tax deduction\n\nBoth use Form 10A. Filed simultaneously. **Both cost nothing** in government fees (only professional fees if you engage a CA).\n\n### Timeline\n- After filing, Form 10A is processed by the Commissioner (Exemptions)\n- Provisional registration is typically granted within **1 month**\n- Order comes in **Form 10AC** \u2014 a PDF you download from the portal\n- Provisional 12AB valid for **3 years**\n- Provisional 80G also valid for 3 years\n- Later, convert to regular via **Form 10AB** within 6 months of starting activities or 6 months before provisional expiry (whichever earlier)\n\n### The Real Blocker\nEvery 12A/80G application asks for the field: **\"Registration No. under the Bombay Public Trust Act, 1950 / State Trust Act\"**. Without a valid CC registration number here, the application either can't be submitted, or gets rejected on review.\n\n**So you can absolutely file this yourself \u2014 once the CC certificate is in hand.**\n\nYour instinct to talk to your CA about it is right, but the actual filing you can do yourself. The CA is useful for the strategy (what to declare in activities, how to word the objects summary, how to project financials for the 3-year provisional period). The mechanical filing takes about 90 minutes.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Can You Legally Take Donations on Monday?\n\nThis is where I need to be very direct with you, because the answer isn't a simple yes.\n\n### Technical Legal Answer\n\n**Yes, an unregistered or partially-registered trust CAN receive donations.** No law prohibits people from voluntarily giving money to a trust. The trust deed itself creates a valid entity capable of receiving funds.\n\n### But Here's What Actually Happens Legally\n\n**(a) On the trust's side:**\n- Without 12A/12AB, **every rupee received is taxable income of the trust**\n- Trust would need to file **ITR-7** and pay income tax at applicable rates (up to 30%+ plus surcharge and cess) on donations received\n- No exemption for money spent on charitable activities either \u2014 because tax exemption under Sections 11 and 12 requires 12A registration\n\n**(b) On the donor's side:**\n- Donor gets **no tax deduction** under Section 80G\n- Donor cannot claim the donation as CSR expenditure (needs CSR-1, which needs 12A/80G)\n- If a corporate donor asks for an 80G receipt and you can't provide one, deal falls apart\n\n**(c) Charity Commissioner side (this is important):**\n- Under **Section 18 of the Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950**, registration is **mandatory** within 3 months of trust creation\n- Operating a public trust that isn't registered can attract penalty under **Section 66** \u2014 fine and potentially imprisonment for the trustees\n- If registration status is unclear, you're technically operating in the grey zone the moment donations start flowing\n\n**(d) Practical operational issues:**\n- Bank may flag unusual credits \u2014 trust accounts are monitored under PMLA (Prevention of Money Laundering Act)\n- If donations come from multiple sources, cash reporting rules kick in\n- Trust must maintain proper books of accounts from day one of operations\n- Auditing becomes mandatory when income crosses threshold\n\n### So If You Take a Donation on Monday\n\nSay your uncle donates \u20b950,000 on Monday. Here's the reality:\n\n- The bank credits the trust account\n- The trust has now started operations\n- The trust must file ITR-7 for FY 2026-27 declaring this \u20b950,000 as income\n- Since no 12A exists, this \u20b950,000 is fully taxable \u2014 tax of ~\u20b915,000+ payable\n- Your uncle gets zero tax benefit for donating\n- If Charity Commissioner registration is incomplete, and someone files a complaint, trustees face inquiry\n\n**Compare to waiting 30-45 days:**\n\n- Verify/complete CC registration (3-4 weeks max)\n- File Form 10A for Provisional 12A + 80G (1-2 hours to file, ~30 days for order)\n- Take the same \u20b950,000 donation with:\n - \u20b90 tax to the trust (fully exempt if spent on activities)\n - Your uncle gets \u20b925,000 tax deduction (50% under 80G)\n - Fully compliant, no future headaches\n\n---\n\n## My Straight Answer to \"Can I Take Donations on Monday?\"\n\n**Legally you can, but you shouldn't.**\n\nThe cost of waiting 45 days is nothing. The cost of starting without registration is:\n- Real tax liability on donations received in the interim\n- Lost donor goodwill (they'll ask \"why can't you give me 80G receipt?\")\n- Legal exposure under BPT Act if CC registration is incomplete\n- Compliance mess to unwind later\n\n**Better plan:**\n\n**Week 1-2:** Verify CC registration status (physical visit to Jamkhambhaliya + bank KYC file + advocate's old office)\n\n**Week 3:** Either get the PTR extract in hand, or complete pending steps for registration\n\n**Week 4:** File Form 10A on income tax portal for Provisional 12A + 80G (you can do this yourself, use your CA as backup for review before submission)\n\n**Week 8:** Provisional registrations in hand\n\n**Week 9 onwards:** Take donations, run activities, publicize, do everything at full scale \u2014 with zero legal, tax, or donor-side friction\n\n---\n\n## One More Thing\n\nYou mentioned you have a lawyer and CA team as backup. That's excellent. Use them for **one specific task this week**: ask them (or better, your father, since he's the President) to write to the Jamkhambhaliya ACC office asking for the current status of the July 2019 filing, and to obtain a certified PTR extract if registered.\n\nYour CA can also do the 12A/80G filing for a small fee (\u20b95,000-\u20b915,000 typically), but honestly, given your background, you can file it yourself once CC registration is verified. I'd suggest doing it yourself and just having the CA review the draft before submission \u2014 that way you learn the process (useful for future compliance work) and save money.\n\nReady to plan the CC verification step in detail? I can help you draft the exact application letter (in Gujarati or English) that your father can carry to the Jamkhambhaliya office, or send by post.",

DEVKUNVARBEN KESHAVLAL BHANAJI VITHALANI CHARITABLE TRUST`**\n\n**Important:** The name must match the trust's PAN card **exactly, character-by-character** \u2014 including punctuation, spelling, and spaces. If the PAN card spells it differently (e.g., \"DEVKUVARBEN\" without the \"n\" after \"kunv\", or \"VITHLANI\" instead of \"VITHALANI\"), use that exact spelling.\n\n**How to verify the correct spelling:**\n- Look at the physical PAN card of the trust\n- Or check the affidavit you already have \u2014 it uses: **`SVA. DEVKUNVARBEN KESHAVLAL BHANAJI VITHALANI CHARITABLE TRUST`**\n\nThe affidavit spelling should match PAN (since the affidavit was generated using PAN data), so this is likely correct.\n\n---\n\n### Date of Incorporation\n\nThis is the **date the trust was created** \u2014 meaning the **date the Trust Deed was executed and signed**.\n\n**Enter:** **`12/06/2019`** (12 June 2019)\n\nThis is the date on your Trust Deed. Do NOT use:\n- The date of Schedule II filing (22/07/2019)\n- The NPO Darpan date (21/01/2020)\n- Any other date\n\nThe **Date of Incorporation** for a trust = **date of execution of the Trust Deed**.\n\n---\n\n## What to Fill in Subsequent Steps\n\nSince you'll move through more tabs and steps, here's what to expect and what to enter:\n\n### Basic Details Tab (this page)\n| Field | Value |\n|---|---|\n| PAN of Organization | AAZTS5070P (auto-filled \u2014 verify it matches) |\n| Name of Organization | SVA. DEVKUNVARBEN KESHAVLAL BHANAJI VITHALANI CHARITABLE TRUST |\n| Date of Incorporation | 12/06/2019 |\n\nClick **Continue**.\n\n### Principal Contact Details Tab\nThis is for the **authorized signatory** \u2014 the person who will be the primary contact for the Income Tax Department. This should be a **trustee**, typically the **President or Treasurer**.\n\nFor your trust, the natural choice is your **father, Hasmukhlal Keshavlal Vithalani (President)**, OR **Vishwa Hasmukhbhai Vithalani (Treasurer)** \u2014 since the treasurer role typically handles tax and financial matters.\n\nYou'll need:\n- Full name (as per Aadhaar/PAN of the trustee)\n- **PAN of the trustee** (not the trust's PAN)\n- Date of birth\n- Aadhaar number\n- Designation (President / Secretary / Treasurer)\n- Mobile number (this will be OTP-verified)\n- Email ID (this will be OTP-verified)\n\n**Important consideration:** The mobile and email you enter here will be the **official contact** for all future IT Department communications. Choose an email you control and check regularly. Also set a **secure question** for recovery.\n\n**Save these credentials safely** \u2014 this is the login for all future IT Department interactions for the trust.\n\n---\n\n## One Important Clarification\n\nJust so we're on the same page \u2014 this registration you're doing right now is **NOT the 12A/80G application**. Receive Form 10AC (provisional registration order) in ~30 days\n5. Then start operations, take donations, everything at full scale\n\n---\n\n## Also \u2014 About the Second Tab \"Aadarsh card Pancard\" I See\n\nI notice you have a second tab open labeled \"Aadarsh card Pancard\" (probably \"Aadhaar card / PAN card\"). In practical terms, the Principal Officer is the linchpin between the tax authorities ...\n\nThe term \u201cPrincipal Officer\u201d carries significant weight within the context of Indian income tax laws. Understanding the responsibilities and implications associated with this role is crucial for businesses and individuals subject to income tax regulations. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the Principal Officer, their duties, and the legal framework governing their actions. Under Section 2(35) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, the Principal Officer is defined as an individual who holds a pivotal position in an organization or it\u2019s a person who has been appointed as such by the organization. \n\nThe key characteristic of a Principal Officer is their authority and responsibility to act on behalf of the entity in matters relating to the Indian income tax. In practical terms, the Principal Officer is the linchpin between the tax authorities and the organization.\n\nThe appointment of a Principal Officer is mandatory for certain entities as per the provisions of the Income Tax Act. In the case of a company, the Managing Director, Director, Manager, or Secretary of the company is usually deemed as the Principal Officer. Alternatively, any person responsible for the management or functioning of the company can also be designated as the Principal Officer. In the context of a firm, the term \u201cPrincipal Officer\u201d encompasses any partner or a person responsible for the management of the firm. \n\nFor other entities such as an association or a body of individuals, any member or person responsible for the management of the affairs of the association or the body would be considered the Principal Officer. Let me analyze based on your trust deed and the law.\n\n## The Legal Basis \u2014 Section 2(35) of Income Tax Act, 1961\n\nThe **\"Principal Officer\"** is a specific legal term defined in Section 2(35) of the Income Tax Act. For a trust (which is treated as an Association of Persons / body of individuals under IT law), the Principal Officer means:\n\n> *\"the **secretary, treasurer, manager or agent** of the authority, company, association or body, or any person connected with the management or administration...\"*\n\n**This is important:** \"Principal Officer\" is a **statutory role** with specific legal responsibilities under Income Tax Act \u2014 including liability for tax compliance, TDS defaults, penalties, and prosecution. It's not just a form field selection.\n\n## Analyzing Your Situation\n\nThe dropdown offers:\n- Principal Officer\n- Trustee\n- Secretary\n- Office Bearer\n- Manager\n- Managing Trustee\n\nNow let me map this against Vishwa's actual role in your Trust Deed:\n\n**From your Trust Deed:** Vishwa Hasmukhbhai Vithalani is designated as **\u0a96\u0a9c\u0abe\u0aa8\u0a9a\u0ac0 (Treasurer)**.\n\n**From Section 2(35) of IT Act:** \"Treasurer\" of an association qualifies as a Principal Officer **by statute** \u2014 no separate appointment needed.\n\n**From your Trust Deed:** There's no \"Managing Trustee\" role defined. The deed defines three specific roles \u2014 President (\u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0aae\u0ac1\u0a96), Secretary (\u0aae\u0a82\u0aa4\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac0), and Treasurer (\u0a96\u0a9c\u0abe\u0aa8\u0a9a\u0ac0). No one is designated as \"Managing Trustee.\"\n\n## My Recommendation \u2014 With Reasoning\n\n**Select: \"Principal Officer\"**\n\n### Why This is the Correct Choice\n\n1. **Statutory alignment** \u2014 Under Section 2(35) of the Income Tax Act, a Treasurer of an association/body of individuals is automatically a Principal Officer. Since Vishwa is the Treasurer per your Trust Deed, she legally qualifies as Principal Officer without needing any additional appointment or resolution.\n\n2. **Matches actual role** \u2014 The IT department uses \"Principal Officer\" as the standard designation for the person handling tax affairs of a trust. This is the most legally accurate and precise selection.\n\n3. **Avoids incorrect designations:**\n - **\"Managing Trustee\"** \u2014 WRONG for your trust. Your Trust Deed does not create a \"Managing Trustee\" role. Selecting this would misrepresent the trust's actual structure. If ever questioned, you'd have to produce a Board Resolution or Trust Deed provision creating a Managing Trustee \u2014 which you don't have.\n - **\"Trustee\"** \u2014 Too generic. She is a trustee, but so are all three. This doesn't identify her specific role.\n - **\"Secretary\"** \u2014 WRONG. The Secretary of your trust is Sagunaben, not Vishwa. Selecting this misrepresents the trust's structure.\n - **\"Manager\"** \u2014 Not applicable; no manager role exists in your Trust Deed.\n - **\"Office Bearer\"** \u2014 Vague, and less precise than Principal Officer.\n\n4. **What the IT department expects** \u2014 The IT portal, Form 10A, ITR-7, all communications with Assessing Officer, refer to the trust's contact person as \"Principal Officer.\" Selecting Principal Officer here creates continuity across all future filings.\n\n5. **Legal implication awareness** \u2014 Being designated as Principal Officer carries responsibilities (as case law confirmed): timely tax filing, TDS compliance, replying to notices. Vishwa should be aware of this. Given you're operating the trust practically on her behalf, ensure she understands that formal notices will legally target her, even if you're handling the operational work.\n\n---\n\n## Final Values to Enter \u2014 Vishwa's Details\n\n| Field | Value | Source |\n|---|---|---|\n| Residential Status | Resident | She lives in India |\n| PAN | BTYPV3797D | Her PAN card |\n| Last Name | VITHLANI | Exact PAN spelling |\n| Middle Name | HASMUKHBHAI | Exact PAN spelling |\n| First Name | VISHVA | Exact PAN spelling (not \"VISHWA\") |\n| Date Of Birth | **19/09/2000** | You confirmed PAN and Aadhaar both show this |\n| Gender | Female | Both PAN and Aadhaar |\n| Designation | **Principal Officer** | Section 2(35) IT Act \u2014 Treasurer qualifies |\n\n---\n\n## Before You Click Continue\n\n**Two small checks:**\n\n1. **DOB confirmation** \u2014 You said you verified manually that PAN and Aadhaar both show the same DOB. Just double-confirm: is it **19/09/2000** or **10/09/2000**? Because in my earlier analysis I noticed what appeared to be a scan artifact. If you've verified physically and both docs show the same date, use whatever that confirmed date is.\n\n2. **Name field spellings** \u2014 I see in your screenshot the Last Name field appears to already show \"VITHLANI\" (visible partially). Confirm Middle Name has HASMUKHBHAI and First Name has VISHVA before proceeding.\n\n---\n\n## One More Thing \u2014 About This Choice Long-Term\n\nSince Vishwa will now be the Principal Officer of record with the Income Tax Department:\n\n- All IT notices come to her name\n- She'll be the \"assessee representative\" in any tax proceedings\n- She should ideally e-verify all future filings using her Aadhaar OTP\n- If she ever moves abroad, changes jobs to a role incompatible with this responsibility, or becomes unavailable, this can be changed via the portal by adding a new authorized signatory (I saw this in the IT portal user manual \u2014 there's an \"Add Authorized Signatory\" flow)\n\nFor now, this is a solid choice. Select **Principal Officer** and proceed. Share the next screen when you're ready.",

Check your father's Aadhaar card PIN \u2014 that's the authoritative PIN for that address.\n\n---\n\n## What I Recommend You Do \u2014 In Order\n\n1. **First, scroll the entire Area/Locality dropdown** \u2014 the screenshot may have cut off. If it says something different from 361335, use that PIN and the dropdowns may repopulate with different options.\n\n3. **Third, check the physical post office** \u2014 Look at any recent postal mail delivered to Kharva Pado. The delivery office name will tell you the exact post office.\n\n4. **If still stuck**, choose:\n - **Post Office:** Dwarka Town S.O\n - **Area/Locality:** Nageshvar (closest match to Kharva Pado area within Dwarka town)\n - **Town/City/District:** JAMNAGAR (mandatory, only option)\n - **State:** Gujarat\n\n---\n\n## Important Point About This Address Selection\n\nI want to be very transparent with you: this address selection issue is a common minor imperfection in the IT portal for small-town addresses. Area/Locality is more of a soft classification.\n\n**But before we finalize:** Please scroll through the full Area/Locality dropdown one more time \u2014 look carefully for any Dwarka-related option I might have missed. This is a completely different thing from what we were doing.\n\n## Why You Must NOT Fill This\n\n**Filing an ITR triggers actual tax compliance for the assessment year you select.** Once filed:\n- It becomes part of the trust's official tax record\n- It cannot be casually undone\n- Filing an incorrect ITR (wrong AY, wrong figures, wrong form type) creates real legal complications\n- Filing an ITR for a trust without 12A/12AB registration means declaring ALL income (even zero) under the wrong tax regime\n- Filing a \"nil\" ITR when the trust hasn't had any activity is still a formal declaration to the IT Department\n\n**Trusts don't file the same ITR forms as individuals.** Trusts file **ITR-7** (for charitable/religious trusts with 12A), not ITR-1/2/3/4. And you don't even have 12A yet, which makes this whole flow inappropriate right now.\n\n## What Happened\n\nThe IT portal has a feature where, after login, it sometimes lands users directly on the ITR filing page (as a \"shortcut\" to encourage filing). You can see the note on the right:\n> *\"You've been directed to the 'File Income Tax Return' page right after login to make it easier to file your return.\"*\n\nThis is just a landing convenience \u2014 **not a requirement**. You don't have to file anything.\n\n---\n\n## What You Should Do RIGHT NOW\n\n### Step 1: Navigate Away From This Page\n\nClick on **\"Dashboard\"** in the top navigation menu (I can see it in your screenshot). Do NOT click Continue on this page.\n\n### Step 2: Log Out (Optional but Recommended)\n\nFor now, log out of the trust's IT portal account. Click on the profile icon (top right where it says \"SVA. DEVKUNVARB...\") and select \"Logout.\"\n\nWe've achieved what we needed to achieve today:\n- \u2705 Registered the trust on the IT e-Filing portal\n- \u2705 Created login credentials for the trust\n- \u2705 Vishwa is now recorded as Principal Officer\n- \u2705 Contact details (mobile, email, address) are on record\n\n**That's all we needed for today.**\n\n### Step 3: Do NOT Come Back to Login Until We're Ready\n\nThe next time you log in, it should be for a specific purpose:\n- To file **Form 10A** for Provisional 12A + 80G registration (only after Charity Commissioner certificate is in hand)\n- To check any notices under \"Pending Actions\"\n- To verify no unexpected filings are needed\n\n---\n\n## Where We Actually Stand Now \u2014 The Real Priorities\n\nLet me remind you of the actual sequence we need to follow:\n\n### \ud83d\udea8 Immediate Priorities (Before Anything Else)\n\n**1. Locate/Verify the Charity Commissioner Registration Certificate**\n\nThis is still the biggest open question. Actions:\n- Ask your father to check every drawer, file, and locker at home\n- Visit the bank branch to get a copy from the trust's KYC file\n- Try to reach the original advocates at Krishna Shopping Center, M.G. Road, Dwarka\n- If all else fails, plan a trip to the Assistant Charity Commissioner office at Jamkhambhaliya\n\n**2. Do NOT Take Any Donations Until Above is Resolved**\n\nWe discussed this. Without the CC certificate and 12A/80G in hand, every donation received becomes fully taxable and legally risky.\n\n**3. Do NOT File Any ITR or Form Yet**\n\nIncluding today's ITR page you're seeing. Nothing needs to be filed for the trust until:\n- CC registration is verified\n- 12A/80G is applied for and received\n- The trust actually starts operations and receives income\n\n### \u23f3 Next Steps (After Above)\n\n- Apply Form 10A for Provisional 12A + 80G\n- Receive Form 10AC (provisional registration order)\n- Start operations, take donations, publicize\n- Then file ITR-7 at year-end\n\n---\n\n## Some Perspective on What You Accomplished Today\n\nVraj, you did really well today. You:\n- Set up the NPO Darpan registration (before I met you)\n- Understood the difference between various compliance layers\n- Pushed back when I made mistakes (which improved the accuracy of the work)\n- Verified details against actual documents instead of trusting my assumptions\n- Registered the trust on the Income Tax e-Filing portal \u2014 an important compliance foundation\n\nThat's genuinely valuable groundwork. The trust now has a proper digital identity with the Income Tax Department, and Vishwa is on record as the Principal Officer.\n\nBut please \u2014 **step away from the ITR filing page**.                 "text": "okay now for the local verify for cc, which office to visit and is it possible that I visit the office in surat instead of where it was registered?",

                "uuid": "019f9b4d-58e0-755f-8256-c6d248adbff8",
                "text": "Good question \u2014 and the answer has important legal nuance. Let me be precise here.\n\n## Short Answer\n\n**No, you cannot handle this at the Surat office.** You must visit either:\n1. **Assistant Charity Commissioner, Jamkhambhaliya** (where the original 2019 filing was made) \u2014 **primary**\n2. **Deputy Charity Commissioner, Rajkot Region** (parent regional office) \u2014 **secondary**\n3. **Charity Commissioner, Ahmedabad (Head Office)** \u2014 **last resort for state-level queries**\n\nLet me explain why the office matters legally.\n\n---\n\n## Why Jurisdiction Matters for This Query\n\nUnder the **Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950** (as applicable in Gujarat), Section 18 mandates that:\n\n> *\"Such application shall be made to the Deputy or Assistant Charity Commissioner **of the region or sub-region within the limits of which the trustee has an office for the administration of the trust or the trust property or where substantial portion of the trust property is situated.**\"*\n\n**Your trust's registered office is in Dwarka.** This falls under:\n- **Sub-region:** Devbhumi Dwarka\n- **Local Office:** Assistant Charity Commissioner, **Jamkhambhaliya**\n- **Regional Office:** Deputy Charity Commissioner, **Rajkot Region** (Jamkhambhaliya falls under Rajkot regional jurisdiction)\n- **State-level Office:** Charity Commissioner, Gujarat State, **Ahmedabad**\n\n**Surat is a completely different region.** Surat has its own Charity Commissioner office serving trusts registered in Surat and surrounding areas (South Gujarat). They:\n- Do NOT have your trust's file\n- Cannot access Jamkhambhaliya's paper records\n- Cannot verify or issue certified copies of trusts outside their jurisdiction\n- Their staff has no obligation to help with a case outside their region\n\nEven if you go to Surat, they'll politely tell you to visit Jamkhambhaliya (or route your query through Ahmedabad).\n\n---\n\n## Why This is Physical Record Territory\n\nHere's the practical reality of Indian charitable trust administration:\n\n**Paper-based system:** Each Assistant Charity Commissioner sub-office maintains its own **paper Public Trust Register (PTR)**, inward registers, order sheets, and case files. These are physical bound registers stored in the office. The Jamkhambhaliya office's PTR is in Jamkhambhaliya \u2014 not synchronized to other offices, not digitized fully, not accessible from Surat, Ahmedabad, or anywhere else.\n\n**No inter-office access:** Unlike Aadhaar or PAN which are centralized databases, Charity Commissioner records are decentralized. Each sub-office is essentially a separate records repository.\n\n**Officer authority:** The Assistant Charity Commissioner at Jamkhambhaliya is the sole authority who can:\n- Look up whether registration was completed\n- Issue certified PTR extracts\n- Confirm the registration number\n- Explain what pending action (if any) exists\n\n---\n\n## Recommended Approach \u2014 In Order\n\n### Option 1 (Best): Physical Visit to Jamkhambhaliya\n\n**Distance from Dwarka:** ~40-50 km (about 1-1.5 hours by road)\n\nThis is a day trip. Realistically, this is the fastest and most reliable route.\n\n**What to carry:**\n- Copy of Trust Deed\n- Copy of the stamped Schedule II (showing 22/07/2019 filing)\n- Copy of the affidavits\n- Copy of trust PAN card\n- Your Aadhaar\n- A signed authorization letter from your father (President) \u2014 because you're not a trustee yourself\n- \u20b9100-500 in cash for certified copy fees\n- Written application (I can help draft this)\n\n**What to ask:**\n- Confirm status of Schedule II application filed on 22/07/2019\n- Request certified copy of PTR entry (Schedule I)\n- Request certified copy of Registration Certificate\n- Ask for the exact registration number (format: G/xxx/Devbhoomi Dwarka)\n\n### Option 2 (If Physical Visit Is Difficult): RTI to Jamkhambhaliya\n\nIf you cannot travel to Jamkhambhaliya soon, file an **RTI (Right to Information)** application by post:\n\n- **Addressed to:** Public Information Officer, Office of the Assistant Charity Commissioner, Jamkhambhaliya, Dist. Devbhumi Dwarka, Gujarat\n- **Fee:** \u20b910 (via IPO \u2014 Indian Postal Order \u2014 payable to the office)\n- **Language:** Gujarati or English\n- **Response mandated within:** 30 days by law\n- **Speed:** Slower than physical visit but legally binding\n\n### Option 3 (If Both Above Fail): Escalate to Head Office\n\n**Only after** Jamkhambhaliya doesn't respond satisfactorily, then:\n- Write to **Office of the Charity Commissioner, Gujarat State, Dr. Jivraj Mehta Bhavan, Gandhinagar Highway, Ahmedabad** (verify current address \u2014 this may have changed)\n- Include copy of your Jamkhambhaliya application/RTI and their response (or non-response)\n- Ask for state-level intervention to resolve status\n\n---\n\n## Why NOT Surat Specifically\n\nI want to address this directly because I suspect you may be based in Surat, or have easier access to Surat than Dwarka right now.\n\n**Reasons Surat won't work:**\n\n1. **No file access** \u2014 Your trust's file is physically at Jamkhambhaliya. Surat's office has no reason to have it.\n\n2. **No system-level access** \u2014 Even if Surat's office wanted to help, they can't pull records from another sub-office's paper register.\n\n3. **Different jurisdiction** \u2014 Trusts registered in Surat file under Surat's Charity Commissioner. Your trust is registered in Devbhumi Dwarka jurisdiction. These are legally distinct.\n\n4. **Cannot issue certified copies** \u2014 Only the office that maintains the register can issue certified copies of entries in that register.\n\n5. **Staff will redirect you** \u2014 Best case, they'll politely tell you to visit Jamkhambhaliya.\n\n---\n\n## A Better Question You Might Be Asking\n\nIf you're asking \"can I avoid the trip to Jamkhambhaliya,\" the honest alternatives are:\n\n**Yes, you can avoid it if you:**\n\n1. **Send someone else with authority** \u2014 Your father (as President) can go directly, or authorize any advocate/CA in the Dwarka/Jamkhambhaliya area to visit on his behalf. This is often the practical solution \u2014 a local advocate in Jamkhambhaliya charging \u20b9500-2000 to handle the entire status inquiry and certified copy request.\n\n2. **File RTI by post** \u2014 Slower but doesn't require travel.\n\n3. **Engage a local advocate** \u2014 Many CA/advocate firms in Jamnagar or Jamkhambhaliya offer this as a routine service. They know the office staff, know the drill, and get results faster than an unfamiliar visitor.\n\n**No, you cannot avoid it if you try to use:**\n\n- Surat office\n- Ahmedabad head office (initially \u2014 they'll route you back)\n- Any online portal (since it doesn't show your trust)\n- Any general email inquiry\n\n---\n\n## My Practical Recommendation\n\nSince you're operating from wherever you are (Surat, based on your question), and physical Jamkhambhaliya visit may be inconvenient:\n\n**Best combined approach:**\n\n1. **Send your father to Jamkhambhaliya** \u2014 He's the President, based in Dwarka (40 km away), and can go with full legal authority. He carries all trust docs. This is ideal.\n\n2. **If your father can't go**, engage a **local advocate in Jamnagar or Dwarka** (any competent advocate practicing at Jamkhambhaliya's ACC office) to handle the entire inquiry. Cost: \u20b91,000-3,000 typically. They'll:\n - File the status inquiry\n - Get certified copies\n - Explain any pending action needed\n - Handle it all in 1-2 weeks\n\n3. **Parallel \u2014 File an RTI by post yourself** \u2014 as a backup track. Doesn't hurt to have both moving.\n\n---\n\n## Where Are You Currently Based?\n\nSince you asked about Surat specifically, I'm guessing you're operating from there. Just so I understand your logistical constraints better:\n\nAre you asking because:\n- (a) You live/work in Surat and can only visit an office there\n- (b) You'll be in Surat soon and hoped to combine trips\n- (c) You have a lawyer/CA contact in Surat you'd prefer to use\n\nLet me know and I can suggest the best route accordingly. If (c) is the answer, your Surat CA can help you draft the RTI or authorize a local advocate in Jamkhambhaliya on your behalf \u2014 that could work even if the physical visit needs to be at Jamkhambhaliya.\n\nAlso \u2014 since we're pausing operations until the CC certificate is resolved anyway, there's no rush to do this in a single day. Even 2-3 weeks to properly resolve this at the correct office is better than shortcuts that lead to dead ends.",

Some are physical actions (obtain copies, verify records).\n\n---\n\n## The List \u2014 For Your Lawyer\n\nYou can copy-paste the below directly into WhatsApp/email to your lawyer:\n\n---\n\n**\u0aa8\u0aae\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a95\u0abe\u0ab0 [\u0ab5\u0a95\u0ac0\u0ab2\u0ab6\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae],**\n\n\u0aae\u0abe\u0ab0\u0abe \u0aaa\u0ab0\u0abf\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab0\u0aa8\u0abe \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0ab8\u0a82\u0aac\u0a82\u0aa7\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0a95\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0ab2\u0ac0\u0a95 \u0aae\u0abe\u0ab9\u0abf\u0aa4\u0ac0 \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa6\u0ab8\u0acd\u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0a9c\u0acb \u0aae\u0ac7\u0ab3\u0ab5\u0ab5\u0abe \u0aae\u0abe\u0a9f\u0ac7 \u0aa4\u0aae\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac0 \u0aae\u0aa6\u0aa6 \u0a9c\u0acb\u0a88\u0a8f \u0a9b\u0ac7. \u0a95\u0ac3\u0aaa\u0abe \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa8\u0ac0\u0a9a\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aac\u0abe\u0aac\u0aa4\u0acb \u0aae\u0abe\u0a9f\u0ac7 \u0a85\u0ab8\u0abf\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0a9a\u0ac7\u0ab0\u0abf\u0a9f\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0aae\u0abf\u0ab6\u0aa8\u0ab0 \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8, \u0a9c\u0abe\u0aae\u0a96\u0a82\u0aad\u0abe\u0ab3\u0abf\u0aaf\u0abe\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aae\u0ac1\u0ab2\u0abe\u0a95\u0abe\u0aa4 \u0ab2\u0a88\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa4\u0aaa\u0abe\u0ab8 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0acb \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa6\u0ab8\u0acd\u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0a9c\u0acb \u0aae\u0ac7\u0ab3\u0ab5\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0aae\u0aa6\u0aa6 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0acb.\n\n**\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0ab5\u0abf\u0a97\u0aa4\u0acb:**\n\n- **\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae:** \u0ab8\u0acd\u0ab5. \u0aa6\u0ac7\u0ab5\u0a95\u0ac1\u0a82\u0ab5\u0ab0\u0aac\u0ac7\u0aa8 \u0a95\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0ab5\u0ab2\u0abe",

Some are physical actions (obtain copies, verify records).\n\n---\n\n## The List \u2014 For Your Lawyer\n\nYou can copy-paste the below directly into WhatsApp/email to your lawyer:\n\n---\n\n**\u0aa8\u0aae\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a95\u0abe\u0ab0 [\u0ab5\u0a95\u0ac0\u0ab2\u0ab6\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae],**\n\n\u0aae\u0abe\u0ab0\u0abe \u0aaa\u0ab0\u0abf\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab0\u0aa8\u0abe \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0ab8\u0a82\u0aac\u0a82\u0aa7\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0a95\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0ab2\u0ac0\u0a95 \u0aae\u0abe\u0ab9\u0abf\u0aa4\u0ac0 \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa6\u0ab8\u0acd\u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0a9c\u0acb \u0aae\u0ac7\u0ab3\u0ab5\u0ab5\u0abe \u0aae\u0abe\u0a9f\u0ac7 \u0aa4\u0aae\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac0 \u0aae\u0aa6\u0aa6 \u0a9c\u0acb\u0a88\u0a8f \u0a9b\u0ac7. \u0a95\u0ac3\u0aaa\u0abe \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa8\u0ac0\u0a9a\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aac\u0abe\u0aac\u0aa4\u0acb \u0aae\u0abe\u0a9f\u0ac7 \u0a85\u0ab8\u0abf\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0a9a\u0ac7\u0ab0\u0abf\u0a9f\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0aae\u0abf\u0ab6\u0aa8\u0ab0 \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8, \u0a9c\u0abe\u0aae\u0a96\u0a82\u0aad\u0abe\u0ab3\u0abf\u0aaf\u0abe\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aae\u0ac1\u0ab2\u0abe\u0a95\u0abe\u0aa4 \u0ab2\u0a88\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa4\u0aaa\u0abe\u0ab8 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0acb \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa6\u0ab8\u0acd\u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0a9c\u0acb \u0aae\u0ac7\u0ab3\u0ab5\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0aae\u0aa6\u0aa6 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0acb.\n\n**\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0ab5\u0abf\u0a97\u0aa4\u0acb:**\n\n- **\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae:** \u0ab8\u0acd\u0ab5. \u0aa6\u0ac7\u0ab5\u0a95\u0ac1\u0a82\u0ab5\u0ab0\u0aac\u0ac7\u0aa8 \u0a95\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0ab5\u0ab2\u0abe",
