                        "type": "text",
                        "text": "Good news: a fair amount is available to you *right now*, even before 12A/80G/FCRA come through \u2014 and a couple of things are worth doing this week because they unlock everything else later. Here's the full picture, organized by what's usable at each stage.\n\n## The one thing to do this week: NGO Darpan registration\n\nThis is separate from 12A/80G/FCRA, is free, and needs only your trust registration certificate, PAN, and basic details (trustee Aadhaar, bank passbook). As soon as your trust is registered and has basic documents like PAN and address proof, you can apply, and registration typically takes about 15\u201330 working days for verification. Do this immediately because it's a mandatory prerequisite for FCRA registration, and the Darpan Unique ID must be entered in your FCRA application later. It also makes you eligible to apply for government grants, schemes, and CSR funding down the line.\n\n## What you can use *right now*, with just the trust deed + PAN (no 12A/80G/FCRA needed)\n\n**Donations infrastructure:**\n- **Razorpay / Cashfree / PhonePe Business** \u2014 you can start accepting donations today. Razorpay Payment Pages let you accept donations online without even needing a website, using just your organization name, address proof, and PAN copy for KYC. The catch: without 80G, you can issue a plain receipt, but not one that gives the *donor* a tax deduction \u2014 that comes automatically once 80G is granted (Razorpay can auto-generate 80G receipts once you have it).\n- **Canva for Nonprofits** \u2014 100% free for registered nonprofits, NGOs, and social impact organizations with up to 50 users, and eligibility is based on being registered as a nonprofit/charitable organization in your country with a mission-driven, non-commercial purpose \u2014 a registered trust deed generally qualifies, doesn't strictly require 12A/80G.\n- **Zoho CRM free tier** \u2014 supports up to 3 users with core CRM functionality \u2014 leads, contacts, accounts, basic pipeline \u2014 usable immediately for donor/volunteer tracking, no registration status required. (Zoho's *discounted* nonprofit tier does ask for 80G/FCRA later.)\n- **TechSoup validation** \u2014 worth starting now. It doesn't require 12A/80G itself, just proof of registration such as your governing documents or a government publication evidencing registration status \u2014 this validation is the gateway to Microsoft/Adobe/other discounts later.\n\n## What's gated behind 12A/80G (your next milestone, 1\u20132 months out)\n\n- **Google Ad Grants** ($10,000/month in free Search ads) \u2014 India eligibility explicitly requires a valid 12A/80G certificate, plus an active website with substantial content.\n- **Microsoft 365 for Nonprofits** (free Business Basic + discounted Standard/Premium) \u2014 Indian nonprofits are verified via TechSoup using 80G, 12A, and trust deed documentation.\n- **Zoho's actual nonprofit discount** (vs. the free CRM tier) \u2014 requires valid 80G and FCRA registration for Indian trusts/societies/Section 8 companies.\n\n## What's gated behind FCRA specifically (the longer-term milestone)\n\nThis is the one to plan for, because it's stricter than most people expect: **Google for Nonprofits** (the umbrella program covering free Workspace, Ad Grants access, YouTube Nonprofit Program, Maps credits) has a peculiar India-specific rule \u2014 Indian NGOs must be registered under 12A/80G AND hold FCRA registration, confirmed directly on Google's own eligibility page: all eligible organizations in India must be registered under the Foreign Contribution Regulations Act. This is unusual \u2014 most countries only need charitable registration \u2014 but it's real, and there are ongoing community threads of young Indian NGOs asking Google for exceptions, generally without success. So: budget Google Workspace as a paid (or discounted-via-TechSoup) tool for now, not free, until FCRA comes through.\n\nNote FCRA itself typically requires ~3 years of operational existence in India before you're eligible to apply (it's not just paperwork \u2014 it's a waiting period), so this is realistically a later-stage goal, not a 1\u20132 month one like 12A/80G.\n\n## Meta/Facebook \u2014 a caveat worth knowing\n\nMeta's on-platform donate button and native fundraising tools are only available in the US, UK, Canada and Australia \u2014 in other countries, including India, Meta only lets you link out to a donation page on your own website. So plan for Instagram/Facebook as *traffic drivers to your own Razorpay-powered donation page*, not as a payment channel themselves.\n\n## Mapping this to your 8 requirements\n\n| Requirement | Usable now | Needs 12A/80G | Needs FCRA |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1. Website | Domain done \u2713; build on WordPress/low-cost hosting | Google Ad Grants for traffic | Google for Nonprofits full suite |\n| 2. Digital marketing | Canva (free), organic social, Meta linking out | Google Ad Grants ($10K/mo) | \u2014 |\n| 3. Trust management | Zoho CRM free tier, Google Sheets/Notion | Zoho nonprofit discount | Google Workspace free |\n| 4. Donations | Razorpay/Cashfree (no 80G receipt yet) | 80G-auto-receipts | Foreign donations legally require FCRA regardless |\n| 5. Volunteers | Zoho CRM/Forms, NGO Darpan listing | \u2014 | \u2014 |\n| 6. Helping the needy | Independent of registration status | \u2014 | \u2014 |\n| 7. Legal docs/receipts | Manual PAN-based receipts | 80G tax-deduction receipts | FCRA utilization reports |\n| 8. CMS | Zoho suite, WordPress, free tiers | Microsoft 365 discount | Google Workspace free |\n\nA quick note since your domain and trust are both fresh: keep 12A/80G and NGO Darpan moving in parallel rather than sequentially \u2014 Darpan has no prerequisites and unlocks credibility/CSR eligibility faster, while 12A/80G unlocks the donor-facing tax benefits and Ad Grants.\n\nWant me to go deeper into any one piece \u2014 like a concrete website tech-stack recommendation, or a step-by-step for the Razorpay/Cashfree donation setup?",

                "text": "I need to check the project knowledge base first, then search for information on grant programs available to charitable trusts like Google Ad Grants and Meta for Nonprofits, along with their eligibility requirements around 12A/80G/FCRA and Darpan registration.\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nI need to dig deeper into the project records to find the specific trust name, and I should also review the trust deed document for any relevant details.\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nI need to research several areas around nonprofit funding and resources in India\u2014Google Ad Grants eligibility, Meta and Instagram programs, TechSoup India, Microsoft and Canva nonprofit offerings, Darpan ID benefits, and the timeline requirements for 12A/80G/FCRA certifications, plus website hosting and CMS options. This is broad enough that I should probably suggest doing focused searches across these different topics.\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nNow I'm confirming that Google Ad Grants requires 501(c)(3) status, so they'll need to work toward that first, but I should search for other immediate options like Meta's nonprofit program for India, Microsoft's offerings, TechSoup India, Canva's nonprofit access, Darpan benefits, and available CMS platforms.\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nMeta's native fundraising tools aren't available in India, but nonprofits there can still use the donate button feature to link to external donation platforms, along with Meta Business Suite ads. Now I need to check what Microsoft, TechSoup India, and Canva offer for nonprofits in that region.\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nNow I'm looking at what NGOs can actually do right away without 12A/80G status\u2014things like setting up a website through free hosting platforms, using domain registrars, leveraging free design tools, accessing GitHub's nonprofit program, Zoho's NGO offerings, and Cloudflare or Netlify for hosting. I should also explore donation platforms available in India that don't require 80G certification, like Milaap, Ketto, ImpactGuru, and DonationBox, plus what they can accomplish during the pre-12A/80G phase.\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nNow I'm looking into NGO Darpan benefits and CSR registration requirements, then exploring donation management platforms suitable for small Indian NGOs\u2014checking options like Give.do and payment solutions that work without needing 80G certification, including crowdfunding platforms and payment gateways that support nonprofits.\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nNow I'm looking at domain-specific tools for nonprofits\u2014hosting options, GitHub, Cloudflare's nonprofit program, Zoho, and donation plugins like GiveWP. I'm also checking payment gateways that work for donations without 80G certification, like Razorpay and Instamojo, which only require PAN and bank account details, though I should note that donations won't be tax-deductible for donors without that certification. I have enough information to put together a thorough, well-organized response, and I'm just verifying a few more details on Zoho.\n\nLet me do a couple more targeted searches\u2014one for Canva, GitHub, and Zoho nonprofit programs, and another for donation payment gateways in India that don't require 80G status.\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nNow I'm organizing this into a clear roadmap\u2014first checking what's immediately actionable versus what depends on getting their 12A/80G and FCRA approvals, then mapping out each of their eight requirements against available programs, and finally laying out a recommended sequence for them to follow. Compiling the full list of source documents for citations across compliance, fundraising platforms, and tech assistance programs... I need to be careful about citing sources with personal contact information, so I'll rely on the general documents instead for the Razorpay and payment gateway requirements rather than the presentation that contains PII. Now I'm ready to structure the response with clear headers and minimal citations, keeping things concise and well-organized.Good news first: even with 12A/80G/FCRA still pending, there's a lot you can set up *right now* that won't need to be redone later. Here's the landscape, mapped to your 8 requirements.\n\n## The core gating factor to understand\n\nAlmost every \"free tech/marketing for nonprofits\" program in India gates on **12A + 80G** (sometimes both, sometimes just one), verified through **TechSoup India**:\n\n- **Google Ad Grants** \u2014 up to $10,000/month in free Search ad credit \u2014 requires a registered charitable organization with a valid 12A/80G certificate and an active website with substantial content. Applied for via registering as an NGO member of NASSCOM Foundation's program, which acts as TechSoup's local partner in India for Google's verification.\n- **Google Workspace for Nonprofits** \u2014 available for NGOs registered under 12A and 80G, applied through TechSoup India, with 2\u20134 week processing.\n- **Microsoft 365 for Nonprofits** \u2014 Business Basic is free for up to 300 users for verified Indian nonprofits with 80G/12A status via Microsoft Philanthropies through TechSoup India, and Business Standard/Premium come at a steep discount.\n- **Canva for Nonprofits** \u2014 100% free Canva Pro access for registered NGOs, again gated behind TechSoup verification.\n- **TechSoup catalog broadly** (Adobe, Zoom, Slack for Charities, security tools) \u2014 same story: organizations must first be validated by TechSoup as operating on a nonprofit basis for the public benefit, then meet each vendor's individual criteria.\n\n**So the single highest-leverage move right now is pushing 12A/80G through fast** \u2014 everything downstream (Google, Microsoft, Canva, Ad Grants) unlocks off the back of that one certificate pair.\n\n## What you can do *this week*, with zero gating\n\n**1. NGO Darpan registration (do this immediately, it's free and has no minimum-age requirement)**\nA newly formed NGO can register on Darpan right away \u2014 there's no minimum age requirement, though applying for specific government schemes may require the org to be at least a year old. It's foundational because:\n- Darpan UID is mandatory for FCRA registration\n- it's required to be mentioned in your CSR-1 filing, and while general CSR-1 rules expect 3 years of track record, a newly formed trust set up specifically to carry out CSR activities is an exception\n- it's required for most government and corporate CSR funding channels, and the unique NITI Aayog ID signals verification and reliability to donors\n\nSince you already have a Darpan ID (per your message) \u2014 good, that's step one done.\n\n**2. Domain + hosting + CMS** \u2014 no eligibility gate at all\n- Your domain (dkbv.org) is registered \u2014 fine.\n- For CMS: WordPress (self-hosted or WordPress.com) is the most practical for a trust at your stage \u2014 free core software, huge plugin ecosystem for donations, volunteer forms, blog/updates, and it's what most Indian NGOs eventually migrate content into anyway. Alternatives: Wix/Squarespace (faster to launch, less flexible) or, once you're TechSoup-verified, Google Sites/Workspace-integrated options.\n- A relevant plugin stack for WordPress: **GiveWP** or **WPForms** (donation/volunteer forms), **Razorpay/Instamojo plugins** (payment gateway), **WP Mail SMTP** (receipts by email).\n\n**3. Payment gateway for donations** \u2014 you don't need 80G to *start* collecting donations, only to make them tax-deductible for the donor\nIf your NGO doesn't have a website yet, Instamojo lets you accept payments via a payment link or smart link even without one. Razorpay Payment Pages work similarly. The catch: 80G registration isn't mandatory to collect donations, but it's what lets donors claim tax deductions, which makes donations meaningfully more attractive to give. Practically:\n- You can start collecting via Razorpay/Instamojo now, issue plain donation receipts (name, PAN, amount, date, purpose) \u2014 just not 80G-tax-deduction receipts yet.\n- Once 80G comes through, Razorpay Payment Pages can auto-generate 80G receipts and email them to donors automatically, removing manual admin work, and Razorpay/Cashfree also offer a discounted nonprofit transaction rate (~1.5\u20131.75% vs standard ~2%) once you submit your 80G/12A certificate.\n\n**4. Meta (Facebook/Instagram) for the trust**\nTwo separate things, don't conflate them:\n- A Facebook Page + Instagram Business account, Meta Business Suite, ads, and the free **Meta Blueprint** marketing courses \u2014 all usable now, no registration gate.\n- Native in-platform fundraising tools (Donate button collecting money *inside* Facebook, Instagram donation stickers, PayPal Giving Fund payouts) \u2014 Meta's own fundraising tools that let donors give directly on Facebook/Instagram are only available in the US, UK, Canada and Australia; in other countries, Meta instead lets you use tools that drive people to donate on your own website. For India, the realistic path is: get your website's donation link reviewed and approved by Meta, after which shares of that link from Facebook/Instagram may surface a Donate button and related features. So \u2014 your own donation page (Razorpay/Instamojo-powered) is actually the more important asset than any Meta-native tool.\n\n**5. Google Ad Grants, Workspace, Microsoft, Canva, TechSoup** \u2014 pre-stage now, activate once 12A/80G lands\nStart the TechSoup India registration process now (it takes time on its own), so the moment 12A/80G certificates are issued you can submit them and unlock everything in one pass, rather than starting the vendor-verification clock only after tax registration.\n\n## Legal docs / receipts / trust management (your #4, #6, #7)\n\n- **Donation receipts now (pre-80G):** trust name, PAN, address, donor name, amount, date, mode of payment, purpose \u2014 legally fine, just not tax-deductible for the donor.\n- **Trust management basics you'll need regardless of 12A/80G status**: holding an AGM, maintaining a compliance manual for trustees, filing annual ITR even with no taxable income, and getting accounts audited once gross receipts cross exemption limits.\n- **When 12A/80G do land**: keep your Darpan details updated, and issue every donor a receipt carrying the trust's name, PAN, and 80G certificate number. Renewal of 12A/80G/FCRA is only needed if you actually hold them \u2014 a plain trust without these has a comparatively lighter compliance load, but that's also exactly why funders/CSR desks discount unregistered trusts, per Darpan-benefits research above.\n- **FCRA** \u2014 separate track, needs 3 years of existence before regular FCRA registration (or Prior Permission for a specific foreign donor in the interim), plus a dedicated SBI Delhi main branch FCRA account. Given your trust's 2019 registration date (even though dormant), it's worth getting a CA to check whether that counts toward the 3-year clock \u2014 that could be materially useful for FCRA timing.\n\n## Volunteers, CMS, everything-in-one-place\n\nFor a trust at your stage, don't over-engineer this yet \u2014 a lean stack:\n- **CMS**: WordPress site (public-facing: about, programs, donate, volunteer sign-up, updates/blog)\n- **Volunteer + donor data**: a simple Google Sheet or Zoho Forms/Airtable is genuinely fine at this scale; graduate to a proper CRM (Zoho for Nonprofits, or a donor-management tool) only once volunteer/donor numbers justify it\n- **Docs/records**: Google Workspace or Google Drive for trust deed, registration certificates, minutes, receipts \u2014 apply for the free nonprofit Workspace tier once TechSoup-verified\n\n## Suggested sequence\n\n1. Darpan \u2014 done (you have it)\n2. File 12A/80G (Form 10A) \u2014 you said this is already in motion for the next 1\u20132 months\n3. In parallel: launch the WordPress site on dkbv.org, connect Razorpay/Instamojo for donations, set up Facebook/Instagram pages\n4. Start TechSoup India registration now so verification is mid-process when 12A/80G certificates arrive\n5. Once 12A/80G land: submit to TechSoup \u2192 unlock Google Workspace, Canva, Microsoft 365 \u2192 apply for Google Ad Grants \u2192 switch Razorpay/Cashfree to nonprofit-rate + auto 80G receipts\n6. File Form CSR-1 (Darpan ID already covers that prerequisite) to become CSR-fund eligible\n7. At the 3-year mark (worth checking with a CA whether 2019 origin counts) \u2014 pursue FCRA if foreign donations are a goal\n\nA few of these tracks (TechSoup verification steps, exact Form 10A document checklist, CSR-1 filing specifics) go deeper than a quick search can responsibly cover \u2014 happy to dig into any one of them in more detail, or if useful, I can pull together a fuller multi-source compliance and grants roadmap specific to trusts in your state.",

                        "text": "Good news first: even with 12A/80G/FCRA still pending, there's a lot you can set up *right now* that won't need to be redone later. Here's the landscape, mapped to your 8 requirements.\n\n## The core gating factor to understand\n\nAlmost every \"free tech/marketing for nonprofits\" program in India gates on **12A + 80G** (sometimes both, sometimes just one), verified through **TechSoup India**:\n\n- **Google Ad Grants** \u2014 up to $10,000/month in free Search ad credit \u2014 requires a registered charitable organization with a valid 12A/80G certificate and an active website with substantial content. Applied for via registering as an NGO member of NASSCOM Foundation's program, which acts as TechSoup's local partner in India for Google's verification.\n- **Google Workspace for Nonprofits** \u2014 available for NGOs registered under 12A and 80G, applied through TechSoup India, with 2\u20134 week processing.\n- **Microsoft 365 for Nonprofits** \u2014 Business Basic is free for up to 300 users for verified Indian nonprofits with 80G/12A status via Microsoft Philanthropies through TechSoup India, and Business Standard/Premium come at a steep discount.\n- **Canva for Nonprofits** \u2014 100% free Canva Pro access for registered NGOs, again gated behind TechSoup verification.\n- **TechSoup catalog broadly** (Adobe, Zoom, Slack for Charities, security tools) \u2014 same story: organizations must first be validated by TechSoup as operating on a nonprofit basis for the public benefit, then meet each vendor's individual criteria.\n\n**So the single highest-leverage move right now is pushing 12A/80G through fast** \u2014 everything downstream (Google, Microsoft, Canva, Ad Grants) unlocks off the back of that one certificate pair.\n\n## What you can do *this week*, with zero gating\n\n**1. NGO Darpan registration (do this immediately, it's free and has no minimum-age requirement)**\nA newly formed NGO can register on Darpan right away \u2014 there's no minimum age requirement, though applying for specific government schemes may require the org to be at least a year old. It's foundational because:\n- Darpan UID is mandatory for FCRA registration\n- it's required to be mentioned in your CSR-1 filing, and while general CSR-1 rules expect 3 years of track record, a newly formed trust set up specifically to carry out CSR activities is an exception\n- it's required for most government and corporate CSR funding channels, and the unique NITI Aayog ID signals verification and reliability to donors\n\nSince you already have a Darpan ID (per your message) \u2014 good, that's step one done.\n\n**2. Domain + hosting + CMS** \u2014 no eligibility gate at all\n- Your domain (dkbv.org) is registered \u2014 fine.\n- For CMS: WordPress (self-hosted or WordPress.com) is the most practical for a trust at your stage \u2014 free core software, huge plugin ecosystem for donations, volunteer forms, blog/updates, and it's what most Indian NGOs eventually migrate content into anyway. Alternatives: Wix/Squarespace (faster to launch, less flexible) or, once you're TechSoup-verified, Google Sites/Workspace-integrated options.\n- A relevant plugin stack for WordPress: **GiveWP** or **WPForms** (donation/volunteer forms), **Razorpay/Instamojo plugins** (payment gateway), **WP Mail SMTP** (receipts by email).\n\n**3. Payment gateway for donations** \u2014 you don't need 80G to *start* collecting donations, only to make them tax-deductible for the donor\nIf your NGO doesn't have a website yet, Instamojo lets you accept payments via a payment link or smart link even without one. Razorpay Payment Pages work similarly. The catch: 80G registration isn't mandatory to collect donations, but it's what lets donors claim tax deductions, which makes donations meaningfully more attractive to give. Practically:\n- You can start collecting via Razorpay/Instamojo now, issue plain donation receipts (name, PAN, amount, date, purpose) \u2014 just not 80G-tax-deduction receipts yet.\n- Once 80G comes through, Razorpay Payment Pages can auto-generate 80G receipts and email them to donors automatically, removing manual admin work, and Razorpay/Cashfree also offer a discounted nonprofit transaction rate (~1.5\u20131.75% vs standard ~2%) once you submit your 80G/12A certificate.\n\n**4. Meta (Facebook/Instagram) for the trust**\nTwo separate things, don't conflate them:\n- A Facebook Page + Instagram Business account, Meta Business Suite, ads, and the free **Meta Blueprint** marketing courses \u2014 all usable now, no registration gate.\n- Native in-platform fundraising tools (Donate button collecting money *inside* Facebook, Instagram donation stickers, PayPal Giving Fund payouts) \u2014 Meta's own fundraising tools that let donors give directly on Facebook/Instagram are only available in the US, UK, Canada and Australia; in other countries, Meta instead lets you use tools that drive people to donate on your own website. For India, the realistic path is: get your website's donation link reviewed and approved by Meta, after which shares of that link from Facebook/Instagram may surface a Donate button and related features. So \u2014 your own donation page (Razorpay/Instamojo-powered) is actually the more important asset than any Meta-native tool.\n\n**5. Google Ad Grants, Workspace, Microsoft, Canva, TechSoup** \u2014 pre-stage now, activate once 12A/80G lands\nStart the TechSoup India registration process now (it takes time on its own), so the moment 12A/80G certificates are issued you can submit them and unlock everything in one pass, rather than starting the vendor-verification clock only after tax registration.\n\n## Legal docs / receipts / trust management (your #4, #6, #7)\n\n- **Donation receipts now (pre-80G):** trust name, PAN, address, donor name, amount, date, mode of payment, purpose \u2014 legally fine, just not tax-deductible for the donor.\n- **Trust management basics you'll need regardless of 12A/80G status**: holding an AGM, maintaining a compliance manual for trustees, filing annual ITR even with no taxable income, and getting accounts audited once gross receipts cross exemption limits.\n- **When 12A/80G do land**: keep your Darpan details updated, and issue every donor a receipt carrying the trust's name, PAN, and 80G certificate number. Renewal of 12A/80G/FCRA is only needed if you actually hold them \u2014 a plain trust without these has a comparatively lighter compliance load, but that's also exactly why funders/CSR desks discount unregistered trusts, per Darpan-benefits research above.\n- **FCRA** \u2014 separate track, needs 3 years of existence before regular FCRA registration (or Prior Permission for a specific foreign donor in the interim), plus a dedicated SBI Delhi main branch FCRA account. Given your trust's 2019 registration date (even though dormant), it's worth getting a CA to check whether that counts toward the 3-year clock \u2014 that could be materially useful for FCRA timing.\n\n## Volunteers, CMS, everything-in-one-place\n\nFor a trust at your stage, don't over-engineer this yet \u2014 a lean stack:\n- **CMS**: WordPress site (public-facing: about, programs, donate, volunteer sign-up, updates/blog)\n- **Volunteer + donor data**: a simple Google Sheet or Zoho Forms/Airtable is genuinely fine at this scale; graduate to a proper CRM (Zoho for Nonprofits, or a donor-management tool) only once volunteer/donor numbers justify it\n- **Docs/records**: Google Workspace or Google Drive for trust deed, registration certificates, minutes, receipts \u2014 apply for the free nonprofit Workspace tier once TechSoup-verified\n\n## Suggested sequence\n\n1. Darpan \u2014 done (you have it)\n2. File 12A/80G (Form 10A) \u2014 you said this is already in motion for the next 1\u20132 months\n3. In parallel: launch the WordPress site on dkbv.org, connect Razorpay/Instamojo for donations, set up Facebook/Instagram pages\n4. Start TechSoup India registration now so verification is mid-process when 12A/80G certificates arrive\n5. Once 12A/80G land: submit to TechSoup \u2192 unlock Google Workspace, Canva, Microsoft 365 \u2192 apply for Google Ad Grants \u2192 switch Razorpay/Cashfree to nonprofit-rate + auto 80G receipts\n6. File Form CSR-1 (Darpan ID already covers that prerequisite) to become CSR-fund eligible\n7. At the 3-year mark (worth checking with a CA whether 2019 origin counts) \u2014 pursue FCRA if foreign donations are a goal\n\nA few of these tracks (TechSoup verification steps, exact Form 10A document checklist, CSR-1 filing specifics) go deeper than a quick search can responsibly cover \u2014 happy to dig into any one of them in more detail, or if useful, I can pull together a fuller multi-source compliance and grants roadmap specific to trusts in your state.",

            {
                "uuid": "019fc81a-47a0-75b5-9268-a8f6d4963b1c",
                "text": "Good question. For a charitable trust site, you'd typically want maybe eight to ten pages: a home page, an about us page covering your mission and story, a page for your programs or causes, a donate page, a volunteer page, a page showing your trust registration and legal transparency documents, a gallery or impact stories page, a news or blog section, a contact page, and eventually a page for annual reports once you have them.\n\nNow, to actually build this out properly, here's what I'd need from you. First, the basics: what's the full name of the trust, and what's the story behind why you started it \u2014 like the actual mission statement in your own words. Second, what specific cause or causes are you focusing on \u2014 is it education, health, poverty relief, something else, or a mix? Third, do you have any photos, logos, or branding already, or are we starting from scratch there?\n\nFourth, who are the key people \u2014 trustees, founders \u2014 and do you want their names and photos on the site, or keep it more low-key for now? And fifth, do you already have any beneficiaries or activities you've done in these last twelve to fifteen days that we could showcase, even informally?\n\nWant to go through these one at a time, or do you want to just dump all the info you have and I'll organize it?",
                "content": [
                    {
                        "start_timestamp": null,
                        "stop_timestamp": null,
                        "flags": null,
                        "type": "text",
                        "text": "Good question. First, the basics: what's the full name of the trust, and what's the story behind why you started it \u2014 like the actual mission statement in your own words. Second, what specific cause or causes are you focusing on \u2014 is it education, health, poverty relief, something else, or a mix? Third, do you have any photos, logos, or branding already, or are we starting from scratch there?\n\nFourth, who are the key people \u2014 trustees, founders \u2014 and do you want their names and photos on the site, or keep it more low-key for now?                                 "text": "     1\t---\n     2\tname: pdf-reading\n     3\tdescription: \"Use this skill when you need to read, inspect, or extract content from PDF files \u2014 especially when file content is NOT in your context and you need to read it from disk. Covers content inventory, text extraction, page rasterization for visual inspection, embedded image/attachment/table/form-field extraction, and choosing the right reading strategy for different document types (text-heavy, scanned, slide-decks, forms, data-heavy). Do NOT use this skill for PDF creation, form filling, merging, splitting, watermarking, or encryption \u2014 use the pdf skill instead.\"\n     4\tlicense: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms\n     5\t---\n     6\t\n     7\t# PDF Processing Guide\n     8\t\n     9\t## Overview\n    10\t\n    11\tThis guide covers essential PDF reading operations using Python libraries and command-line tools. For advanced features (pypdfium2 rendering, pdfplumber table settings, OCR fallback, encrypted/corrupted PDF handling), see REFERENCE.md.\n    12\t\n    13\t## Reading & Inspecting PDFs\n    14\t\n    15\tBefore doing anything with a PDF, understand what you're working with.\n    16\t\n    17\t### Content inventory\n    18\t\n    19\tRun a quick diagnostic first. For simple tasks (\"summarize this\n    20\tdocument\"), `pdfinfo` + `pdffonts` + a text sample may suffice. For\n    21\tanything involving figures, attachments, or extraction issues, run the\n    22\tfull set:\n    23\t\n    24\t```bash\n    25\t# Always: page count, file size, PDF version, metadata\n    26\tpdfinfo document.pdf\n    27\t\n    28\t# Always: does a text layer exist? No fonts \u2192 scanned/raster \u2192 see \"Scanned documents\"\n    29\tpdffonts document.pdf\n    30\t\n    31\t# If fonts are present: sample the text layer\n    32\tpdftotext -f 1 -l 1 document.pdf - | head -20\n    33\t\n    34\t# If figures/charts may matter:\n    35\tpdfimages -list document.pdf\n    36\t\n    37\t# If the PDF might contain embedded files (reports, portfolios):\n    38\tpdfdetach -list document.pdf\n    39\t```\n    40\t\n    41\tThis tells you:\n    42\t- **Page count and size** \u2014 how big is the job?\n    43\t- **Font status** \u2014 are any fonts present? An empty `pdffonts` table\n    44\t  means the PDF is scanned or raster-only: `pdftotext` will return\n    45\t  nothing, so skip straight to \"Scanned documents\" below. Fonts shown\n    46\t  as not embedded (\"emb: no\") with custom encodings may produce wrong\n    47\t  characters on extraction.\n    48\t- **Text extractability** \u2014 when fonts exist, does `pdftotext` return\n    49\t  clean text, or is it garbled (broken encoding)?\n    50\t- **Embedded raster images** \u2014 are there photos or raster figures?\n    51\t  (Note: vector-drawn charts from matplotlib/Excel won't appear \u2014 see\n    52\t  \"Extracting embedded images\" below)\n    53\t- **Attachments** \u2014 are there embedded spreadsheets, data files, etc.?\n    54\t\n    55\t### Text extraction\n    56\t\n    57\t**pypdf** for basic text:\n    58\t```python\n    59\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader\n    60\t\n    61\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n    62\tprint(f\"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}\")\n    63\t\n    64\t# Extract text\n    65\ttext = \"\"\n    66\tfor page in reader.pages:\n    67\t    text += page.extract_text()\n    68\t```\n    69\t\n    70\t**pdftotext** preserving layout (better for multi-column docs):\n    71\t```bash\n    72\t# Layout mode preserves spatial positioning\n    73\tpdftotext -layout document.pdf output.txt\n    74\t\n    75\t# Specific page range\n    76\tpdftotext -f 1 -l 5 document.pdf output.txt\n    77\t```\n    78\t\n    79\t**pdfplumber** for layout-aware extraction with positioning data:\n    80\t```python\n    81\timport pdfplumber\n    82\t\n    83\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n    84\t    for page in pdf.pages:\n    85\t        text = page.extract_text()\n    86\t        print(text)\n    87\t```\n    88\t\n    89\t### Visual inspection (rasterize pages)\n    90\t\n    91\tText extraction is **blind** to charts, diagrams, figures, equations,\n    92\tmulti-column layout, and form structures. When any of these matter,\n    93\trasterize the relevant page and Read the image:\n    94\t\n    95\t```bash\n    96\t# Rasterize a single page (page 3 here) at 150 DPI\n    97\tpdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 -f 3 -l 3 document.pdf /tmp/page\n    98\t\n    99\t# pdftoppm zero-pads the output filename based on TOTAL page count\n   100\t# (e.g., page-03.jpg for a 50-page PDF, page-003.jpg for 200+ pages)\n   101\t# Don't guess the filename \u2014 find it:\n   102\tls /tmp/page-*.jpg\n   103\t```\n   104\t\n   105\tThen Read the resulting image file. This gives you full visual\n   106\tunderstanding of that page \u2014 layout, charts, equations, everything.\n   107\t\n   108\t**When to rasterize vs. text-extract:**\n   109\t- **Content/data questions \u2192 text extraction** (cheaper, searchable)\n   110\t- **Figures, charts, visual layout \u2192 rasterize the page**\n   111\t- **Tables \u2192 try text extraction first, rasterize if garbled**\n   112\t- **Precision matters \u2192 do both** (extract text AND rasterize; use text\n   113\t  for data, image for context \u2014 this is what Claude's API does natively\n   114\t  with PDF uploads)\n   115\t\n   116\t**Token cost awareness:**\n   117\t- Text extraction: ~200\u2013400 tokens per page\n   118\t- Rasterized image: ~1,600 tokens per page (at 150 DPI)\n   119\t- Both together: ~2,000\u20132,400 tokens per page\n   120\t\n   121\tFor a 100-page PDF, rasterizing everything would consume ~160K tokens.\n   122\tOnly rasterize pages that matter for the question at hand.\n   123\t\n   124\t### Choosing your reading strategy\n   125\t\n   126\t**Text-heavy documents** (reports, articles, books):\n   127\t\u2192 Text extraction is primary. Rasterize only for specific figures or\n   128\t  pages where layout matters.\n   129\t\n   130\t**Scanned documents** (`pdffonts` shows no fonts):\n   131\t\u2192 `pdftotext` will return nothing \u2014 don't run it. Rasterize pages at\n   132\t  150 DPI and Read them visually. For bulk text extraction, use OCR\n   133\t  (pytesseract after converting pages to images \u2014 see REFERENCE.md for\n   134\t  a complete example).\n   135\t\n   136\t**Slide-deck PDFs** (exported presentations):\n   137\t\u2192 Every page is primarily visual. Rasterize individual pages on demand.\n   138\t  Text extraction gives you bullet-point text but loses all layout.\n   139\t\n   140\t**Form-heavy documents**:\n   141\t\u2192 Extract form field values programmatically first (see below). Rasterize\n   142\t  the form page for visual context if needed.\n   143\t\n   144\t**Data-heavy documents** (tables, charts, figures):\n   145\t\u2192 Use pdfplumber for tables. Rasterize pages with charts/figures.\n   146\t  Extract text for surrounding narrative. Consider both text AND image\n   147\t  for the same page when precision matters.\n   148\t\n   149\t### Extracting embedded images\n   150\t\n   151\t```bash\n   152\t# List all embedded images with metadata (size, color, compression)\n   153\tpdfimages -list document.pdf\n   154\t\n   155\t# Extract all images as PNG\n   156\tpdfimages -png document.pdf /tmp/img\n   157\t\n   158\t# Extract from specific pages only (pages 3-5)\n   159\tpdfimages -png -f 3 -l 5 document.pdf /tmp/img\n   160\t\n   161\t# Extract in original format (JPEG stays JPEG, etc.)\n   162\tpdfimages -all document.pdf /tmp/img\n   163\t```\n   164\t\n   165\tThen Read `/tmp/img-000.png` (etc.) to see each extracted image.\n   166\t\n   167\t**Gotcha \u2014 vector graphics:** `pdfimages` extracts only raster image\n   168\tdata. Charts and diagrams drawn as vector graphics (common in\n   169\tmatplotlib, Excel, and R exports) will NOT appear \u2014 they are page\n   170\tcontent operators, not image objects. For these, rasterize the whole\n   171\tpage with `pdftoppm` instead.\n   172\t\n   173\t**Gotcha \u2014 empty images:** `pdfimages` sometimes produces many tiny or\n   174\tempty image files \u2014 these are typically background masks, transparency\n   175\tlayers, or decorative elements. Filter by file size to find the real\n   176\tcontent images.\n   177\t\n   178\tProgrammatic extraction with position data:\n   179\t```python\n   180\timport fitz  # PyMuPDF\n   181\t\n   182\tdoc = fitz.open(\"document.pdf\")\n   183\tfor page in doc:\n   184\t    for img in page.get_images():\n   185\t        xref = img[0]\n   186\t        pix = fitz.Pixmap(doc, xref)\n   187\t        if pix.n - pix.alpha > 3:  # CMYK or other non-RGB\n   188\t            pix = fitz.Pixmap(fitz.csRGB, pix)\n   189\t        pix.save(f\"/tmp/img_{xref}.png\")\n   190\t```\n   191\t\n   192\t### Extracting file attachments\n   193\t\n   194\tPDFs can contain embedded files \u2014 spreadsheets, data files, other\n   195\tdocuments. Common in business reports, PDF portfolios, and PDF/A-3\n   196\tcompliance documents.\n   197\t\n   198\t```bash\n   199\t# List all attachments\n   200\tpdfdetach -list document.pdf\n   201\t\n   202\t# Extract all attachments to a directory\n   203\tmkdir -p /tmp/attachments\n   204\tpdfdetach -saveall -o /tmp/attachments/ document.pdf\n   205\t\n   206\t# Extract a specific attachment by number (1-based index from -list output)\n   207\tpdfdetach -save 1 -o /tmp/attachment.pdf document.pdf\n   208\t```\n   209\t\n   210\tIn Python:\n   211\t```python\n   212\timport os\n   213\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader\n   214\t\n   215\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n   216\tfor name, content_list in reader.attachments.items():\n   217\t    safe_name = os.path.basename(name)  # sanitize \u2014 name comes from the PDF\n   218\t    for content in content_list:\n   219\t        with open(f\"/tmp/{safe_name}\", \"wb\") as f:\n   220\t            f.write(content)\n   221\t```\n   222\t\n   223\t**Two attachment mechanisms exist in PDFs:** page-level file annotation\n   224\tattachments (shown as paperclip icons in viewers) and document-level\n   225\tembedded files (in the EmbeddedFiles name tree). Both `pdfdetach` and\n   226\tpypdf handle the common cases. Rich media assets (3D, video) embedded\n   227\tas annotations may not appear in the attachment list \u2014 use PyMuPDF to\n   228\titerate page annotations for those.\n   229\t\n   230\t### Extracting form field data\n   231\t\n   232\tPDFs with interactive forms (government forms, applications, contracts)\n   233\thave fillable fields whose values can be read programmatically:\n   234\t\n   235\t```python\n   236\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader\n   237\t\n   238\treader = PdfReader(\"form.pdf\")\n   239\t\n   240\t# Text input fields only:\n   241\tfields = reader.get_form_text_fields()\n   242\tfor name, value in fields.items():\n   243\t    print(f\"{name}: {value}\")\n   244\t\n   245\t# All field types (checkboxes, radio buttons, dropdowns too):\n   246\tall_fields = reader.get_fields() or {}\n   247\tfor name, field in all_fields.items():\n   248\t    print(f\"{name}: {field.get('/V', '')} (type: {field.get('/FT', '')})\")\n   249\t```\n   250\t\n   251\t`get_form_text_fields()` returns only text input fields. For\n   252\tgovernment forms and contracts that use checkboxes, radio buttons,\n   253\tand dropdowns, use `get_fields()` instead to see all field types.\n   254\t\n   255\tFor comprehensive field info (types, options, defaults):\n   256\t```bash\n   257\tpdftk form.pdf dump_data_fields\n   258\t```\n   259\t\n   260\tFor anything beyond reading form data \u2014 filling forms, creating forms \u2014\n   261\tuse the `pdf` skill \u2014 invoke it by name if you have a Skill tool, or\n   262\tRead its SKILL.md (listed in your available skills, or in the same\n   263\tskills directory as this file).\n   264\t\n   265\t### Audio, video, and other rare embedded content\n   266\t\n   267\tPDFs can occasionally embed audio, video, or 3D models. Check\n   268\t`pdfdetach -list` first \u2014 if the media appears as an attachment,\n   269\textract with `pdfdetach -saveall`. If not, it may be a Rich Media\n   270\tannotation (harder to extract; requires PyMuPDF to iterate page\n   271\tannotations). This is very rare in practice. Most PDF viewers outside\n   272\tAdobe Acrobat do not support media playback.\n   273\t\n   274\t### Font diagnostics\n   275\t\n   276\tIf text extraction produces garbled output (wrong characters, missing\n   277\ttext, mojibake), look back at the `pdffonts` output from the Content\n   278\tinventory. Check the \"emb\" column \u2014 fonts showing \"no\" (not embedded)\n   279\twith custom encodings mean the PDF's character mapping may be broken\n   280\tfor text extraction. In that case, rasterize the page and use vision\n   281\tinstead.\n   282\t\n   283\tAlso check encoding: fonts with \"Custom\" or \"Identity-H\" encoding\n   284\twithout embedded CIDToGID maps can cause character substitution issues\n   285\teven when the font is technically embedded.\n   286\t\n   287\t---\n   288\t\n   289\t## Quick Reference\n   290\t\n   291\t| Task | Best Tool | Command/Code |\n   292\t|------|-----------|--------------|\n   293\t| Inspect PDF | poppler-utils | `pdfinfo`, `pdfimages -list`, `pdfdetach -list`, `pdffonts` |\n   294\t| Extract text | pdfplumber | `page.extract_text()` |\n   295\t| Extract text (CLI) | pdftotext | `pdftotext -layout input.pdf output.txt` |\n   296\t| Extract tables | pdfplumber | `page.extract_tables()` |\n   297\t| See page visually | pdftoppm | `pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 -f N -l N` |\n   298\t| Extract images | pdfimages | `pdfimages -png input.pdf prefix` |\n   299\t| Extract attachments | pdfdetach | `pdfdetach -saveall -o /tmp/` |\n   300\t| Read form fields | pypdf | `reader.get_fields()` |\n   301\t| OCR scanned PDFs | pytesseract | Convert to image first |\n   302\t\n   303\t## PDF Form Filling, Creation, Merging, Splitting, and Other Operations\n   304\t\n   305\tThis skill covers **reading and inspection** only. For filling forms,\n   306\tcreating, merging, splitting, rotating, watermarking, encrypting, or\n   307\tother PDF manipulation tasks, use the `pdf` skill (find its SKILL.md\n   308\tlocation in your available skills).\n   309\t",
                                "uuid": "a58bb062-b165-4a77-b4f5-24f78734aad1"
                            }

                                "text": "     1\t---\n     2\tname: docx\n     3\tdescription: \"Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.\"\n     4\tlicense: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms\n     5\t---\n     6\t\n     7\t# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis\n     8\t\n     9\tA `.docx` is a ZIP archive of XML files. Choose your approach by task:\n    10\t\n    11\t| Task | Approach |\n    12\t|---|---|\n    13\t| **Create** a new document | Write a `docx` (npm) script \u2014 see gotchas below |\n    14\t| **Edit** an existing document | `unzip` \u2192 edit `word/document.xml` \u2192 `zip` (docx-js cannot open existing files) |\n    15\t| **Read** content | `pandoc -t markdown file.docx` |\n    16\t\n    17\t> Script paths below are relative to this skill's directory.\n    18\t\n    19\t## Creating with docx-js \u2014 gotchas\n    20\t\n    21\t`docx` is preinstalled \u2014 do not run `npm install` first; write the script and `require('docx')` directly. Only if that require fails: `npm install docx`. The model knows the API; these are the footguns:\n    22\t\n    23\t- **Page size defaults to A4.** For US Letter set `page: { size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 } }` (DXA; 1440 = 1\u2033).\n    24\t- **Landscape:** pass portrait dimensions and `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE` \u2014 docx-js swaps width/height internally.\n    25\t- **Tables need dual widths:** set `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on every cell, both in `WidthType.DXA` (PERCENTAGE breaks in Google Docs). Column widths must sum to the table width.\n    26\t- **Table shading:** use `ShadingType.CLEAR`, never `SOLID` (renders black).\n    27\t- **Lists:** never insert `\u2022` literally; use a `numbering` config with `LevelFormat.BULLET`.\n    28\t- **`ImageRun` requires `type:`** (`\"png\"`, `\"jpg\"`, \u2026).\n    29\t- **`PageBreak` must be inside a `Paragraph`.**\n    30\t- **Never use `\\n`** \u2014 use separate `Paragraph` elements.\n    31\t- **TOC:** headings must use built-in `HeadingLevel.*`; custom heading styles need `outlineLevel` set or they won't appear.\n    32\t- **Don't use a table as a horizontal rule** \u2014 use a paragraph bottom border instead.\n    33\t- **Dot-leader / right-aligned-on-same-line:** use `PositionalTab` (`alignment: PositionalTabAlignment.RIGHT`, `leader: PositionalTabLeader.DOT`) inside a `TextRun`, not literal `.` or space padding.\n    34\t\n    35\t## Verify the output\n    36\t\n    37\tAfter writing a `.docx`, render it and look at it:\n    38\t\n    39\t```bash\n    40\tpython scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf output.docx\n    41\tpdftoppm -jpeg -r 100 output.pdf page\n    42\tls page-*.jpg   # then Read the images\n    43\t```\n    44\t\n    45\t`pdftoppm` zero-pads page numbers to the width of the page count (`page-01.jpg`\u2026`page-12.jpg`).\n    46\t\n    47\t## Editing existing documents\n    48\t\n    49\tLegacy `.doc` files must be converted first: `python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx file.doc`.\n    50\t\n    51\t```bash\n    52\tunzip -q doc.docx -d unpacked/\n    53\tfind unpacked -type l -delete   # strip symlink entries \u2014 docx from external parties is untrusted\n    54\tpython scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/   # coalesce fragmented runs so text is findable\n    55\t# edit unpacked/word/document.xml in place \u2014 do NOT reformat or pretty-print\n    56\t(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.docx && zip -Xr ../out.docx .)\n    57\tpython scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original doc.docx   # XSD checks; --auto-repair fixes common issues\n    58\t# redlining? add --author \"<the name you redlined under>\" to check every edit is tracked\n    59\t```\n    60\t\n    61\tWord splits text across many `<w:r>` runs (revision ids, spell-check markers), so a phrase you can see in the document often doesn't exist as a contiguous string in the XML. `merge_runs.py` merges adjacent identically-formatted runs in `word/document.xml` without changing content or rendering; it also accepts a `.docx` directly (`python scripts/merge_runs.py doc.docx -o merged.docx`).\n    62\t\n    63\t**Tracked changes:** when redlining, validate with `--author \"<the name you redlined under>\"` (needs `--original`) \u2014 it reports any text you changed without a `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` around it, which is easy to do by accident and invisible in the accepted view. Wrap runs in `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` with `w:id`, `w:author`, `w:date` attributes. Inside `<w:del>`, the text element is `<w:delText>`, not `<w:t>`. A deleted paragraph mark (`<w:pPr><w:rPr><w:del w:id=\"..\" w:author=\"..\" w:date=\"..\"/></w:rPr></w:pPr>`) means \"merge this paragraph into the next\" \u2014 so deleting a paragraph outright is that plus a `<w:del>` around every run. The `<w:del/>` must come before the rPr's other children; their order is schema-enforced.\n    64\t\n    65\tTo produce a clean copy with all tracked changes accepted: `python scripts/accept_changes.py in.docx out.docx`.\n    66\t\n    67\tAccepting a deleted paragraph mark should join that paragraph to the one below it, so a paragraph whose runs are *all* deleted vanishes. Word does this; `accept_changes.py` and `pandoc --track-changes=accept` don't always. Both fail the same way \u2014 they strip the deleted text but leave the emptied paragraph behind, which reads as a stray empty bullet when it was auto-numbered:\n    68\t\n    69\t- `pandoc --track-changes=accept` never joins the paragraphs.\n    70\t- `accept_changes.py` (LibreOffice) joins them correctly, except when the deleted paragraph is followed by an empty spacer paragraph.\n    71\t\n    72\tAn empty bullet in either view is an artifact of that view, not a defect in the document. Check paragraph deletions in the XML.\n    73\t\n    74\t## Comments\n    75\t\n    76\tComments require six cross-linked files. Use the helper \u2014 directory mode when you'll also be editing `document.xml` (saves an unzip/rezip cycle), `.docx`-direct mode otherwise:\n    77\t\n    78\t```bash\n    79\t# Against an already-unpacked directory (preferred when also placing markers)\n    80\tpython scripts/comment.py unpacked/ \"Fees & expenses cap is too low\"\n    81\tpython scripts/comment.py unpacked/ \"Agreed\" --parent 0\n    82\t\n    83\t# Against a .docx directly\n    84\tpython scripts/comment.py contract.docx \"This cap is too low\" -o annotated.docx\n    85\t```\n    86\t\n    87\tThe script writes `comments.xml`, `commentsExtended.xml`, `commentsIds.xml`, `commentsExtensible.xml`, the relationships, and the content-type overrides. Comment IDs are auto-assigned. It then prints the `<w:commentRangeStart>`/`<w:commentRangeEnd>`/`<w:commentReference>` snippet to add to `word/document.xml` so the comment anchors to specific text \u2014 until you place those markers, the comment exists but is not visible.\n    88\t\n    89\t## Dependencies\n    90\t\n    91\t`docx` (npm, preinstalled \u2014 install only if `require('docx')` fails) \u00b7 `pandoc` \u00b7 LibreOffice (`soffice`) \u00b7 `pdftoppm` (Poppler)\n    92\t",

                            }

false : false })] })]\n      }),\n      new TableCell({\n        width: { size: COL_WIDTHS[2], type: WidthType.DXA },\n        children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun({ text: blankNote || \"\", size: 20, color: \"808080\", italics: true })] })]\n      })\n    ]\n  });\n}\n\nfunction sectionHeading(num, title) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1,\n    spacing: { before: 400, after: 150 },\n    children: [new TextRun({ text: `${num}. ${title}` })]\n  });\n}\n\nfunction sectionTable(rows) {\n  return new Table({\n    width: { size: TABLE_WIDTH, type: WidthType.DXA },\n    columnWidths: COL_WIDTHS,\n    rows: [headerRow(), ...rows]\n  });\n}\n\nfunction note(text) {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    spacing: { before: 100, after: 200 },\n    children: [new TextRun({ text, italics: true, size: 18, color: \"555555\" })]\n  });\n}\n\nconst doc = new Document({\n  sections: [{\n    properties: {\n      page: { size: { width: 11906, height: 16838 } } // A4\n    },\n    children: [\n      new Paragraph({\n        heading: HeadingLevel.TITLE,\n        children: [new TextRun({ text: \"DKBV Charitable Trust \u2014 Website Blueprint Questionnaire\" })]\n      }),\n      new Paragraph({\n        spacing: { before: 100, after: 100 },\n        children: [new TextRun({ text: \"Prepared to plan the complete structure and content of dkbv.org\", italics: true, size: 22 })]\n      }),\n      new Paragraph({\n        spacing: { after: 300 },\n        children: [new TextRun({\n          text: \"I reviewed all the documents currently in your project (Trust Deed, Trust Registration Form, Anusuchi/Schedule, Vakilatnama, Sogandnama/Affidavit, Sammati Patra, PAN card, and the affidavit draft).                         "flags": null,
                        "type": "text",
                        "text": "I went through everything in the project \u2014 the Trust Deed, Registration Form, Anusuchi, Vakilatnama, Sogandnama, Sammati Patra, PAN card, and the affidavit draft.\n\nOne honest flag: several of these are handwritten/stamp-paper scans in Gujarati, so I did **not** guess at things like exact trustee names, the precise registration number, or the registered address just to fill a cell \u2014 where I couldn't read something with confidence, the document says so plainly and asks you to confirm, rather than me inventing a plausible-sounding answer. What I could pick up (PAN AAZTS5070P, your 2019 registration + recent restart, the domain, Darpan status) is filled in as \"found.\"\n\nThe doc has 10 sections \u2014 legal identity, story/mission, programs, trustees, branding, donations, volunteers, legal/transparency, contact, and a proposed page structure at the end \u2014 each as a 3-column table: Question \u2192 What I found \u2192 Your answer.\n\nFill in column 3 (in the file, or just reply to me with the answers) and I'll turn it straight into the full page-by-page website blueprint.",
                        "citations": []
                    }

            {

                "text": "I answered all the questions into the file itself, do let me know if there's anything else that I need to provide.",

            {

                        "text": "Here's what I found.\n\n## Darpan ID \u2014 which one is real\n\nThe confirmed official format (per NITI Aayog's own documentation) is:\n\n**State Code / Year / 7-digit unique number** \u2014 e.g. `RJ/2024/1234567` for Rajasthan.\n\nYour `GJ/2026/1044195` matches this exactly \u2014 **GJ is Gujarat's state code**, 2026 is the year you registered on the portal, and 1044195 is your unique 7-digit serial. So yes, your instinct is right: **that's the actual Darpan Unique ID.**\n\nThe other one, `64/2026/1044195`, shares the same year and same 7-digit serial, just with \"64\" instead of \"GJ\" \u2014 that strongly suggests it's a different field from the same certificate (Darpan certificates also show a **sector code** \u2014 the numeric category you selected, like health/education/social welfare \u2014 which can look similar), not a competing version of your ID. It's not the number banks, CSR desks, or grant portals will ask for.\n\n**To be 100% sure before it goes on the website**: log into ngodarpan.gov.in with your credentials and check the field explicitly labeled \"Unique ID\" at the top of your certificate \u2014 that's the one to publish. I'd rather you confirm it directly from the source than take my inference as final, since this number will sit on a public legal page.\n\n## What \"1448\" actually is\n\nThis is **not a CIN** \u2014 CIN (Corporate Identification Number) is a 21-character alphanumeric code that only applies to companies registered under the Companies Act with the MCA (e.g., `L01631KA2010PTC096843`). Trusts don't get one. The affidavit template just uses lazy generic wording (\"registration no./incorporation no./CIN\") to mean \"whatever number your registering authority gave you\" \u2014 it wasn't written trust-specific.\n\nSince your affidavit itself says the trust was founded/settled/incorporated under The Public Trust Act, 1950 \u2014 **1448 is almost certainly your Trust Registration Number**, issued by the Charity Commissioner/Sub-Registrar of Public Trusts for Devbhumi Dwarka district under the Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950 (Gujarat still uses this Act). These numbers are typically short, sequential, and often carry a letter prefix specific to that registry \u2014 commonly shown as something like \"Regd. No. E-1448\" or \"F-1448\" rather than a bare number.\n\n**One thing worth checking**: your original **Trust Registration Certificate** (a separate document from the Trust Deed \u2014 it's the certificate the Sub-Registrar's office issues after registering the deed) will have this exact number printed on it, likely with a prefix letter.                         "type": "text",
                        "text": "This pulls together everything confirmed so far into a build-ready document:\n\n- **Section 1** \u2014 a legal/reference table (name, PAN, registration no., Darpan ID, registered office, etc.) as the single source of truth for the footer, legal page, and receipts\n- **Section 2\u20134** \u2014 sitemap (9 pages), tech stack (WordPress + WPForms now, Razorpay later), and design notes matching your minimal/fast-loading preference\n- **Section 5** \u2014 page-by-page blueprint with actual draft copy for Home, About, Wheelchair Program, Donate, Volunteer, Legal & Transparency, Gallery, Updates, and Contact \u2014 including suggested volunteer form fields and 3 tagline options to pick from\n- **Section 6** \u2014 a 3-phase rollout: what goes live now, what activates once 12A/80G land, what waits for the 3-year/FCRA mark\n- **Section 7** \u2014 a short open-items list (registration number prefix, Darpan ID final verification, logo swap-in, founder's story, first activity photos)\n\nThe \"About Us\" story section is intentionally left as a placeholder \u2014 that one really does need your own words, everything else is draft-ready.\n\nNext step is your call: I can build this out as an actual working prototype (HTML/React, viewable right away), or leave it as this document for your developer/designer to work from directly.",

                        "text": "Short answer: the first version was donor-friendly, but not yet SEO- or Ad-Grants-ready. I checked it against Google's current (2026) Ad Grants website policy and standard nonprofit SEO practice, and closed the gaps \u2014 here's what changed:\n\n**Real problems it had, now fixed:**\n- **No Privacy Policy or FAQ page** \u2014 both are checklist items Ad Grants reviewers specifically look for; their absence is one of the most common rejection reasons. Added both (now 11 pages).\n- **Wheelchair deposit wording was a genuine risk** \u2014 \"borrow, return, small deposit\" reads close to a rental transaction, which Ad Grants policy flags as commercial activity. Rewritten as a \"refundable security deposit, returned in full\" \u2014 same real-world process, worded so it's unambiguously non-commercial.\n- **Donate page had no \"how funds are used\" statement** \u2014 just a phone number. Added one line (\"100% of donations currently go toward wheelchairs\"); both Ad Grants reviewers and donors specifically look for this.\n- **No SSL/sitemap/Search Console/structured data** in the tech stack \u2014 added all of these as explicit build requirements, not afterthoughts.\n\n**New Section 6 \u2014 SEO & Google Ad Grants Readiness** now covers:\n- A requirement-by-requirement table showing exactly where this blueprint stands against Google's real 2026 Ad Grants checklist (12A/80G, HTTPS, no broken links, conversion tracking, CTR/keyword rules for later)\n- Title tags + meta descriptions drafted for every major page (Home, About, Programs, Donate, FAQ)\n- Local SEO plan \u2014 since the program is Surat-only, a free Google Business Profile will likely outperform ads early on\n- Keyword direction: specific local phrases (\"free wheelchair Surat\") instead of the generic single-word terms (\"charity,\" \"donate\") that Google's 2026 policy restricts anyway\n- First blog post topics for the Updates page, since a live blog is one of the clearest \"active, legitimate site\" signals to both search and Ad Grants review\n\nOne honest note: none of this gets you Ad Grants *approval* by itself \u2014 that still needs the 12A/80G certificates first. What it does is make sure the site won't get rejected on a technicality once you do apply, and gives it a real shot at organic search traffic in the meantime.",

                                "text": "Software Alternatives, Accelerators & Startups\n\nVite VS Next.js\n\nCompare Vite VS Next.js and see what are their differences\n\nVite logo Vite\n\nNext Generation Frontend Tooling\n\nNext.js logo Next.js\n\nA small framework for server-rendered universal JavaScript apps\n  \u2022 Vite Landing page\n    Landing page //\n    2023-09-17\n  \u2022 Next.js Landing page\n    Landing page //\n    2023-06-19\n\nVite features and specs\n\n  \u2022 Fast Development Server\n    Vite uses native ES Modules and leverages browser support for them, which allows for an extremely fast development startup time.\n  \u2022 Hot Module Replacement (HMR)\n    Vite supports fast Hot Module Replacement (HMR), which allows developers to see changes almost instantly without reloading the entire application.\n  \u2022 Optimized Build\n    Vite has a built-in build command that bundles your code with Rollup, providing out-of-the-box optimizations for production.\n  \u2022 Plugin Ecosystem\n\n\n  \u2022 Next.js is a popular React framework known for its server-side rendering, static site generation, and API route features. If you need to fill out a PDF form, read FORMS.md and follow its instructions.\n    12\t\n    13\t## Quick Start\n    14\t\n    15\t```python\n    16\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter\n    17\t\n    18\t# Read a PDF\n    19\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n    20\tprint(f\"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}\")\n    21\t\n    22\t# Extract text\n    23\ttext = \"\"\n    24\tfor page in reader.pages:\n    25\t    text += page.extract_text()\n    26\t```\n    27\t\n    28\t## Python Libraries\n    29\t\n    30\t### pypdf - Basic Operations\n    31\t\n    32\t#### Merge PDFs\n    33\t```python\n    34\tfrom pypdf import PdfWriter, PdfReader\n    35\t\n    36\twriter = PdfWriter()\n    37\tfor pdf_file in [\"doc1.pdf\", \"doc2.pdf\", \"doc3.pdf\"]:\n    38\t    reader = PdfReader(pdf_file)\n    39\t    for page in reader.pages:\n    40\t        writer.add_page(page)\n    41\t\n    42\twith open(\"merged.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n    43\t    writer.write(output)\n    44\t```\n    45\t\n    46\t#### Split PDF\n    47\t```python\n    48\treader = PdfReader(\"input.pdf\")\n    49\tfor i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):\n    50\t    writer = PdfWriter()\n    51\t    writer.add_page(page)\n    52\t    with open(f\"page_{i+1}.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n    53\t        writer.write(output)\n    54\t```\n    55\t\n    56\t#### Extract Metadata\n    57\t```python\n    58\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n    59\tmeta = reader.metadata\n    60\tprint(f\"Title: {meta.title}\")\n    61\tprint(f\"Author: {meta.author}\")\n    62\tprint(f\"Subject: {meta.subject}\")\n    63\tprint(f\"Creator: {meta.creator}\")\n    64\t```\n    65\t\n    66\t#### Rotate Pages\n    67\t```python\n    68\treader = PdfReader(\"input.pdf\")\n    69\twriter = PdfWriter()\n    70\t\n    71\tpage = reader.pages[0]\n    72\tpage.rotate(90)  # Rotate 90 degrees clockwise\n    73\twriter.add_page(page)\n    74\t\n    75\twith open(\"rotated.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n    76\t    writer.write(output)\n    77\t```\n    78\t\n    79\t### pdfplumber - Text and Table Extraction\n    80\t\n    81\t#### Extract Text with Layout\n    82\t```python\n    83\timport pdfplumber\n    84\t\n    85\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n    86\t    for page in pdf.pages:\n    87\t        text = page.extract_text()\n    88\t        print(text)\n    89\t```\n    90\t\n    91\t#### Extract Tables\n    92\t```python\n    93\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n    94\t    for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):\n    95\t        tables = page.extract_tables()\n    96\t        for j, table in enumerate(tables):\n    97\t            print(f\"Table {j+1} on page {i+1}:\")\n    98\t            for row in table:\n    99\t                print(row)\n   100\t```\n   101\t\n   102\t#### Advanced Table Extraction\n   103\t```python\n   104\timport pandas as pd\n   105\t\n   106\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n   107\t    all_tables = []\n   108\t    for page in pdf.pages:\n   109\t        tables = page.extract_tables()\n   110\t        for table in tables:\n   111\t            if table:  # Check if table is not empty\n   112\t                df = pd.DataFrame(table[1:], columns=table[0])\n   113\t                all_tables.append(df)\n   114\t\n   115\t# Combine all tables\n   116\tif all_tables:\n   117\t    combined_df = pd.concat(all_tables, ignore_index=True)\n   118\t    combined_df.to_excel(\"extracted_tables.xlsx\", index=False)\n   119\t```\n   120\t\n   121\t### reportlab - Create PDFs\n   122\t\n   123\t#### Basic PDF Creation\n   124\t```python\n   125\tfrom reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter\n   126\tfrom reportlab.pdfgen import canvas\n   127\t\n   128\tc = canvas.Canvas(\"hello.pdf\", pagesize=letter)\n   129\twidth, height = letter\n   130\t\n   131\t# Add text\n   132\tc.drawString(100, height - 100, \"Hello World!\")\n   133\tc.drawString(100, height - 120, \"This is a PDF created with reportlab\")\n   134\t\n   135\t# Add a line\n   136\tc.line(100, height - 140, 400, height - 140)\n   137\t\n   138\t# Save\n   139\tc.save()\n   140\t```\n   141\t\n   142\t#### Create PDF with Multiple Pages\n   143\t```python\n   144\tfrom reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter\n   145\tfrom reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak\n   146\tfrom reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet\n   147\t\n   148\tdoc = SimpleDocTemplate(\"report.pdf\", pagesize=letter)\n   149\tstyles = getSampleStyleSheet()\n   150\tstory = []\n   151\t\n   152\t# Add content\n   153\ttitle = Paragraph(\"Report Title\", styles['Title'])\n   154\tstory.append(title)\n   155\tstory.append(Spacer(1, 12))\n   156\t\n   157\tbody = Paragraph(\"This is the body of the report. \" * 20, styles['Normal'])\n   158\tstory.append(body)\n   159\tstory.append(PageBreak())\n   160\t\n   161\t# Page 2\n   162\tstory.append(Paragraph(\"Page 2\", styles['Heading1']))\n   163\tstory.append(Paragraph(\"Content for page 2\", styles['Normal']))\n   164\t\n   165\t# Build PDF\n   166\tdoc.build(story)\n   167\t```\n   168\t\n   169\t#### Subscripts and Superscripts\n   170\t\n   171\t**IMPORTANT**: Never use Unicode subscript/superscript characters (\u2080\u2081\u2082\u2083\u2084\u2085\u2086\u2087\u2088\u2089, \u2070\u00b9\u00b2\u00b3\u2074\u2075\u2076\u2077\u2078\u2079) in ReportLab PDFs. The built-in fonts do not include these glyphs, causing them to render as solid black boxes.\n   172\t\n   173\tInstead, use ReportLab's XML markup tags in Paragraph objects:\n   174\t```python\n   175\tfrom reportlab.platypus import Paragraph\n   176\tfrom reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet\n   177\t\n   178\tstyles = getSampleStyleSheet()\n   179\t\n   180\t# Subscripts: use <sub> tag\n   181\tchemical = Paragraph(\"H<sub>2</sub>O\", styles['Normal'])\n   182\t\n   183\t# Superscripts: use <super> tag\n   184\tsquared = Paragraph(\"x<super>2</super> + y<super>2</super>\", styles['Normal'])\n   185\t```\n   186\t\n   187\tFor canvas-drawn text (not Paragraph objects), manually adjust font the size and position rather than using Unicode subscripts/superscripts.\n   188\t\n   189\t## Command-Line Tools\n   190\t\n   191\t### pdftotext (poppler-utils)\n   192\t```bash\n   193\t# Extract text\n   194\tpdftotext input.pdf output.txt\n   195\t\n   196\t# Extract text preserving layout\n   197\tpdftotext -layout input.pdf output.txt\n   198\t\n   199\t# Extract specific pages\n   200\tpdftotext -f 1 -l 5 input.pdf output.txt  # Pages 1-5\n   201\t```\n   202\t\n                                 "text": "     1\t---\n     2\tname: pdf\n     3\tdescription: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.\n     4\tlicense: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms\n     5\t---\n     6\t\n     7\t# PDF Processing Guide\n     8\t\n     9\t## Overview\n    10\t\n    11\tThis guide covers essential PDF processing operations using Python libraries and command-line tools. For advanced features, JavaScript libraries, and detailed examples, see REFERENCE.md. If you need to fill out a PDF form, read FORMS.md and follow its instructions.\n    12\t\n    13\t## Quick Start\n    14\t\n    15\t```python\n    16\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter\n    17\t\n    18\t# Read a PDF\n    19\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n    20\tprint(f\"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}\")\n    21\t\n    22\t# Extract text\n    23\ttext = \"\"\n    24\tfor page in reader.pages:\n    25\t    text += page.extract_text()\n    26\t```\n    27\t\n    28\t## Python Libraries\n    29\t\n    30\t### pypdf - Basic Operations\n    31\t\n    32\t#### Merge PDFs\n    33\t```python\n    34\tfrom pypdf import PdfWriter, PdfReader\n    35\t\n    36\twriter = PdfWriter()\n    37\tfor pdf_file in [\"doc1.pdf\", \"doc2.pdf\", \"doc3.pdf\"]:\n    38\t    reader = PdfReader(pdf_file)\n    39\t    for page in reader.pages:\n    40\t        writer.add_page(page)\n    41\t\n    42\twith open(\"merged.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n    43\t    writer.write(output)\n    44\t```\n    45\t\n    46\t#### Split PDF\n    47\t```python\n    48\treader = PdfReader(\"input.pdf\")\n    49\tfor i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):\n    50\t    writer = PdfWriter()\n    51\t    writer.add_page(page)\n    52\t    with open(f\"page_{i+1}.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n    53\t        writer.write(output)\n    54\t```\n    55\t\n    56\t#### Extract Metadata\n    57\t```python\n    58\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n    59\tmeta = reader.metadata\n    60\tprint(f\"Title: {meta.title}\")\n    61\tprint(f\"Author: {meta.author}\")\n    62\tprint(f\"Subject: {meta.subject}\")\n    63\tprint(f\"Creator: {meta.creator}\")\n    64\t```\n    65\t\n    66\t#### Rotate Pages\n    67\t```python\n    68\treader = PdfReader(\"input.pdf\")\n    69\twriter = PdfWriter()\n    70\t\n    71\tpage = reader.pages[0]\n    72\tpage.rotate(90)  # Rotate 90 degrees clockwise\n    73\twriter.add_page(page)\n    74\t\n    75\twith open(\"rotated.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n    76\t    writer.write(output)\n    77\t```\n    78\t\n    79\t### pdfplumber - Text and Table Extraction\n    80\t\n    81\t#### Extract Text with Layout\n    82\t```python\n    83\timport pdfplumber\n    84\t\n    85\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n    86\t    for page in pdf.pages:\n    87\t        text = page.extract_text()\n    88\t        print(text)\n    89\t```\n    90\t\n    91\t#### Extract Tables\n    92\t```python\n    93\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n    94\t    for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):\n    95\t        tables = page.extract_tables()\n    96\t        for j, table in enumerate(tables):\n    97\t            print(f\"Table {j+1} on page {i+1}:\")\n    98\t            for row in table:\n    99\t                print(row)\n   100\t```\n   101\t\n   102\t#### Advanced Table Extraction\n   103\t```python\n   104\timport pandas as pd\n   105\t\n   106\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n   107\t    all_tables = []\n   108\t    for page in pdf.pages:\n   109\t        tables = page.extract_tables()\n   110\t        for table in tables:\n   111\t            if table:  # Check if table is not empty\n   112\t                df = pd.DataFrame(table[1:], columns=table[0])\n   113\t                all_tables.append(df)\n   114\t\n   115\t# Combine all tables\n   116\tif all_tables:\n   117\t    combined_df = pd.concat(all_tables, ignore_index=True)\n   118\t    combined_df.to_excel(\"extracted_tables.xlsx\", index=False)\n   119\t```\n   120\t\n   121\t### reportlab - Create PDFs\n   122\t\n   123\t#### Basic PDF Creation\n   124\t```python\n   125\tfrom reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter\n   126\tfrom reportlab.pdfgen import canvas\n   127\t\n   128\tc = canvas.Canvas(\"hello.pdf\", pagesize=letter)\n   129\twidth, height = letter\n   130\t\n   131\t# Add text\n   132\tc.drawString(100, height - 100, \"Hello World!\")\n   133\tc.drawString(100, height - 120, \"This is a PDF created with reportlab\")\n   134\t\n   135\t# Add a line\n   136\tc.line(100, height - 140, 400, height - 140)\n   137\t\n   138\t# Save\n   139\tc.save()\n   140\t```\n   141\t\n   142\t#### Create PDF with Multiple Pages\n   143\t```python\n   144\tfrom reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter\n   145\tfrom reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak\n   146\tfrom reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet\n   147\t\n   148\tdoc = SimpleDocTemplate(\"report.pdf\", pagesize=letter)\n   149\tstyles = getSampleStyleSheet()\n   150\tstory = []\n   151\t\n   152\t# Add content\n   153\ttitle = Paragraph(\"Report Title\", styles['Title'])\n   154\tstory.append(title)\n   155\tstory.append(Spacer(1, 12))\n   156\t\n   157\tbody = Paragraph(\"This is the body of the report. \" * 20, styles['Normal'])\n   158\tstory.append(body)\n   159\tstory.append(PageBreak())\n   160\t\n   161\t# Page 2\n   162\tstory.append(Paragraph(\"Page 2\", styles['Heading1']))\n   163\tstory.append(Paragraph(\"Content for page 2\", styles['Normal']))\n   164\t\n   165\t# Build PDF\n   166\tdoc.build(story)\n   167\t```\n   168\t\n   169\t#### Subscripts and Superscripts\n   170\t\n   171\t**IMPORTANT**: Never use Unicode subscript/superscript characters (\u2080\u2081\u2082\u2083\u2084\u2085\u2086\u2087\u2088\u2089, \u2070\u00b9\u00b2\u00b3\u2074\u2075\u2076\u2077\u2078\u2079) in ReportLab PDFs. The built-in fonts do not include these glyphs, causing them to render as solid black boxes.\n   172\t\n   173\tInstead, use ReportLab's XML markup tags in Paragraph objects:\n   174\t```python\n   175\tfrom reportlab.platypus import Paragraph\n   176\tfrom reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet\n   177\t\n   178\tstyles = getSampleStyleSheet()\n   179\t\n   180\t# Subscripts: use <sub> tag\n   181\tchemical = Paragraph(\"H<sub>2</sub>O\", styles['Normal'])\n   182\t\n   183\t# Superscripts: use <super> tag\n   184\tsquared = Paragraph(\"x<super>2</super> + y<super>2</super>\", styles['Normal'])\n   185\t```\n   186\t\n   187\tFor canvas-drawn text (not Paragraph objects), manually adjust font the size and position rather than using Unicode subscripts/superscripts.\n   188\t\n   189\t## Command-Line Tools\n   190\t\n   191\t### pdftotext (poppler-utils)\n   192\t```bash\n   193\t# Extract text\n   194\tpdftotext input.pdf output.txt\n   195\t\n   196\t# Extract text preserving layout\n   197\tpdftotext -layout input.pdf output.txt\n   198\t\n   199\t# Extract specific pages\n   200\tpdftotext -f 1 -l 5 input.pdf output.txt  # Pages 1-5\n   201\t```\n   202\t\n   203\t### qpdf\n   204\t```bash\n   205\t# Merge PDFs\n   206\tqpdf --empty --pages file1.pdf file2.pdf -- merged.pdf\n   207\t\n   208\t# Split pages\n   209\tqpdf input.pdf --pages . 1-5 -- pages1-5.pdf\n   210\tqpdf input.pdf --pages . 6-10 -- pages6-10.pdf\n   211\t\n   212\t# Rotate pages\n   213\tqpdf input.pdf output.pdf --rotate=+90:1  # Rotate page 1 by 90 degrees\n   214\t\n   215\t# Remove password\n   216\tqpdf --password=mypassword --decrypt encrypted.pdf decrypted.pdf\n   217\t```\n   218\t\n   219\t### pdftk (if available)\n   220\t```bash\n   221\t# Merge\n   222\tpdftk file1.pdf file2.pdf cat output merged.pdf\n   223\t\n   224\t# Split\n   225\tpdftk input.pdf burst\n   226\t\n   227\t# Rotate\n   228\tpdftk input.pdf rotate 1east output rotated.pdf\n   229\t```\n   230\t\n   231\t## Common Tasks\n   232\t\n   233\t### Extract Text from Scanned PDFs\n   234\t```python\n   235\t# Requires: pip install pytesseract pdf2image\n   236\timport pytesseract\n   237\tfrom pdf2image import convert_from_path\n   238\t\n   239\t# Convert PDF to images\n   240\timages = convert_from_path('scanned.pdf')\n   241\t\n   242\t# OCR each page\n   243\ttext = \"\"\n   244\tfor i, image in enumerate(images):\n   245\t    text += f\"Page {i+1}:\\n\"\n   246\t    text += pytesseract.image_to_string(image)\n   247\t    text += \"\\n\\n\"\n   248\t\n   249\tprint(text)\n   250\t```\n   251\t\n   252\t### Add Watermark\n   253\t```python\n   254\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter\n   255\t\n   256\t# Create watermark (or load existing)\n   257\twatermark = PdfReader(\"watermark.pdf\").pages[0]\n   258\t\n   259\t# Apply to all pages\n   260\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n   261\twriter = PdfWriter()\n   262\t\n   263\tfor page in reader.pages:\n   264\t    page.merge_page(watermark)\n   265\t    writer.add_page(page)\n   266\t\n   267\twith open(\"watermarked.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n   268\t    writer.write(output)\n   269\t```\n   270\t\n   271\t### Extract Images\n   272\t```bash\n   273\t# Using pdfimages (poppler-utils)\n   274\tpdfimages -j input.pdf output_prefix\n   275\t\n   276\t# This extracts all images as output_prefix-000.jpg, output_prefix-001.jpg, etc.\n   277\t```\n   278\t\n   279\t### Password Protection\n   280\t```python\n   281\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader, row_h\n\n# ---------- FOOTER ----------\nc.setFillColor(colors.HexColor(\"#888888\"))\nc.setFont(\"Helvetica-Oblique\", 7)\nc.drawString(8*mm, 6*mm, \"* Train 22951 stops at Wankaner Jn (~38 km from  (\"19217\", \"Saurashtra Janta Express\", \"17:40\", \"03:23\", \"9h 43m\", \"Mail/Express\"),\n    (\"19577\", \"Tirunelveli - Jamnagar Express (TEN JAM)\", \"18:26\", \"02:41\", \"8h 15m\",
