                                "text": "     1\t---\n     2\tname: docx\n     3\tdescription: \"Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.\"\n     4\tlicense: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms\n     5\t---\n     6\t\n     7\t# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis\n     8\t\n     9\tA `.docx` is a ZIP archive of XML files. Choose your approach by task:\n    10\t\n    11\t| Task | Approach |\n    12\t|---|---|\n    13\t| **Create** a new document | Write a `docx` (npm) script \u2014 see gotchas below |\n    14\t| **Edit** an existing document | `unzip` \u2192 edit `word/document.xml` \u2192 `zip` (docx-js cannot open existing files) |\n    15\t| **Read** content | `pandoc -t markdown file.docx` |\n    16\t\n    17\t> Script paths below are relative to this skill's directory.\n    18\t\n    19\t## Creating with docx-js \u2014 gotchas\n    20\t\n    21\t`docx` is preinstalled \u2014 do not run `npm install` first; write the script and `require('docx')` directly. Only if that require fails: `npm install docx`. The model knows the API; these are the footguns:\n    22\t\n    23\t- **Page size defaults to A4.** For US Letter set `page: { size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 } }` (DXA; 1440 = 1\u2033).\n    24\t- **Landscape:** pass portrait dimensions and `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE` \u2014 docx-js swaps width/height internally.\n    25\t- **Tables need dual widths:** set `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on every cell, both in `WidthType.DXA` (PERCENTAGE breaks in Google Docs). Column widths must sum to the table width.\n    26\t- **Table shading:** use `ShadingType.CLEAR`, never `SOLID` (renders black).\n    27\t- **Lists:** never insert `\u2022` literally; use a `numbering` config with `LevelFormat.BULLET`.\n    28\t- **`ImageRun` requires `type:`** (`\"png\"`, `\"jpg\"`, \u2026).\n    29\t- **`PageBreak` must be inside a `Paragraph`.**\n    30\t- **Never use `\\n`** \u2014 use separate `Paragraph` elements.\n    31\t- **TOC:** headings must use built-in `HeadingLevel.*`; custom heading styles need `outlineLevel` set or they won't appear.\n    32\t- **Don't use a table as a horizontal rule** \u2014 use a paragraph bottom border instead.\n    33\t- **Dot-leader / right-aligned-on-same-line:** use `PositionalTab` (`alignment: PositionalTabAlignment.RIGHT`, `leader: PositionalTabLeader.DOT`) inside a `TextRun`, not literal `.` or space padding.\n    34\t\n    35\t## Verify the output\n    36\t\n    37\tAfter writing a `.docx`, render it and look at it:\n    38\t\n    39\t```bash\n    40\tpython scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf output.docx\n    41\tpdftoppm -jpeg -r 100 output.pdf page\n    42\tls page-*.jpg   # then Read the images\n    43\t```\n    44\t\n    45\t`pdftoppm` zero-pads page numbers to the width of the page count (`page-01.jpg`\u2026`page-12.jpg`).\n    46\t\n    47\t## Editing existing documents\n    48\t\n    49\tLegacy `.doc` files must be converted first: `python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx file.doc`.\n    50\t\n    51\t```bash\n    52\tunzip -q doc.docx -d unpacked/\n    53\tfind unpacked -type l -delete   # strip symlink entries \u2014 docx from external parties is untrusted\n    54\tpython scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/   # coalesce fragmented runs so text is findable\n    55\t# edit unpacked/word/document.xml in place \u2014 do NOT reformat or pretty-print\n    56\t(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.docx && zip -Xr ../out.docx .)\n    57\tpython scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original doc.docx   # XSD checks; --auto-repair fixes common issues\n    58\t# redlining? add --author \"<the name you redlined under>\" to check every edit is tracked\n    59\t```\n    60\t\n    61\tWord splits text across many `<w:r>` runs (revision ids, spell-check markers), so a phrase you can see in the document often doesn't exist as a contiguous string in the XML. `merge_runs.py` merges adjacent identically-formatted runs in `word/document.xml` without changing content or rendering; it also accepts a `.docx` directly (`python scripts/merge_runs.py doc.docx -o merged.docx`).\n    62\t\n    63\t**Tracked changes:** when redlining, validate with `--author \"<the name you redlined under>\"` (needs `--original`) \u2014 it reports any text you changed without a `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` around it, which is easy to do by accident and invisible in the accepted view. Wrap runs in `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` with `w:id`, `w:author`, `w:date` attributes. Inside `<w:del>`, the text element is `<w:delText>`, not `<w:t>`. A deleted paragraph mark (`<w:pPr><w:rPr><w:del w:id=\"..\" w:author=\"..\" w:date=\"..\"/></w:rPr></w:pPr>`) means \"merge this paragraph into the next\" \u2014 so deleting a paragraph outright is that plus a `<w:del>` around every run. The `<w:del/>` must come before the rPr's other children; their order is schema-enforced.\n    64\t\n    65\tTo produce a clean copy with all tracked changes accepted: `python scripts/accept_changes.py in.docx out.docx`.\n    66\t\n    67\tAccepting a deleted paragraph mark should join that paragraph to the one below it, so a paragraph whose runs are *all* deleted vanishes. Word does this; `accept_changes.py` and `pandoc --track-changes=accept` don't always. Both fail the same way \u2014 they strip the deleted text but leave the emptied paragraph behind, which reads as a stray empty bullet when it was auto-numbered:\n    68\t\n    69\t- `pandoc --track-changes=accept` never joins the paragraphs.\n    70\t- `accept_changes.py` (LibreOffice) joins them correctly, except when the deleted paragraph is followed by an empty spacer paragraph.\n    71\t\n    72\tAn empty bullet in either view is an artifact of that view, not a defect in the document. Check paragraph deletions in the XML.\n    73\t\n    74\t## Comments\n    75\t\n    76\tComments require six cross-linked files. Use the helper \u2014 directory mode when you'll also be editing `document.xml` (saves an unzip/rezip cycle), `.docx`-direct mode otherwise:\n    77\t\n    78\t```bash\n    79\t# Against an already-unpacked directory (preferred when also placing markers)\n    80\tpython scripts/comment.py unpacked/ \"Fees & expenses cap is too low\"\n    81\tpython scripts/comment.py unpacked/ \"Agreed\" --parent 0\n    82\t\n    83\t# Against a .docx directly\n    84\tpython scripts/comment.py contract.docx \"This cap is too low\" -o annotated.docx\n    85\t```\n    86\t\n    87\tThe script writes `comments.xml`, `commentsExtended.xml`, `commentsIds.xml`, `commentsExtensible.xml`, the relationships, and the content-type overrides. Comment IDs are auto-assigned. It then prints the `<w:commentRangeStart>`/`<w:commentRangeEnd>`/`<w:commentReference>` snippet to add to `word/document.xml` so the comment anchors to specific text \u2014 until you place those markers, the comment exists but is not visible.\n    88\t\n    89\t## Dependencies\n    90\t\n    91\t`docx` (npm, preinstalled \u2014 install only if `require('docx')` fails) \u00b7 `pandoc` \u00b7 LibreOffice (`soffice`) \u00b7 `pdftoppm` (Poppler)\n    92\t",

                            "title": "Chunari/Bandhani Saree D2C: Two-Phase Social Commerce Blueprint 2026",
                            "type": "text/markdown",
                            "language": null,
                            "content": "# Two-Phase Social-Commerce Proposal Blueprint: Chunari/Bandhani Saree D2C (2026)\n\n## TL;DR\n- **Run Phase 1 at \u20b912,000/month for 2 months (~\u20b924,000 total), split roughly \u20b96,000 ad spend / \u20b94,000 fresher execution / \u20b91,000 tools+creative / \u20b91,000 your token oversight fee.** Prioritise an **Instagram-Reels-for-discovery + WhatsApp-for-closing** funnel driven by Click-to-WhatsApp (CTWA) ads; treat Facebook as a free bonus placement and defer the website/Instagram Shop.\n- **Realistic Phase 1 proof (cumulative over 8 weeks): 1,000\u20133,000 followers, ~120\u2013150 WhatsApp conversations, ~12\u201322 orders, \u20b98,000\u201314,000 revenue** \u2014 which clears the daughter's \u20b910,000 trigger. First DM enquiries realistically appear in weeks 4\u20136, not week 1.\n- **Phase 2 (month 3 onward, timed to the Oct\u2013Nov 2026 festive peak): \u20b925,000\u201330,000/month** (the daughter's doubled budget), with ad spend pushed past the \u20b915,000 \"real optimisation\" threshold, a proper service fee for you, expanded content, and 3\u20135 nano-influencer micro-collabs.\n\n## Key Findings\n\n**1. The budget range you're considering is right, but land at the top of it.** Below roughly \u20b915,000/month in *ad spend alone*, Meta's algorithm struggles to exit its learning phase, so Phase 1 is deliberately a \"learning + proof\" budget, not an \"optimised scale\" budget \u2014 set expectations accordingly. Because your total Phase 1 envelope (\u20b97,000\u201312,000) has to cover ad spend *plus* people *plus* tools, the only realistic way to generate visible sales is to protect ad spend at ~\u20b96,000/month (~\u20b9200/day, the platform's practical starting floor) and keep everything else lean via the fresher.\n\n**2. Fresher/freelancer rates support your lean model.** Fresher freelance digital marketers in India bill roughly \u20b9300\u2013600/hour, and entry-level social-media executives earn \u20b915,000\u201325,000/month full-time. A part-time fresher managing one small account (content + posting + basic ad management, ~8\u201310 hrs/week) realistically costs \u20b94,000\u20137,000/month \u2014 which is exactly why your Phase 1 math works. A full freelance SMM retainer runs \u20b98,000\u201330,000/month and a small agency \u20b920,000\u201360,000, so you are correctly undercutting the market for the proof phase.\n\n**3. The winning channel mix is Instagram + WhatsApp, not a website.** Your client's instinct to skip the website is defensible for Phase 1. India was the world's largest Instagram market with an advertising audience of 414 million users as of January 2025 \u2014 ahead of the US (172M) and Brazil (141M) \u2014 per DataReportal's analysis of Meta's ad-planning tools (Digital 2025); Meta's India Business Report Q4 2025 gives 362M monthly active users. Instagram Reels are the cheapest, highest-reach discovery format (Reels CPMs run 25\u201340% below feed; Reels deliver ~3.5x the reach of carousels), while WhatsApp is where Indian buyers actually place orders. Click-to-WhatsApp ads are the connective tissue: cost per WhatsApp conversation in India runs \u20b95\u201325 for e-commerce/consumer products (per WA.Expert's India CTWA benchmarks), and click-to-paid-order conversion lands at \"4 to 12 percent measured over a 30 day window\" (per getKanal's Click-to-WhatsApp Ads Benchmarks 2026) \u2014 a far shorter, cheaper funnel than sending cold traffic to a website. You should still record NAP consistency groundwork (a Google Business Profile is free and worth doing), but a transactional website can wait for Phase 2/3.\n\n**4. Sarees are a high-return, expectation-sensitive category \u2014 plan for it.** Apparel bought online in India hit a 24.4% return rate in 2023 versus the 16.5% global average (Coresight Research), and clothing is India's most-returned category at 25\u201340% (Unicommerce India Ecommerce Index Report, via Fibre2Fashion) \u2014 driven by colour-mismatch and fabric-expectation gaps. Your \u20b9200\u20132,000 budget-to-lower-mid positioning helps (lower value at risk), but you must mitigate with fabric-in-motion Reels, honest fabric/length/blouse-piece descriptions, and \u2014 critically \u2014 a WhatsApp COD-confirmation step plus a prepaid incentive. COD accounts for ~45% of Indian D2C orders (down from 55% in 2024, per Growww Tech's State of Indian D2C 2026), and COD orders see ~26% RTO versus under 2% for prepaid (\"COD orders in Indian e-commerce see RTO rates of nearly 26%, compared to less than 2% for prepaid orders,\" per GoKwik); WhatsApp confirmation cuts RTO by 30\u201355%.\n\n**5. Your timing is strategically excellent.** Launching Phase 1 in August 2026 means the proof phase (Aug\u2013Sep) sets up the machine, and Phase 2 scale-up (Oct onward) lands squarely in the festive peak \u2014 Navratri (Oct 11\u201319), Dussehra/Vijayadashami (Oct 20), and Diwali 2026 on Sunday, 8 November (Lakshmi Puja), with the five-day festival running 6\u201310 November (per Diwali.info; the date falls ~19 days later than 2025 because of a leap month, *adhik maas*). Bandhani/bandhej is *the* auspicious festive-and-wedding textile of Gujarat and Rajasthan, so demand seasonality aligns perfectly with the client's existing regional strength (Gujarat/MP/UP). Budget for ad costs to rise sharply in this window (see Caveats).\n\n## Details\n\n### A. Recommended Phase 1 budget and breakdown (\u20b912,000/month \u00d7 ~2 months)\n\n| Line item | Monthly | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Meta ad spend (CTWA + engagement/reach)** | **\u20b96,000** (~\u20b9200/day) | Practical starting floor; enough to generate conversations and first sales, but understood to be a learning budget |\n| **Fresher freelancer (execution)** | **\u20b94,000** | Content shooting/editing, posting, story/status, basic ad management, DM handling \u2014 ~8\u201310 hrs/week at fresher rates |\n| **Tools + creative** | **\u20b91,000** | Canva Pro (~\u20b9500), a WhatsApp catalog tool (plans from \u20b979/month), amortised props/model/photography |\n| **Your strategy & oversight fee (token)** | **\u20b91,000** | Deliberately near-nominal to build trust on a first referral project \u2014 framed explicitly as an investment in the relationship |\n| **TOTAL** | **\u20b912,000/month** | ~\u20b924,000 across the 8-week proof phase |\n\n**Why \u20b912,000, not \u20b97,000:** at the \u20b97,000 floor, after paying the fresher and tools you'd have only ~\u20b92,000\u20133,000 for ads, which would not generate enough conversations to hit the \u20b910,000 revenue trigger. At \u20b912,000 you protect ~\u20b96,000/month (~\u20b912,000 over two months) of ad fuel, which models to roughly 120\u2013150 conversations and ~12\u201322 orders \u2014 enough to clear \u20b910,000 cumulative revenue. If the client insists on a lower number, \u20b99,000\u201310,000/month is the absolute floor and ad spend should never drop below \u20b95,000.\n\n**Ad-economics model (present as an estimate, not a guarantee):** \u20b912,000 ad spend over 8 weeks, at India CTWA conversation costs of \u20b95\u201325 (e-commerce) to as high as ~\u20b980 for tougher targeting, models to roughly 120\u2013150+ WhatsApp conversations \u2192 at a 4\u201312% click-to-paid-order conversion (getKanal, 30-day window) \u2248 ~12\u201322 orders \u2192 at a blended \u20b9500\u2013700 order value \u2248 **\u20b98,000\u201314,000 revenue.** In 2026 the median Meta ROAS for fashion brands is 2.18x (range 2.18x\u20132.96x, top 10% at 6.0x, per AdAmigo.ai's Fashion eCommerce Meta Ads ROAS Benchmarks 2026), but a brand-new account with no retargeting pool and no pixel history will likely run *below* median in Phase 1 \u2014 expect roughly break-even-to-1.5x on ad spend, which is normal and acceptable for a proof phase.\n\n### B. Recommended Phase 2 budget and breakdown (\u20b925,000\u201330,000/month)\n\nThe daughter's stated trigger is to *double her investment*. Doubling the \u20b912,000 Phase 1 gives ~\u20b924,000; round to a \u20b925,000\u201330,000/month working range for month 3 onward.\n\n| Line item | Monthly (\u20b925k\u201330k range) | Change vs Phase 1 |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Meta ad spend** | \u20b915,000\u201317,000 | Crosses the \u20b915,000 threshold where Meta reliably optimises; funds prospecting + retargeting + festive push |\n| **Fresher/expanded execution** | \u20b96,000\u20138,000 | More content volume, daily posting, faster DM/order response |\n| **Your service/strategy fee (proper)** | \u20b95,000\u20137,000 | Now a real, justified fee (see framing below) |\n| **Tools + nano-influencer micro-collabs** | \u20b93,000\u20135,000 | BSP/WhatsApp automation, 3\u20135 nano creators (\u20b92,000\u20138,000/reel, or product-gifting) |\n\n**How to justify the Phase 2 increase honestly:** frame it as *\"we spent Phase 1 proving the model with minimal risk; now we invest in scaling what already works.\"* The three honest reasons: (1) ad spend crosses the optimisation threshold so cost-per-order *falls*; (2) a retargeting pool and pixel/CTWA data now exist, so ROAS improves; (3) Phase 2 coincides with the festive peak when bandhani demand is highest. Your own fee rising from token to real is justified because you're now managing a proven, higher-stakes account \u2014 not asking for trust on faith.\n\n### C. Platform prioritisation (with reasoning)\n\n1. **Instagram (primary \u2014 discovery).** India is Instagram's largest market. Reels are the single highest-reach organic tool and the cheapest paid placement. This is where a zero-following brand gets seen. Content anchor: fabric-in-motion draping Reels (they reportedly get 3\u20135x the views of static saree photos).\n2. **WhatsApp Business (primary \u2014 conversion).** Most Indian buyers prefer to order via WhatsApp. Set up the free WhatsApp Business app + Catalog (up to 500 products, best-sellers first, clear \u20b9 prices, no \"DM for price\"). This is your storefront and checkout without a website.\n3. **Facebook (secondary \u2014 free bonus).** Don't build a separate FB content strategy; simply enable Facebook as a Meta ad placement and let Advantage+ distribute. Bandhani skews toward women 25\u201345 who are well-represented on Facebook in tier-2/3 India.\n4. **Defer:** website, Instagram Shop checkout, Meesho/marketplace listings. Revisit in Phase 2/3.\n\n### D. Realistic KPI targets, weeks 1\u20138\n\n*(Deliberately conservative. Agency case studies claiming \"3x followers in 7 days\" or \"10,000 followers in 45 days\" exist but are self-promotional best-cases involving heavy influencer spend \u2014 do not put these in the client proposal.)*\n\n| Window | Activity | Followers (cumulative) | Conversations | Orders | Notes |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **Weeks 1\u20132** | Setup: profile, catalog, pixel/CTWA, content bank, soft-launch posts | 100\u2013400 | 0\u20135 | 0\u20131 | Minimal/no ad spend; foundation |\n| **Weeks 3\u20134** | Ads live (CTWA + reach); first optimisation | 400\u20131,000 | 30\u201345 | 2\u20135 | First real enquiries begin ~week 4 |\n| **Weeks 5\u20136** | Scale winning creatives; retarget engagers | 1,000\u20132,000 | 40\u201355 | 4\u20138 | Cost-per-order starts falling |\n| **Weeks 7\u20138** | Urgency/festive-preview push | 1,500\u20133,000 | 40\u201355 | 5\u20139 | Cumulative revenue crosses \u20b910k |\n| **8-week total** | \u2014 | **1,000\u20133,000** | **~120\u2013150** | **~12\u201322** | **\u20b98,000\u201314,000 revenue** |\n\nSupporting benchmarks: engagement rate for a 0\u20131k account should target 8\u201315%; ads at this budget realistically reach a few tens of thousands of people/month; purely organic growth for a brand-new account is only ~50\u2013200 followers in months 1\u20132, which is why paid amplification is essential to hit these numbers on your timeline.\n\n### E. Deliverables checklist \u2014 Phase 1 vs Phase 2\n\n**Phase 1 (included in \u20b912,000/month):**\n- Instagram Business + Facebook Page setup, optimised bio with WhatsApp click-through\n- WhatsApp Business app + Catalog setup (best-sellers, clear pricing, collections)\n- Google Business Profile creation (free NAP groundwork)\n- Meta pixel / CTWA + Conversions API basic setup\n- **3 Reels/week + 2\u20133 static/carousel posts/week + daily Stories + daily WhatsApp Status**\n- 1\u20132 CTWA ad campaigns + 1 reach/engagement campaign, weekly optimisation\n- WhatsApp order flow: welcome message, COD-confirmation step, prepaid-incentive (5\u201310% off) message\n- DM/enquiry handling within a few hours\n- **Simple weekly WhatsApp update + one end-of-phase results report** (followers, reach, conversations, orders, revenue, ROAS)\n\n**Reserved / upsold for Phase 2:**\n- Expanded content (5 Reels/week, UGC, customer testimonial reposts, \"pack-an-order-with-me\" Reels)\n- 3\u20135 nano/micro-influencer micro-collabs (gifting-first)\n- Full retargeting + lookalike-audience funnel; festive campaign calendar\n- WhatsApp Business API / BSP automation (broadcast lists, abandoned-cart, drip nurture)\n- Deeper analytics/reporting cadence (fortnightly dashboards, cohort/repeat-purchase tracking)\n- Basic transactional website + Instagram Shop + Google local SEO\n- Possible marketplace expansion (Meesho) for volume\n\n## Recommendations\n\n1. **Propose Phase 1 at \u20b912,000/month for 2 months.** Present the four-line breakdown above. Make ad spend a protected, non-negotiable \u20b96,000/month line so the proof has fuel.\n2. **Frame the \u20b910,000 trigger as cumulative over 8 weeks, not monthly** \u2014 and put the conservative KPI table in writing so the daughter's expectations match reality. This protects the relationship.\n3. **Build the funnel as Reels \u2192 profile \u2192 WhatsApp \u2192 COD-confirmation \u2192 prepaid nudge.** Lead all creative with fabric-in-motion draping Reels and festive/occasion framing (Navratri, weddings, Garba).\n4. **Attack returns proactively:** honest fabric/length/blouse descriptions, real-product video, WhatsApp COD confirmation, and a 5\u201310% prepaid discount. Track return/RTO rate as a Phase 1 KPI \u2014 with COD RTO near 26% versus under 2% prepaid, shifting the payment mix is the single highest-leverage margin lever.\n5. **Pre-sell Phase 2 now** by tying it to the festive peak: *\"If we prove the model by end September, we scale into Navratri (Oct 11\u201319) and Diwali (Nov 8) when bandhani demand peaks.\"* This turns the budget doubling into an obvious, time-sensitive decision.\n6. **Benchmarks that should change the plan:** if by week 4 cost-per-conversation exceeds ~\u20b9120 or click-to-order conversion is below ~4%, pause and rework creative/targeting before spending more. If week-8 revenue clears \u20b910,000, trigger Phase 2 immediately. If return/RTO exceeds ~30%, shift aggressively to prepaid-only and tighten product descriptions before scaling ad spend.\n\n## Caveats\n- **Sarees are among the highest-return categories online (clothing 25\u201340% in India; apparel 24.4% overall in 2023 vs 16.5% global).** Effective margins can compress to 10\u201315% net after returns; the proof-phase revenue number matters less than the *net* number, so track returns from day one.\n- **Sub-\u20b915,000/month ad spend limits Meta's optimisation.** Phase 1 numbers carry real variance; the \u20b98,000\u201314,000 revenue range is a modeled estimate, not a guarantee. CTWA conversation-cost sources conflict (\u20b95\u201325 for e-commerce per WA.Expert vs ~\u20b980 per Meta+Sinch regional data) \u2014 budget on the conservative side.\n- **Meta ad costs for saree D2C have risen sharply** \u2014 India CPMs rose ~23% year-over-year (Monaqo / Wittelsbach.ai, H1 2026, 340+ accounts) \u2014 and festive-season demand produces ROAS spikes of 40\u2013120% above baseline alongside higher CPMs; budget for this in Phase 2.\n- **Festive-date sources conflict** (Navratri is consistently Oct 11\u201319, 2026; Diwali is most reliably 8 November 2026 per Diwali.info/Drik Panchang, though some tourism sites erroneously list October). Confirm exact dates before locking the festive campaign calendar.\n- **Agency case-study growth claims are promotional.** The conservative KPI table is the honest one to show the client; the aspirational \"3x in 7 days\" / \"10k in 45 days\" numbers are not.\n- **CTWA/WhatsApp API for marketing carries India DPDP (in force Nov 2025) consent obligations** \u2014 collect only necessary data, explain why, and make opt-out easy once you move to broadcast/automation in Phase 2.",

                                "text": "     1\t---\n     2\tname: pdf\n     3\tdescription: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.\n     4\tlicense: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms\n     5\t---\n     6\t\n     7\t# PDF Processing Guide\n     8\t\n     9\t## Overview\n    10\t\n    11\tThis guide covers essential PDF processing operations using Python libraries and command-line tools. For advanced features, JavaScript libraries, and detailed examples, see REFERENCE.md. If you need to fill out a PDF form, read FORMS.md and follow its instructions.\n    12\t\n    13\t## Quick Start\n    14\t\n    15\t```python\n    16\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter\n    17\t\n    18\t# Read a PDF\n    19\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n    20\tprint(f\"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}\")\n    21\t\n    22\t# Extract text\n    23\ttext = \"\"\n    24\tfor page in reader.pages:\n    25\t    text += page.extract_text()\n    26\t```\n    27\t\n    28\t## Python Libraries\n    29\t\n    30\t### pypdf - Basic Operations\n    31\t\n    32\t#### Merge PDFs\n    33\t```python\n    34\tfrom pypdf import PdfWriter, PdfReader\n    35\t\n    36\twriter = PdfWriter()\n    37\tfor pdf_file in [\"doc1.pdf\", \"doc2.pdf\", \"doc3.pdf\"]:\n    38\t    reader = PdfReader(pdf_file)\n    39\t    for page in reader.pages:\n    40\t        writer.add_page(page)\n    41\t\n    42\twith open(\"merged.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n    43\t    writer.write(output)\n    44\t```\n    45\t\n    46\t#### Split PDF\n    47\t```python\n    48\treader = PdfReader(\"input.pdf\")\n    49\tfor i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):\n    50\t    writer = PdfWriter()\n    51\t    writer.add_page(page)\n    52\t    with open(f\"page_{i+1}.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n    53\t        writer.write(output)\n    54\t```\n    55\t\n    56\t#### Extract Metadata\n    57\t```python\n    58\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n    59\tmeta = reader.metadata\n    60\tprint(f\"Title: {meta.title}\")\n    61\tprint(f\"Author: {meta.author}\")\n    62\tprint(f\"Subject: {meta.subject}\")\n    63\tprint(f\"Creator: {meta.creator}\")\n    64\t```\n    65\t\n    66\t#### Rotate Pages\n    67\t```python\n    68\treader = PdfReader(\"input.pdf\")\n    69\twriter = PdfWriter()\n    70\t\n    71\tpage = reader.pages[0]\n    72\tpage.rotate(90)  # Rotate 90 degrees clockwise\n    73\twriter.add_page(page)\n    74\t\n    75\twith open(\"rotated.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n    76\t    writer.write(output)\n    77\t```\n    78\t\n    79\t### pdfplumber - Text and Table Extraction\n    80\t\n    81\t#### Extract Text with Layout\n    82\t```python\n    83\timport pdfplumber\n    84\t\n    85\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n    86\t    for page in pdf.pages:\n    87\t        text = page.extract_text()\n    88\t        print(text)\n    89\t```\n    90\t\n    91\t#### Extract Tables\n    92\t```python\n    93\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n    94\t    for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):\n    95\t        tables = page.extract_tables()\n    96\t        for j, table in enumerate(tables):\n    97\t            print(f\"Table {j+1} on page {i+1}:\")\n    98\t            for row in table:\n    99\t                print(row)\n   100\t```\n   101\t\n   102\t#### Advanced Table Extraction\n   103\t```python\n   104\timport pandas as pd\n   105\t\n   106\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n   107\t    all_tables = []\n   108\t    for page in pdf.pages:\n   109\t        tables = page.extract_tables()\n   110\t        for table in tables:\n   111\t            if table:  # Check if table is not empty\n   112\t                df = pd.DataFrame(table[1:], columns=table[0])\n   113\t                all_tables.append(df)\n   114\t\n   115\t# Combine all tables\n   116\tif all_tables:\n   117\t    combined_df = pd.concat(all_tables, ignore_index=True)\n   118\t    combined_df.to_excel(\"extracted_tables.xlsx\", index=False)\n   119\t```\n   120\t\n   121\t### reportlab - Create PDFs\n   122\t\n   123\t#### Basic PDF Creation\n   124\t```python\n   125\tfrom reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter\n   126\tfrom reportlab.pdfgen import canvas\n   127\t\n   128\tc = canvas.Canvas(\"hello.pdf\", pagesize=letter)\n   129\twidth, height = letter\n   130\t\n   131\t# Add text\n   132\tc.drawString(100, height - 100, \"Hello World!\")\n   133\tc.drawString(100, height - 120, \"This is a PDF created with reportlab\")\n   134\t\n   135\t# Add a line\n   136\tc.line(100, height - 140, 400, height - 140)\n   137\t\n   138\t# Save\n   139\tc.save()\n   140\t```\n   141\t\n   142\t#### Create PDF with Multiple Pages\n   143\t```python\n   144\tfrom reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter\n   145\tfrom reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak\n   146\tfrom reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet\n   147\t\n   148\tdoc = SimpleDocTemplate(\"report.pdf\", pagesize=letter)\n   149\tstyles = getSampleStyleSheet()\n   150\tstory = []\n   151\t\n   152\t# Add content\n   153\ttitle = Paragraph(\"Report Title\", styles['Title'])\n   154\tstory.append(title)\n   155\tstory.append(Spacer(1, 12))\n   156\t\n   157\tbody = Paragraph(\"This is the body of the report. \" * 20, styles['Normal'])\n   158\tstory.append(body)\n   159\tstory.append(PageBreak())\n   160\t\n   161\t# Page 2\n   162\tstory.append(Paragraph(\"Page 2\", styles['Heading1']))\n   163\tstory.append(Paragraph(\"Content for page 2\", styles['Normal']))\n   164\t\n   165\t# Build PDF\n   166\tdoc.build(story)\n   167\t```\n   168\t\n   169\t#### Subscripts and Superscripts\n   170\t\n   171\t**IMPORTANT**: Never use Unicode subscript/superscript characters (\u2080\u2081\u2082\u2083\u2084\u2085\u2086\u2087\u2088\u2089, \u2070\u00b9\u00b2\u00b3\u2074\u2075\u2076\u2077\u2078\u2079) in ReportLab PDFs. The built-in fonts do not include these glyphs, causing them to render as solid black boxes.\n   172\t\n   173\tInstead, use ReportLab's XML markup tags in Paragraph objects:\n   174\t```python\n   175\tfrom reportlab.platypus import Paragraph\n   176\tfrom reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet\n   177\t\n   178\tstyles = getSampleStyleSheet()\n   179\t\n   180\t# Subscripts: use <sub> tag\n   181\tchemical = Paragraph(\"H<sub>2</sub>O\", styles['Normal'])\n   182\t\n   183\t# Superscripts: use <super> tag\n   184\tsquared = Paragraph(\"x<super>2</super> + y<super>2</super>\", styles['Normal'])\n   185\t```\n   186\t\n   187\tFor canvas-drawn text (not Paragraph objects), manually adjust font the size and position rather than using Unicode subscripts/superscripts.\n   188\t\n   189\t## Command-Line Tools\n   190\t\n   191\t### pdftotext (poppler-utils)\n   192\t```bash\n   193\t# Extract text\n   194\tpdftotext input.pdf output.txt\n   195\t\n   196\t# Extract text preserving layout\n   197\tpdftotext -layout input.pdf output.txt\n   198\t\n   199\t# Extract specific pages\n   200\tpdftotext -f 1 -l 5 input.pdf output.txt  # Pages 1-5\n   201\t```\n   202\t\n   203\t### qpdf\n   204\t```bash\n   205\t# Merge PDFs\n   206\tqpdf --empty --pages file1.pdf file2.pdf -- merged.pdf\n   207\t\n   208\t# Split pages\n   209\tqpdf input.pdf --pages . 1-5 -- pages1-5.pdf\n   210\tqpdf input.pdf --pages . 6-10 -- pages6-10.pdf\n   211\t\n   212\t# Rotate pages\n   213\tqpdf input.pdf output.pdf --rotate=+90:1  # Rotate page 1 by 90 degrees\n   214\t\n   215\t# Remove password\n   216\tqpdf --password=mypassword --decrypt encrypted.pdf decrypted.pdf\n   217\t```\n   218\t\n   219\t### pdftk (if available)\n   220\t```bash\n   221\t# Merge\n   222\tpdftk file1.pdf file2.pdf cat output merged.pdf\n   223\t\n   224\t# Split\n   225\tpdftk input.pdf burst\n   226\t\n   227\t# Rotate\n   228\tpdftk input.pdf rotate 1east output rotated.pdf\n   229\t```\n   230\t\n   231\t## Common Tasks\n   232\t\n   233\t### Extract Text from Scanned PDFs\n   234\t```python\n   235\t# Requires: pip install pytesseract pdf2image\n   236\timport pytesseract\n   237\tfrom pdf2image import convert_from_path\n   238\t\n   239\t# Convert PDF to images\n   240\timages = convert_from_path('scanned.pdf')\n   241\t\n   242\t# OCR each page\n   243\ttext = \"\"\n   244\tfor i, image in enumerate(images):\n   245\t    text += f\"Page {i+1}:\\n\"\n   246\t    text += pytesseract.image_to_string(image)\n   247\t    text += \"\\n\\n\"\n   248\t\n   249\tprint(text)\n   250\t```\n   251\t\n   252\t### Add Watermark\n   253\t```python\n   254\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter\n   255\t\n   256\t# Create watermark (or load existing)\n   257\twatermark = PdfReader(\"watermark.pdf\").pages[0]\n   258\t\n   259\t# Apply to all pages\n   260\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n   261\twriter = PdfWriter()\n   262\t\n   263\tfor page in reader.pages:\n   264\t    page.merge_page(watermark)\n   265\t    writer.add_page(page)\n   266\t\n   267\twith open(\"watermarked.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n   268\t    writer.write(output)\n   269\t```\n   270\t\n   271\t### Extract Images\n   272\t```bash\n   273\t# Using pdfimages (poppler-utils)\n   274\tpdfimages -j input.pdf output_prefix\n   275\t\n   276\t# This extracts all images as output_prefix-000.jpg, output_prefix-001.jpg, etc.\n   277\t```\n   278\t\n   279\t### Password Protection\n   280\t```python\n   281\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter\n   282\t\n   283\treader = PdfReader(\"input.pdf\")\n   284\twriter = PdfWriter()\n   285\t\n   286\tfor page in reader.pages:\n   287\t    writer.add_page(page)\n   288\t\n   289\t# Add password\n   290\twriter.encrypt(\"userpassword\", \"ownerpassword\")\n   291\t\n   292\twith open(\"encrypted.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n   293\t    writer.write(output)\n   294\t```\n   295\t\n   296\t## Quick Reference\n   297\t\n   298\t| Task | Best Tool | Command/Code |\n   299\t|------|-----------|--------------|\n   300\t| Merge PDFs | pypdf | `writer.add_page(page)` |\n   301\t| Split Quotation</div>\n  <h1>Taking Your Chunari Sarees<br>Online</h1>\n  <div class=\"cover-rule\"></div>\n  <div class=\"sub\">A phased social-commerce launch plan built for a first-time online venture</div>\n\n  <div class=\"cover-meta\">\n    <div><b>Prepared for:</b> [Client / Business Name]</div>\n    <div><b>Prepared by:</b> Vraj Vithalani</div>\n    <div><b>Date:</b> 11 August 2026</div>\n    <div><b>Validity:</b> This quotation is valid for 15 days from the date above</div>\n  </div>\n</div>\n\n<!-- PAGE 1: INTRO -->\n<h2 class=\"section\">Understanding Your Business</h2>\n<p>\nYour family has built a strong wholesale presence in chunari sarees over 15 years, with an established\ndistribution footprint across Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Uttar Pradesh. This proposal is for the next\nchapter \u2014 taking that same craftsmanship and trust directly to individual customers, pan-India, through\nsocial media.\n</p>\n<p>\nSince this is a first-time online launch \u2014 no existing page, no content, no prior digital sales \u2014 the\nright approach is to prove the model works before scaling spend on it. This proposal is structured in\ntwo phases for exactly that reason.\n</p>\n\n<div class=\"callout\">\n<b>Our approach in one line:</b> Start lean, get real orders flowing through Instagram and WhatsApp,\nand only scale the budget once results are visible \u2014 with Phase 2 timed to land right at the festive\nseason (Navratri &amp; Diwali), when demand for bandhani and festive sarees peaks.\n</div>\n\n<h3 class=\"sub\">Where We'll Sell</h3>\n<div class=\"two-col\">\n  <div class=\"col\">\n    <p><b>Instagram \u2014 for discovery.</b> Reels showing the drape, fall, and colour of each saree are the\n    most effective way to get a brand-new page seen by the right audience, at the lowest cost.</p>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"col\">\n    <p><b>WhatsApp \u2014 for closing the sale.</b> Most customers in India prefer to finalise a purchase over\n    WhatsApp. We'll set up a proper Catalog with clear pricing, so browsing turns into orders smoothly.</p>\n  </div>\n</div>\n<p class=\"footnote\">\nA website is intentionally not part of Phase 1 \u2014 it isn't needed to start selling, and keeping the\nbudget focused on Instagram + WhatsApp gets you to real orders faster. We recommend revisiting a simple\nwebsite once the online leg is established, mainly for consistent business information across the web.\n</p>\n\n<div class=\"page-break\"></div>\n\n<!-- PHASE 1 -->\n<h2 class=\"section\">Phase 1 \u2014 Proof of Concept</h2>\n<p>The goal of Phase 1 is simple: launch professionally, generate genuine first orders, and prove the\nmodel with minimal risk \u2014 before any bigger investment is made.</p>\n\n<div class=\"phase-header\">\n  <span class=\"pprice\">\u20b912,000<span style=\"font-size:9pt; font-weight:400;\"> /month</span></span>\n  <div class=\"ptitle\">Phase 1: Launch &amp; Proof</div>\n  <div class=\"pmeta\">Duration: 2 months &nbsp;\u2022&nbsp; Total investment: \u20b924,000</div>\n</div>\n\n<table>\n  <tr><th>Investment Area</th><th class=\"num\">Monthly</th></tr>\n  <tr><td>Instagram &amp; WhatsApp advertising (audience reach + orders)</td><td class=\"num\">\u20b96,000</td></tr>\n  <tr><td>Content creation &amp; day-to-day execution</td><td class=\"num\">\u20b94,000</td></tr>\n  <tr><td>Tools, design software &amp; catalog setup</td><td class=\"num\">\u20b91,000</td></tr>\n  <tr><td>Strategy, planning &amp; account management</td><td class=\"num\">\u20b91,000</td></tr>\n  <tr class=\"total\"><td>Total</td><td class=\"num\">\u20b912,000 / month</td></tr>\n</table>\n\n<h3 class=\"sub\">What's Included</h3>\n<div class=\"two-col\">\n  <div class=\"col\">\n    <ul>\n      <li>Instagram &amp; Facebook page setup and optimisation</li>\n      <li>WhatsApp Business Catalog setup with clear pricing</li>\n      <li>Google Business Profile creation</li>\n      <li>3 Reels + 2\u20133 posts per week</li>\n      <li>Daily Stories &amp; WhatsApp Status</li>\n    </ul>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"col\">\n    <ul>\n      <li>Targeted ad campaigns, optimised weekly</li>\n      <li>Order enquiry &amp; WhatsApp response handling</li>\n      <li>Order-confirmation process to reduce returns</li>\n      <li>Weekly progress updates on WhatsApp</li>\n      <li>Full results report at the end of Phase 1</li>\n    </ul>\n  </div>\n</div>\n\n<h3 class=\"sub\">What You Can Realistically Expect (8 weeks)</h3>\n<div class=\"kpi-grid\">\n  <div class=\"kpi-row\">\n    <div class=\"kpi-cell\"><span class=\"kpi-num\">1,000\u20133,000</span><span class=\"kpi-label\">New Followers</span></div>\n    <div class=\"kpi-cell\"><span class=\"kpi-num\">120\u2013150</span><span class=\"kpi-label\">Buyer Conversations</span></div>\n    <div class=\"kpi-cell\"><span class=\"kpi-num\">12\u201322</span><span class=\"kpi-label\">Orders</span></div>\n    <div class=\"kpi-cell\"><span class=\"kpi-num\">\u20b98k\u201314k</span><span class=\"kpi-label\">Revenue Generated</span></div>\n  </div>\n</div>\n<p class=\"footnote\">\nThese are realistic, research-backed estimates for a brand-new page with this budget \u2014 not a guarantee.\nThe first two weeks focus on setup; enquiries typically pick up from week 3\u20134 onward as ads optimise.\n</p>\n\n<div class=\"page-break\"></div>\n\n<!-- PHASE 2 -->\n<h2 class=\"section\">Phase 2 \u2014 Scale-Up</h2>\n<p>Once Phase 1 proves the model works, Phase 2 builds on it \u2014 with a bigger budget, deeper content,\nand timing aligned to the festive season, when demand for chunari and bandhani sarees is at its highest.</p>\n\n<div class=\"phase-header\">\n  <span class=\"pprice\">\u20b925,000\u201330,000<span style=\"font-size:9pt; font-weight:400;\"> /month</span></span>\n  <div class=\"ptitle\">Phase 2: Scale &amp; Festive Push</div>\n  <div class=\"pmeta\">Starts: Month 3 onward &nbsp;\u2022&nbsp; Timed for Navratri &amp; Diwali 2026</div>\n</div>\n\n<table>\n  <tr><th>Investment Area</th><th class=\"num\">Monthly Range</th></tr>\n  <tr><td>Instagram &amp; WhatsApp advertising (scaled)</td><td class=\"num\">\u20b915,000 \u2013 17,000</td></tr>\n  <tr><td>Expanded content &amp; execution</td><td class=\"num\">\u20b96,000 \u2013 8,000</td></tr>\n  <tr><td>Strategy, planning &amp; account management</td><td class=\"num\">\u20b95,000 \u2013 7,000</td></tr>\n  <tr><td>Tools &amp; nano-influencer collaborations</td><td class=\"num\">\u20b93,000 \u2013 5,000</td></tr>\n  <tr class=\"total\"><td>Total</td><td class=\"num\">\u20b925,000 \u2013 30,000 / month</td></tr>\n</table>\n\n<h3 class=\"sub\">What Changes in Phase 2</h3>\n<ul>\n  <li><b>Bigger ad budget, better efficiency</b> \u2014 at this spend level, advertising platforms optimise\n  properly, which typically lowers the cost of each order compared to Phase 1.</li>\n  <li><b>More content, more often</b> \u2014 expanded Reels output, customer testimonials, and real\n  order-packing content that builds trust.</li>\n  <li><b>Nano-influencer collaborations</b> \u2014 3\u20135 small, relevant creators to extend reach beyond organic\n  followers.</li>\n  <li><b>Festive campaign calendar</b> \u2014 campaigns built specifically around Navratri and Diwali, when\n  demand for festive sarees is highest.</li>\n  <li><b>Deeper reporting</b> \u2014 fortnightly performance dashboards instead of a single end-of-phase report.</li>\n</ul>\n\n<div class=\"callout\">\n<b>Why the increase is worth it:</b> Phase 1 exists to prove the model at low risk. Phase 2 spends more\nbecause it now has data, a warm audience, and proof behind it \u2014 which means every rupee works harder,\nright as festive demand peaks.\n</div>\n\n<h3 class=\"sub\">Also Available From Phase 2 Onward</h3>\n<p>A simple website (for consistent business information online), Instagram Shop, and \u2014 as volume grows \u2014\nlisting on wholesale-friendly marketplaces for additional reach.</p>\n\n<div class=\"page-break\"></div>\n\n<h2 class=\"section\">Why This Structure</h2>\n<div class=\"two-col\">\n  <div class=\"col\">\n    <h3 class=\"sub\">Low risk, real proof first</h3>\n    <p>Rather than asking for a large budget upfront on an unproven channel, Phase 1 is deliberately\n    lean \u2014 enough to generate genuine orders and prove the model works, before any bigger commitment.</p>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"col\">\n    <h3 class=\"sub\">Timed to your advantage</h3>\n    <p>Phase 1 runs through the setup months; Phase 2 scales right into Navratri and Diwali 2026 \u2014\n    exactly when festive and bandhani saree demand is at its annual peak.</p>\n  </div>\n</div>\n\n<h3 class=\"sub\">Payment Terms</h3>\n<ul>\n  <li>Phase 1: 100% payable at the start of each month</li>\n  <li>Ad spend is billed separately and directly through the ad platform, at cost \u2014 no markup</li>\n  <li>Phase 2 begins only once Phase 1 results are shared and reviewed together</li>\n</ul>\n\n<div class=\"closing-box\">\n  <h3>Ready to Begin</h3>\n  <p>This proposal is designed to get your online journey started the right way \u2014 carefully, with real\n  proof at every step. We're looking forward to building this with you.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"signature-block\">\n  <div class=\"sig-col\">\n    <div class=\"sig-line\">For [Client / Business Name] \u2014 Signature &amp; Date</div>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"sig-col\">\n    <div class=\"sig-line\">Vraj Vithalani \u2014 Signature &amp; Date</div>\n  </div>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"validity\">\nThis quotation is valid for 15 days from the date of issue &nbsp;|&nbsp; Prepared by Vraj Vithalani &nbsp;|&nbsp; 11 August 2026\n</div>\n\n</body>\n</html>\n"

enquiries typically pick up from week 3\\u20134 onward as ads optimise.\\n</p>\\n\\n<div class=\\\"page-break\\\"></div>\\n\\n<!-- PHASE 2 -->\\n<h2 class=\\\"section\\\">Phase 2 \\u2014 Scale-Up</h2>\\n<p>Once Phase 1 proves the model works, Phase 2 builds on it \\u2014 with a bigger budget, deeper content,\\nand timing aligned to the festive season, when demand for chunari and bandhani sarees is at its highest.</p>\\n\\n<div class=\\\"phase-header\\\">\\n  <span class=\\\"pprice\\\">\\u20b925,000\\u201330,000<span style=\\\"font-size:9pt; font-weight:400;\\\"> /month</span></span>\\n  <div class=\\\"ptitle\\\">Phase 2: Scale &amp; Festive Push</div>\\n  <div class=\\\"pmeta\\\">Starts: Month 3 onward &nbsp;\\u2022&nbsp; Timed for Navratri &amp; Diwali 2026</div>\\n</div>\\n\\n<table>\\n  <tr><th>Investment Area</th><th class=\\\"num\\\">Monthly Range</th></tr>\\n  <tr><td>Instagram &amp; WhatsApp advertising (scaled)</td><td class=\\\"num\\\">\\u20b915,000 \\u2013 17,000</td></tr>\\n  <tr><td>Expanded content &amp; Phase 2 spends more\\nbecause it now has data, a warm audience, and proof behind it \\u2014 which means every rupee works harder,\\nright as festive demand peaks.\\n</div>\\n\\n<h3 class=\\\"sub\\\">Also Available From Phase 2 Onward</h3>\\n<p>A simple website (for consistent business information online), Instagram Shop, and \\u2014 as volume grows \\u2014\\nlisting on wholesale-friendly marketplaces for additional reach.</p>\\n\\n<div class=\\\"page-break\\\"></div>\\n\\n<h2 class=\\\"section\\\">Why This Structure</h2>\\n<div class=\\\"two-col\\\">\\n  <div class=\\\"col\\\">\\n    <h3 class=\\\"sub\\\">Low risk, real proof first</h3>\\n    <p>Rather than asking for a large budget upfront on an unproven channel, Phase 1 is deliberately\\n    lean \\u2014 enough to generate genuine orders and prove the model works, before any bigger commitment.</p>\\n  </div>\\n  <div class=\\\"col\\\">\\n    <h3 class=\\\"sub\\\">Timed to your advantage</h3>\\n    <p>Phase 1 runs through the setup months; Phase 2 scales right into Navratri and Diwali 2026 \\u2014\\n    exactly when festive and bandhani saree demand is at its annual peak.</p>\\n  </div>\\n</div>\\n\\n<h3 class=\\\"sub\\\">Payment Terms</h3>\\n<ul>\\n  <li>Phase 1: 100% payable at the start of each month</li>\\n  <li>Ad spend is billed separately and directly through the ad platform, at cost \\u2014 no markup</li>\\n  <li>Phase 2 begins only once Phase 1 results are shared and reviewed together</li>\\n</ul>\\n\\n<div class=\\\"closing-box\\\">\\n  <h3>Ready to Begin</h3>\\n  <p>This proposal is designed to get your online journey started the right way \\u2014 carefully, with real\\n  proof at every step.     {
        "uuid": "82dba497-143c-44db-a98d-328bd5700a08",
        "name": "Trust audit reports and 12A/80G certification",
        "summary": "",
        "created_at": "2026-08-13T05:23:06.559444Z",
        "updated_at": "2026-08-13T05:23:31.264357Z",
        "account": {
            "uuid": "271dba8a-47e6-483f-9a1d-d504ad12c578"
        },
        "chat_messages": [
            {
                "uuid": "019ff992-f9f6-7871-bc77-fc91c4e2e7b4",
                "text": "Hey as you know I'm dealing with a trust as for now. So I want to know about one thing. As I said the trust was established in 2019 and from then on the trust was not on operation. I somehow managed to start the trust again after the verification and kyc's and all. And now I want to apply for 12A/80G certifications, but for this we need audit reports and we've not filled any from 2019. Now there were no transactions as well, so we're supposed to fill NIL report only. But what are the incometax charges and can I file it myself or I need a CA for it?",
                "content": [
                    {
                        "start_timestamp": "2026-08-13T05:23:07.960060Z",
                        "stop_timestamp": "2026-08-13T05:23:07.960060Z",
                        "flags": null,
                        "type": "text",
                        "text": "Hey as you know I'm dealing with a trust as for now. So I want to know about one thing. As I said the trust was established in 2019 and from then on the trust was not on operation. I somehow managed to start the trust again after the verification and kyc's and all. And now I want to apply for 12A/80G certifications, but for this we need audit reports and we've not filled any from 2019. Now there were no transactions as well, so we're supposed to fill NIL report only. But what are the incometax charges and can I file it myself or I need a CA for it?",
                        "citations": []
                    }
                ],
                "sender": "human",
                "created_at": "2026-08-13T05:23:07.960265Z",
                "updated_at": "2026-08-13T05:23:07.960265Z",
                "attachments": [],
                "files": [],
                "parent_message_uuid": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"
            },
            {
                "uuid": "019ff992-f9f6-7888-83ef-c751aa7a0543",
                "text": "\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nThis project's files don't cover this specific tax question \u2014 they're just registration/affidavit documents for your trust. Let me answer from general knowledge instead.\n\nHere's the situation, broken into the two things you're asking:\n\n**Can you self-file, or do you need a CA?**\n\nFor a trust, income tax return filing (ITR-7) and the accompanying audit report (Form 10B/10BB) are two different things:\n\n- **The ITR-7 return itself** \u2014 you technically *can* file this yourself if you're comfortable with the income tax portal, since it doesn't legally require a CA.\n- **The audit report (Form 10B or 10BB)** \u2014 this **must** be filed by a Chartered Accountant. It requires a CA's digital signature and UDIN (Unique Document Identification Number) generated through ICAI. There's no way around this even for a NIL report \u2014 the audit itself is a statutory requirement once a trust crosses the applicability threshold or is applying for 12A/80G, and only a CA can certify it.\n\nSo practically: you'll need a CA at least for the audit report, even if the underlying work is minimal since there were no transactions.\n\n**Backlog filing (2019 to now) and charges**\n\n- Since there's a gap of several years, each year's ITR-7 and Form 10B/10BB (where applicable) generally has to be filed separately for each assessment year, not combined.\n- **Late filing fees**: Section 234F penalty (\u20b91,000\u2013\u20b95,000 depending on the year and whether income exceeded the basic exemption) applies per year if filed after the due date \u2014 though for a NIL-income trust this is often on the lower end or sometimes waived depending on circumstances.\n- **Condonation of delay**: If you're filing return/audit reports for past years beyond the normal time limit, you likely need to apply for **condonation of delay under Section 119(2)(b)** (or the specific circular for delayed Form 10B/10BB, e.g., CBDT circulars periodically extend these) \u2014 this needs to be done before the backlog filings will even be accepted by the portal in some cases.\n- **CA professional fees** (not income tax charges, but their service fee) for NIL audit reports are usually modest since there's no transaction complexity \u2014 but exact fees vary a lot by CA and region, so that's a \"ask a couple of local CAs\" question, not something I can quote precisely.\n- There's no separate \"audit fee\" charged by the Income Tax Department \u2014 the cost you're likely thinking of is the CA's professional fee plus any late filing penalty under 234F.\n\n**Bottom line**: You'll need a CA to sign off on the audit reports (even NIL ones) for each pending year, and likely a condonation-of-delay application before those old years can be filed. The return filing itself you could do yourself, but most people bundle it with the same CA since the audit and return need to reconcile.\n\nSince this involves real penalty calculations and condonation procedure specifics that change with CBDT circulars, it'd be worth a quick search for the current circular before you proceed \u2014 want me to check the latest CBDT guidance on condonation for delayed Form 10B filing?",

                        "type": "text",
                        "text": "This project's files don't cover this specific tax question \u2014 they're just registration/affidavit documents for your trust. Let me answer from general knowledge instead.\n\nHere's the situation, broken into the two things you're asking:\n\n**Can you self-file, or do you need a CA?**\n\nFor a trust, income tax return filing (ITR-7) and the accompanying audit report (Form 10B/10BB) are two different things:\n\n- **The ITR-7 return itself** \u2014 you technically *can* file this yourself if you're comfortable with the income tax portal, since it doesn't legally require a CA.\n- **The audit report (Form 10B or 10BB)** \u2014 this **must** be filed by a Chartered Accountant. It requires a CA's digital signature and UDIN (Unique Document Identification Number) generated through ICAI. There's no way around this even for a NIL report \u2014 the audit itself is a statutory requirement once a trust crosses the applicability threshold or is applying for 12A/80G, and only a CA can certify it.\n\nSo practically: you'll need a CA at least for the audit report, even if the underlying work is minimal since there were no transactions.\n\n**Backlog filing (2019 to now) and charges**\n\n- Since there's a gap of several years, each year's ITR-7 and Form 10B/10BB (where applicable) generally has to be filed separately for each assessment year, not combined.\n- **Late filing fees**: Section 234F penalty (\u20b91,000\u2013\u20b95,000 depending on the year and whether income exceeded the basic exemption) applies per year if filed after the due date \u2014 though for a NIL-income trust this is often on the lower end or sometimes waived depending on circumstances.\n- **Condonation of delay**: If you're filing return/audit reports for past years beyond the normal time limit, you likely need to apply for **condonation of delay under Section 119(2)(b)** (or the specific circular for delayed Form 10B/10BB, e.g., CBDT circulars periodically extend these) \u2014 this needs to be done before the backlog filings will even be accepted by the portal in some cases.\n- **CA professional fees** (not income tax charges, but their service fee) for NIL audit reports are usually modest since there's no transaction complexity \u2014 but exact fees vary a lot by CA and region, so that's a \"ask a couple of local CAs\" question, not something I can quote precisely.\n- There's no separate \"audit fee\" charged by the Income Tax Department \u2014 the cost you're likely thinking of is the CA's professional fee plus any late filing penalty under 234F.\n\n**Bottom line**: You'll need a CA to sign off on the audit reports (even NIL ones) for each pending year, and likely a condonation-of-delay application before those old years can be filed. The return filing itself you could do yourself, but most people bundle it with the same CA since the audit and return need to reconcile.\n\nSince this involves real penalty calculations and condonation procedure specifics that change with CBDT circulars, it'd be worth a quick search for the current circular before you proceed \u2014 want me to check the latest CBDT guidance on condonation for delayed Form 10B filing?",

                    }

3,500\u20137,000 |\n| SiteGround | GoGeek | 3,000\u20135,000 |\n\n**Enterprise-grade** (if you expect high traffic/scale)\n- AWS/GCP with managed WooCommerce setup (via a DevOps partner): \u20b915,000\u201340,000+/month depending on server specs, CDN, and traffic\n- Cloudways + dedicated server: \u20b910,000\u201325,000/month\n\n## Additional Costs to Budget For\n\n- **Domain**: \u20b9800\u20131,500/year\n- **SSL**: Usually free (Let's Encrypt) or \u20b95,000\u201315,000/year for premium/EV SSL (recommended for luxury brand trust)\n- **CDN** (Cloudflare Pro/Business or BunnyCDN): \u20b91,500\u20138,000/month\n- **Backup & security** (Sucuri, Wordfence Premium): \u20b91,500\u20135,000/month\n- **Premium WooCommerce extensions** (payment gateways, inventory, shipping for Pan-India logistics): \u20b95,000\u201320,000/year\n- **Premium theme/page builder**: \u20b93,000\u201315,000 one-time or annual\n\n## Key Considerations for a Pan-India Luxury Store\n\n- **Server location**: Choose a data center in Mumbai (AWS ap-south-1, DigitalOcean Bangalore) for lower latency across India rather than Singapore/US\n- **CDN is essential**: Pan-India delivery needs fast                 "uuid": "019ffb50-1b20-7d80-9682-dcfd266314c3",
                "text": "With \u20b950,000 total (one-time dev + hosting + plugins), here's how that realistically breaks down \u2014 you'll need to be strategic since \u20b950k is tight for a \"luxury-feel\" custom build.\n\n## Realistic Allocation\n\n| Item | Cost (\u20b9) |\n|---|---|\n| Hosting (1 year) | 4,000\u20138,000 |\n| Domain | 800\u20131,200 |\n| Premium theme (luxury-style, e.g. Flatsome, Woodmart) | 3,000\u20135,000 |\n| SSL | Free (Let's Encrypt) |\n| Essential paid plugins (payment gateway, shipping, SEO) | 3,000\u20138,000 |\n| Development (self-build or freelancer) | 25,000\u201335,000 |\n| **Total** | **~40,000\u201350,000** |\n\n## Key Trade-offs at This Budget\n\n**Hosting**: Skip Kinsta/WP Engine \u2014 go with **Hostinger Business/Cloud** or **Cloudways (DO basic)** at \u20b9300\u2013600/month. Perfectly fine for a launch-stage store; you can upgrade later once you have revenue/traffic.\n\n**Development**: This is where \u20b950k gets tight. Your real options:\n- **DIY with a premium theme** (Woodmart, Flatsome, Porto \u2014 \u20b93,000\u20135,000) + drag-and-drop builder (Elementor). This is how most \"luxury-looking\" WooCommerce stores on small budgets are actually built \u2014 the theme does the heavy lifting for visual polish.\n- **Freelancer** (not agency) for setup/customization \u2014 \u20b915,000\u201330,000 for a template-based build. A fully custom design from an agency will blow past \u20b950k easily (agencies typically start at \u20b975k\u20132L+ for custom WooCommerce builds).\n\n**Plugins** \u2014 prioritize only what you truly need:\n- Payment gateway (Razorpay \u2014 free plugin, transaction fees only)\n- WooCommerce Shipping/India-specific shipping plugin (Shiprocket integration \u2014 often free tier available)\n- SEO (Rank Math free version is excellent, skip premium initially)\n- Skip heavy premium plugin bundles at launch\n\n## Honest Advice\n\n\"Luxury feel\" at \u20b950k comes from **design discipline, not budget** \u2014 good typography, whitespace, high-quality product photography, and a clean premium theme will do more for perceived luxury than expensive plugins or hosting. Spend saved money on **professional product photography** instead if you can \u2014 that matters more visually than backend infrastructure at this stage.\n\nWant help picking a specific theme + plugin stack that fits this budget, or a rough week-by-week plan if you're building it yourself?",

                "uuid": "019ffb55-d28d-7344-87c9-328a3e3efb18",
                "text": "Quick sanity check first \u2014 those numbers seem way off for what you're describing. Elementor Pro is typically ~$60-200/year, not 20k. Wordfence and Yoast premium are each roughly $100-130/year. Are those figures in a different currency (like INR or PKR), or are they for multi-year/multi-site licenses? That changes the picture a lot.\n\nAssuming these are just your budget line items (whatever currency), here's what else a real WooCommerce store typically needs:\n\n**Essential**\n- **SSL certificate** \u2014 often free/included with hosting, but confirm\n- **Payment gateway** \u2014 Stripe/PayPal/local gateway; usually free to integrate, but they take a % per transaction (2-3% typical)\n- **A WooCommerce-compatible theme** \u2014 either free (Storefront) or premium (~$50-100 one-time)\n- **Product photography/content** \u2014 cost varies wildly depending on if you DIY or hire\n- **Backup plugin** \u2014 UpdraftPlus or similar (~$70/year premium, or free tier)\n- **Transactional email service** \u2014 WP Mail SMTP or similar so order confirmations don't land in spam (~$50-100/year for a paid tier, or free with limits via Mailgun/SendGrid)\n\n**Often needed depending on your store**\n- Shipping plugin/calculator (depends on carrier \u2014 some are free, some paid)\n- Tax calculation plugin (TaxJar, Avalara, or WooCommerce's built-in \u2014 free to paid)\n- Inventory/stock management extras if you have complex SKUs\n- A caching plugin (WP Rocket ~$59/year, or free alternatives) for site speed\n- GDPR/cookie consent plugin (mostly free)\n\n**One-time, not recurring**\n- Developer/agency setup time if you're not building it yourself\n- Logo/branding\n\n**Ongoing beyond what you listed**\n- Plugin/theme renewal fees (annual, not one-time)\n- Site maintenance/updates if you're not doing it yourself\n\nWant me to sketch out a rough total budget once you clarify the currency/period on those first four numbers?",

                "uuid": "019ffb5e-3909-7e87-9d4a-b2f177ad915d",
                "text": "Got it \u2014 here's the fuller picture, developer-to-developer.\n\n**Email (transactional)**\nDon't rely on Hostinger's default mail for order confirmations \u2014 deliverability is bad. Go with **WP Mail SMTP (free) + Brevo (formerly Sendinblue) free tier** \u2014 300 emails/day free, which covers 5-50 orders/month easily. If it scales, Brevo's paid tier starts around $9-25/month. No need to pay for WP Mail SMTP Pro unless you need advanced routing/logs.\n\n**Tax calculation**\nFor a client at this scale, **use WooCommerce's built-in tax settings** \u2014 don't add an external plugin. Avalara/TaxJar are overkill unless the client sells across multiple states/countries with complex nexus rules (India GST especially \u2014 WooCommerce's native tax classes + manual GST setup handle this fine for most single-country sellers). Only go external if they're crossing into international tax compliance territory later.\n\n**Custom checkout funnel**\nSince you're ditching default WooCommerce flow, you have two paths:\n- **CartFlows** (~$200-300/year for Pro) \u2014 pre-built funnel builder, faster to ship, less flexibility\n- **Fully custom** via Elementor Pro + WooCommerce hooks/custom PHP \u2014 more dev time, but since you already have Elementor Pro, this is likely your better ROI. No extra licensing cost, just your build hours.\n\nGiven you're already deep in Elementor, I'd lean custom-built over CartFlows unless the client wants something turnkey fast.\n\n**Other upfront costs to quote the client**\n\n*Recurring (annual/monthly \u2014 pass through or mark up):*\n- Elementor Pro \u2014 $180/yr\n- Wordfence Premium \u2014 $149/yr\n- Yoast Premium \u2014 $178.80/yr\n- Shiprocket \u2014 ~$2400/yr (starter tier)\n- Hosting/domain \u2014 whatever Hostinger plan\n- Brevo email \u2014 free tier initially\n- Backup plugin \u2014 UpdraftPlus Premium ~$70/yr (don't skip this \u2014 Hostinger backups alone aren't enough for a store with transactional data)\n- SSL \u2014 usually free with Hostinger\n\n*One-time (your dev fee, separate from licenses):*\n- Custom checkout/funnel build\n- Custom shipping calculator logic/integration\n- Theme customization / custom design implementation\n- Product catalog setup & import\n- Payment gateway (Razorpay) integration & testing\n- Staging \u2192 live migration\n- Post-launch QA across devices\n- Client training/handover documentation\n\n*Easy to forget, worth quoting separately:*\n- **Abandoned cart recovery** (built into some email tools, or a plugin like CartFlows/FunnelKit \u2014 helps recoup revenue, good upsell to client)\n- **Order/invoice PDF generation** plugin if they need GST invoices \u2014 free options like PDF Invoices & Packing Slips for WooCommerce\n- **Legal pages** \u2014 privacy policy, refund policy, terms \u2014 templated but need review, especially with GST/e-commerce rules in India\n\nThat should round out your scope of work and pricing sheet.",

                                "text": "     1\t---\n     2\tname: pdf\n     3\tdescription: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.\n     4\tlicense: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms\n     5\t---\n     6\t\n     7\t# PDF Processing Guide\n     8\t\n     9\t## Overview\n    10\t\n    11\tThis guide covers essential PDF processing operations using Python libraries and command-line tools. For advanced features, JavaScript libraries, and detailed examples, see REFERENCE.md. If you need to fill out a PDF form, read FORMS.md and follow its instructions.\n    12\t\n    13\t## Quick Start\n    14\t\n    15\t```python\n    16\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter\n    17\t\n    18\t# Read a PDF\n    19\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n    20\tprint(f\"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}\")\n    21\t\n    22\t# Extract text\n    23\ttext = \"\"\n    24\tfor page in reader.pages:\n    25\t    text += page.extract_text()\n    26\t```\n    27\t\n    28\t## Python Libraries\n    29\t\n    30\t### pypdf - Basic Operations\n    31\t\n    32\t#### Merge PDFs\n    33\t```python\n    34\tfrom pypdf import PdfWriter, PdfReader\n    35\t\n    36\twriter = PdfWriter()\n    37\tfor pdf_file in [\"doc1.pdf\", \"doc2.pdf\", \"doc3.pdf\"]:\n    38\t    reader = PdfReader(pdf_file)\n    39\t    for page in reader.pages:\n    40\t        writer.add_page(page)\n    41\t\n    42\twith open(\"merged.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n    43\t    writer.write(output)\n    44\t```\n    45\t\n    46\t#### Split PDF\n    47\t```python\n    48\treader = PdfReader(\"input.pdf\")\n    49\tfor i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):\n    50\t    writer = PdfWriter()\n    51\t    writer.add_page(page)\n    52\t    with open(f\"page_{i+1}.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n    53\t        writer.write(output)\n    54\t```\n    55\t\n    56\t#### Extract Metadata\n    57\t```python\n    58\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n    59\tmeta = reader.metadata\n    60\tprint(f\"Title: {meta.title}\")\n    61\tprint(f\"Author: {meta.author}\")\n    62\tprint(f\"Subject: {meta.subject}\")\n    63\tprint(f\"Creator: {meta.creator}\")\n    64\t```\n    65\t\n    66\t#### Rotate Pages\n    67\t```python\n    68\treader = PdfReader(\"input.pdf\")\n    69\twriter = PdfWriter()\n    70\t\n    71\tpage = reader.pages[0]\n    72\tpage.rotate(90)  # Rotate 90 degrees clockwise\n    73\twriter.add_page(page)\n    74\t\n    75\twith open(\"rotated.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n    76\t    writer.write(output)\n    77\t```\n    78\t\n    79\t### pdfplumber - Text and Table Extraction\n    80\t\n    81\t#### Extract Text with Layout\n    82\t```python\n    83\timport pdfplumber\n    84\t\n    85\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n    86\t    for page in pdf.pages:\n    87\t        text = page.extract_text()\n    88\t        print(text)\n    89\t```\n    90\t\n    91\t#### Extract Tables\n    92\t```python\n    93\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n    94\t    for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):\n    95\t        tables = page.extract_tables()\n    96\t        for j, table in enumerate(tables):\n    97\t            print(f\"Table {j+1} on page {i+1}:\")\n    98\t            for row in table:\n    99\t                print(row)\n   100\t```\n   101\t\n   102\t#### Advanced Table Extraction\n   103\t```python\n   104\timport pandas as pd\n   105\t\n   106\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n   107\t    all_tables = []\n   108\t    for page in pdf.pages:\n   109\t        tables = page.extract_tables()\n   110\t        for table in tables:\n   111\t            if table:  # Check if table is not empty\n   112\t                df = pd.DataFrame(table[1:], columns=table[0])\n   113\t                all_tables.append(df)\n   114\t\n   115\t# Combine all tables\n   116\tif all_tables:\n   117\t    combined_df = pd.concat(all_tables, ignore_index=True)\n   118\t    combined_df.to_excel(\"extracted_tables.xlsx\", index=False)\n   119\t```\n   120\t\n   121\t### reportlab - Create PDFs\n   122\t\n   123\t#### Basic PDF Creation\n   124\t```python\n   125\tfrom reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter\n   126\tfrom reportlab.pdfgen import canvas\n   127\t\n   128\tc = canvas.Canvas(\"hello.pdf\", pagesize=letter)\n   129\twidth, height = letter\n   130\t\n   131\t# Add text\n   132\tc.drawString(100, height - 100, \"Hello World!\")\n   133\tc.drawString(100, height - 120, \"This is a PDF created with reportlab\")\n   134\t\n   135\t# Add a line\n   136\tc.line(100, height - 140, 400, height - 140)\n   137\t\n   138\t# Save\n   139\tc.save()\n   140\t```\n   141\t\n   142\t#### Create PDF with Multiple Pages\n   143\t```python\n   144\tfrom reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter\n   145\tfrom reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak\n   146\tfrom reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet\n   147\t\n   148\tdoc = SimpleDocTemplate(\"report.pdf\", pagesize=letter)\n   149\tstyles = getSampleStyleSheet()\n   150\tstory = []\n   151\t\n   152\t# Add content\n   153\ttitle = Paragraph(\"Report Title\", styles['Title'])\n   154\tstory.append(title)\n   155\tstory.append(Spacer(1, 12))\n   156\t\n   157\tbody = Paragraph(\"This is the body of the report. \" * 20, styles['Normal'])\n   158\tstory.append(body)\n   159\tstory.append(PageBreak())\n   160\t\n   161\t# Page 2\n   162\tstory.append(Paragraph(\"Page 2\", styles['Heading1']))\n   163\tstory.append(Paragraph(\"Content for page 2\", styles['Normal']))\n   164\t\n   165\t# Build PDF\n   166\tdoc.build(story)\n   167\t```\n   168\t\n   169\t#### Subscripts and Superscripts\n   170\t\n   171\t**IMPORTANT**: Never use Unicode subscript/superscript characters (\u2080\u2081\u2082\u2083\u2084\u2085\u2086\u2087\u2088\u2089, \u2070\u00b9\u00b2\u00b3\u2074\u2075\u2076\u2077\u2078\u2079) in ReportLab PDFs. The built-in fonts do not include these glyphs, causing them to render as solid black boxes.\n   172\t\n   173\tInstead, use ReportLab's XML markup tags in Paragraph objects:\n   174\t```python\n   175\tfrom reportlab.platypus import Paragraph\n   176\tfrom reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet\n   177\t\n   178\tstyles = getSampleStyleSheet()\n   179\t\n   180\t# Subscripts: use <sub> tag\n   181\tchemical = Paragraph(\"H<sub>2</sub>O\", styles['Normal'])\n   182\t\n   183\t# Superscripts: use <super> tag\n   184\tsquared = Paragraph(\"x<super>2</super> + y<super>2</super>\", styles['Normal'])\n   185\t```\n   186\t\n   187\tFor canvas-drawn text (not Paragraph objects), manually adjust font the size and position rather than using Unicode subscripts/superscripts.\n   188\t\n   189\t## Command-Line Tools\n   190\t\n   191\t### pdftotext (poppler-utils)\n   192\t```bash\n   193\t# Extract text\n   194\tpdftotext input.pdf output.txt\n   195\t\n   196\t# Extract text preserving layout\n   197\tpdftotext -layout input.pdf output.txt\n   198\t\n   199\t# Extract specific pages\n   200\tpdftotext -f 1 -l 5 input.pdf output.txt  # Pages 1-5\n   201\t```\n   202\t\n   203\t### qpdf\n   204\t```bash\n   205\t# Merge PDFs\n   206\tqpdf --empty --pages file1.pdf file2.pdf -- merged.pdf\n   207\t\n   208\t# Split pages\n   209\tqpdf input.pdf --pages . 1-5 -- pages1-5.pdf\n   210\tqpdf input.pdf --pages . 6-10 -- pages6-10.pdf\n   211\t\n   212\t# Rotate pages\n   213\tqpdf input.pdf output.pdf --rotate=+90:1  # Rotate page 1 by 90 degrees\n   214\t\n   215\t# Remove password\n   216\tqpdf --password=mypassword --decrypt encrypted.pdf decrypted.pdf\n   217\t```\n   218\t\n   219\t### pdftk (if available)\n   220\t```bash\n   221\t# Merge\n   222\tpdftk file1.pdf file2.pdf cat output merged.pdf\n   223\t\n   224\t# Split\n   225\tpdftk input.pdf burst\n   226\t\n   227\t# Rotate\n   228\tpdftk input.pdf rotate 1east output rotated.pdf\n   229\t```\n   230\t\n   231\t## Common Tasks\n   232\t\n   233\t### Extract Text from Scanned PDFs\n   234\t```python\n   235\t# Requires: pip install pytesseract pdf2image\n   236\timport pytesseract\n   237\tfrom pdf2image import convert_from_path\n   238\t\n   239\t# Convert PDF to images\n   240\timages = convert_from_path('scanned.pdf')\n   241\t\n   242\t# OCR each page\n   243\ttext = \"\"\n   244\tfor i, image in enumerate(images):\n   245\t    text += f\"Page {i+1}:\\n\"\n   246\t    text += pytesseract.image_to_string(image)\n   247\t    text += \"\\n\\n\"\n   248\t\n   249\tprint(text)\n   250\t```\n   251\t\n   252\t### Add Watermark\n   253\t```python\n   254\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter\n   255\t\n   256\t# Create watermark (or load existing)\n   257\twatermark = PdfReader(\"watermark.pdf\").pages[0]\n   258\t\n   259\t# Apply to all pages\n   260\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n   261\twriter = PdfWriter()\n   262\t\n   263\tfor page in reader.pages:\n   264\t    page.merge_page(watermark)\n   265\t    writer.add_page(page)\n   266\t\n   267\twith open(\"watermarked.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n   268\t    writer.write(output)\n   269\t```\n   270\t\n   271\t### Extract Images\n   272\t```bash\n   273\t# Using pdfimages (poppler-utils)\n   274\tpdfimages -j input.pdf output_prefix\n   275\t\n   276\t# This extracts all images as output_prefix-000.jpg, output_prefix-001.jpg, etc.\n   277\t```\n   278\t\n   279\t### Password Protection\n   280\t```python\n   281\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter\n   282\t\n   283\treader = PdfReader(\"input.pdf\")\n   284\twriter = PdfWriter()\n   285\t\n   286\tfor page in reader.pages:\n   287\t    writer.add_page(page)\n   288\t\n   289\t# Add password\n   290\twriter.encrypt(\"userpassword\", \"ownerpassword\")\n   291\t\n   292\twith open(\"encrypted.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n   293\t    writer.write(output)\n   294\t```\n   295\t\n   296\t## Quick Reference\n   297\t\n   298\t| Task | Best Tool | Command/Code |\n   299\t|------|-----------|--------------|\n   300\t| Merge PDFs | pypdf | `writer.add_page(page)` |\n   301\t| Split                                 "text": "- Born: 1929\n- Origin: Hyderabad, Telangana, India\n- Died: 25 June 2015 (aged 85\u201386) Hyderabad\n- Genres: Ghazals\n- Occupation: singer\n- Years active: 1920s \u2013 2015\n\nVithal Rao Aatmaram Shivpurkar also known as Pandit Vithal Rao (1929 \u2013 25 June 2015) was an Indian classical vocalist.\n[[1]](./Vithal_Rao#cite_note-1) He is considered to have been one of the last few maestros of 'Ghazals' and was the last court singer of the [Last Nizam of Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osman_Ali_Khan). He is popular with the noble families of Hyderabad. Among his notable accompanists include Ustad Sardar Khan (tabla).\n\n\nSome of his notable disciples include Kiran Ahluwalia, playback and folk singer\n[Rahul Sipligunj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahul_Sipligunj), and ghazal and qawwali singer [Chetan Ramlu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chetan_Ramlu).\nSome his popular ghazals are:\n- Ek chamele ke mandve tale\n- Maine teri aaakho mein pada, sab bhool gaya bus yaad raha sirf Allah hi Allah (Sufiana Kalam)\n- Aye mere ham nasheen\n- Nindiya Na Aaye\n- O Sitamgar Tera Muskurana Kaam Aane Ke Qabil Nahin Hai\n- Zehal-e miskin makun taghaful, duraye naina banaye batiyan\n[[3]](./Vithal_Rao#cite_note-3)\n- Ghazals of Janab Sayeed Shaheedi\n[\u2191](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vithal_Rao#cite_ref-1) [\"Legendary Ghazal singer Vithal Rao dead\"](http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/legendary-ghazal-singer-vithal-rao-dead/article7358221.ece).                                 "is_missing": false,
                                "text": "- Born: Vrajlal Kalidas Shastri 26 November 1825 Malataj, Petlad, Gujarat\n- Died: 14 November 1892 (aged 66)\n- Occupation: philologist, poet, scholar, translator\n- Language: Gujarati\n- Nationality: Indian\n- Notable works: Gujarati Bhashano Itihas (1866); Utsargmala (1870); Dhatusangrah (1870); Gurjar Bhasha Prakash (1892);\n\nVrajlal Kalidas Shastri (26 November 1825 \u2013 14 November 1892) was a pioneer of\n[philology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philology) in [Gujarati language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarati_language) and writer who wrote books on Gujarati language. [[2]](./Vrajlal_Shastri#cite_note-Lal1992-2) [[3]](./Vrajlal_Shastri#cite_note-Sebeok1972-3)\nHe was born on 26 November 1825 in Malataj, a village in\n[Petlad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petlad), [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat). He took his primary education in his village Malataj. [[1]](./Vrajlal_Shastri#cite_note-vs-1) He had studied Sanskrit poetry and grammar in Sanskrit pathshalas. \n\nHe also studied [Prakrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prakrit_language) grammar and literature. He taught Sanskrit at Jain Mandir, [Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad). Due to Jain religious books, he became familiar with Prakrit- [Pali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pali), [Apabhramsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apabhramsa), [Ardha Magadhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magadhi_Prakrit) so he wrote books on philology of Gujarati. He worked with [Gujarat Vernacular Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Vidhya_Sabha) and Dharma Sabha and edited their two journals, [Buddhiprakash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhiprakash) and Dharmaprakash. He had a long career of twenty five years as a researcher and scholar. [[2]](./Vrajlal_Shastri#cite_note-Lal1992-2) [[4]](./Vrajlal_Shastri#cite_note-Mukherjee1998-4)\nHe died on 14 November 1892.\n[[1]](./Vrajlal_Shastri#cite_note-vs-1)\nHe had written fifteen books. \n\nHis books on Gujarati language include Gujarati Bhashano Iti",
