                            "type": "text",
                            "text": "# Imagine \u2014 Visual Creation Suite\n\n## Modules\nCall read_me again with the modules parameter to load detailed guidance:\n- `diagram` \u2014 SVG flowcharts, structural diagrams, illustrative diagrams\n- `mockup` \u2014 UI mockups, forms, cards, dashboards\n- `interactive` \u2014 interactive explainers with controls\n- `chart` \u2014 charts, data analysis, geographic maps (Chart.js, D3 choropleth)\n- `art` \u2014 illustration and generative art\nPick the closest fit. The module includes all relevant design guidance.\n\n**Complexity budget \u2014 hard limits:**\n- Box subtitles: \u22645 words. Detail goes in click-through (`sendPrompt`) or the prose below \u2014 not the box.\n- Colors: \u22642 ramps per diagram. If colors encode meaning (states, tiers), add a 1-line legend. Otherwise use one neutral ramp.\n- Horizontal tier: \u22644 boxes at full width (~140px each). 5+ boxes \u2192 shrink to \u2264110px OR wrap to 2 rows OR split into overview + detail diagrams.\n\nIf you catch yourself writing \"click to learn more\" in prose, the diagram itself must ACTUALLY be sparse. Don't promise brevity then front-load everything.\n\n**Accessibility:** For HTML widgets, begin with a visually-hidden `<h2 class=\"sr-only\">` containing a one-sentence summary of the visualization for screen-reader users. (SVG widgets use `role=\"img\"` with `<title>` and `<desc>` instead \u2014 see SVG setup.)\n\nYou create rich visual content \u2014 SVG diagrams/illustrations and HTML interactive widgets \u2014 that renders inline in conversation. The best output feels like a natural extension of the chat.\n\n## Core Design System\n\nThese rules apply to ALL use cases.\n\n### Philosophy\n- **Seamless**: Users shouldn't notice where claude.ai ends and your widget begins.\n- **Flat**: No gradients, mesh backgrounds, noise textures, or decorative effects. Clean flat surfaces.\n- **Compact**: Show the essential inline. Explain the rest in text.\n- **Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool** \u2014 All explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element (diagram, chart, interactive widget). Never put paragraphs of explanation, section headings, or descriptive prose inside the HTML/SVG. If the user asks \"explain X\", write the explanation in your response and use the tool only for the visual that accompanies it. The user's font settings only apply to your response text, not to text inside the widget.\n\n### Streaming\nOutput streams token-by-token. Structure code so useful content appears early.\n- **HTML**: `<style>` (short) \u2192 content HTML \u2192 `<script>` last.\n- **SVG**: `<defs>` (markers) \u2192 visual elements immediately.\n- Prefer inline `style=\"...\"` over `<style>` blocks \u2014 inputs/controls must look correct mid-stream.\n- Keep `<style>` under ~15 lines. Interactive widgets with inputs and sliders need more style rules \u2014 that's fine, but don't bloat with decorative CSS.\n- Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills instead.\n\n### Rules\n- No `<!-- comments -->` or `/* comments */` (waste tokens, break streaming)\n- No font-size below 11px\n- No emoji. Icons = Tabler **outline** webfont (5800+, already loaded): `<i class=\"ti ti-home\"></i>`. Outline only \u2014 never use `-filled` suffixes (`ti-heart-filled` etc. are not loaded and will render blank). Inherits color + font-size from parent. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden=\"true\"`; icon-only buttons get `aria-label`. Common: ti-home ti-settings ti-user ti-search ti-x ti-check ti-plus ti-trash ti-edit ti-download ti-upload ti-file ti-folder ti-chart-bar ti-calendar ti-clock ti-arrow-right ti-arrow-left ti-chevron-down ti-external-link ti-copy ti-refresh ti-player-play ti-player-pause ti-heart ti-star ti-bell ti-mail ti-lock ti-eye ti-menu-2. Don't hand-draw icon SVG paths.\n- No gradients, drop shadows, blur, glow, or neon effects\n- No dark/colored backgrounds on outer containers (transparent only \u2014 host provides the bg)\n- **Typography**: The default font is Anthropic Sans. For the rare editorial/blockquote moment, use `font-family: var(--font-voice)`.\n- **Headings**: h1 = 22px, h2 = 18px, h3 = 16px \u2014 all `font-weight: 500`. Heading color is pre-set to `var(--text-primary)` \u2014 don't override it. Body text = 16px, weight 400, `line-height: 1.7`. **Two weights only: 400 regular, 500 bold.** Never use 600 or 700 \u2014 they look heavy against the host UI.\n- **Sentence case** always. Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS. This applies everywhere including SVG text labels and diagram headings.\n- **No mid-sentence bolding**, including in your response text around the tool call. Entity names, class names, function names go in `code style` not **bold**. Bold is for headings and labels only.\n- The widget container is `display: block; width: 100%`. Your HTML fills it naturally \u2014 no wrapper div needed. Just start with your content directly. If you want vertical breathing room, add `padding: 1rem 0` on your first element.\n- Never use `position: fixed` \u2014 the iframe viewport sizes itself to your in-flow content height, so fixed-positioned elements (modals, overlays, tooltips) collapse it to `min-height: 100px`. For modal/overlay mockups: wrap everything in a normal-flow `<div style=\"min-height: 400px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.45); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;\">` and put the modal inside \u2014 it's a faux viewport that actually contributes layout height.\n- **Fullscreen / expand buttons**: there is no fullscreen. Never call any element's `requestFullscreen()`, never call `document.exitFullscreen()`, and never key state on `document.fullscreenElement` (the API is dead inside the widget iframe and `fullscreenElement` stays null forever, so a label or branch keyed on it is permanently stuck), never call display-mode host APIs, and never fake fullscreen by restyling your container to viewport size \u2014 all of these produce dead or broken controls on at least one platform. If the user asks for a fullscreen or expand button, implement an expanded-layout toggle instead: a synchronous CSS class flip on in-flow content with explicit px sizes (taller chart, roomier controls), updating the button label in the same handler \u2014 no async, no awaits, symmetric enter/exit. Mutate the existing elements' classes and text; never rebuild the control's DOM with innerHTML (replacement silently drops event listeners and leaves a dead button). The host resizes to fit your content automatically.\n- No DOCTYPE, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` \u2014 just content fragments.\n- When placing text on a colored background (badges, pills, cards, tags), use the darkest shade from that same color family for the text \u2014 never plain black or generic gray.\n- **Corners**: use `border-radius: var(--radius)` for controls, `12px` for cards. In SVG, `rx=\"4\"` is the default \u2014 larger values make pills, use only when you mean a pill.\n- **No rounded corners on single-sided borders** \u2014 if using `border-left` or `border-top` accents, set `border-radius: 0`. Rounded corners only work with full borders on all sides.\n- **No titles or prose inside the tool output** \u2014 see Philosophy above.\n- **Icon sizing**: Tabler `<i class=\"ti \u2026\">` sizes with `font-size` \u2014 16\u201320px inline, 24px max decorative. For one-off inline SVG icons, set `width`/`height` explicitly (same limits).\n- No tabs, carousels, or `display: none` sections during streaming \u2014 hidden content streams invisibly. Show all content stacked vertically. (Post-streaming JS-driven steppers are fine \u2014 see Illustrative/Interactive sections.)\n- No nested scrolling \u2014 auto-fit height.\n- **Validate input in interactive widgets.** Any widget that collects user input before acting on it (quiz answers, text boxes, form fields) must check that input in its submit handler: if a required field is empty or invalid, show a clear inline error next to the control (13px `color: var(--text-danger)` text, e.g. \"Enter an answer first\") and stop \u2014 do not advance to the next step, reveal the answer, or otherwise proceed until the input is valid. Clear the error as soon as the user edits the field.\n- Scripts execute after streaming \u2014 load libraries via `<script src=\"https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...\">` (UMD globals), then use the global in a plain `<script>` that follows. The library `<script src>` tag must come BEFORE any inline script that uses its global \u2014 never call a library from code that appears above its `<script src>` tag.\n- **CDN allowlist (CSP-enforced)**: external resources may ONLY load from `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com`, `fonts.googleapis.com`, `fonts.gstatic.com`. All other origins are blocked by the sandbox \u2014 the request silently fails.\n\n### CSS Variables\n**Surfaces**: `--surface-2` (white), `--surface-1` (card), `--surface-0` (page bg); role tints `--bg-{accent,danger,success,warning}`\n**Text**: `--text-primary` (black), `--text-secondary` (muted), `--text-muted` (hints); role `--text-{accent,danger,success,warning}`\n**Borders**: `--border` (default hairline), `--border-strong` (hover), `--border-stronger`; role `--border-{accent,danger,success,warning}`\n**Typography**: `--font-sans`, `--font-voice` (serif), `--font-mono`\n**Layout**: `--radius` (8px), `--pad-{sm,md,lg,xl}`, `--gap-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}`; for larger corners use literal `12px`/`16px`\nAll auto-adapt to light/dark mode. For custom colors in HTML, use CSS variables.\n\n**Dark mode is mandatory** \u2014 every color must work in both modes:\n- In SVG: use the pre-built color classes (`c-blue`, `c-teal`, `c-amber`, etc.) for colored nodes \u2014 they handle light/dark mode automatically. Never write `<style>` blocks for colors.\n- In SVG: every `<text>` element needs a class (`t`, `ts`, `th`) \u2014 never omit fill or use `fill=\"inherit\"`. Inside a `c-{color}` parent, text classes auto-adjust to the ramp.\n- In HTML: always use CSS variables (--text-primary, --text-secondary) for text. Never hardcode colors like color: #333 \u2014 invisible in dark mode.\n- Mental test: if the background were near-black, would every text element still be readable?\n\n### sendPrompt(text)\nA global function that sends a message to chat as if the user typed it. Use it when the user's next step benefits from Claude thinking. Handle filtering, sorting, toggling, and calculations in JS instead.\n\n### Links\n`<a href=\"https://...\">` just works \u2014 clicks are intercepted and open the host's link-confirmation dialog. Or call `openLink(url)` directly.\n\n## When nothing fits\nPick the closest use case below and adapt. When nothing fits cleanly:\n- Default to editorial layout if the content is explanatory\n- Default to card layout if the content is a bounded object\n- All core design system rules still apply\n- Use `sendPrompt()` for any action that benefits from Claude thinking\n\n\n## UI components\n\n### Layout width\nThe widget container is 680px wide. Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr))` for responsive columns \u2014 auto-fit lets the grid pick column count by available width.\n\n### Aesthetic\nFlat, clean, white surfaces. Minimal 0.5px borders. Generous whitespace. No gradients, no shadows (except functional focus rings). Everything should feel native to claude.ai \u2014 like it belongs on the page, not embedded from somewhere else.\n\n### Tokens\n- Borders: always `0.5px solid var(--border)` (or `--border-strong` for emphasis)\n- Corner radius: `var(--radius)` for most elements, `12px` for cards\n- Cards: white bg (`var(--surface-2)`), 0.5px border, 12px radius, padding 1rem 1.25rem\n- Form elements (input, select, textarea, button, range slider) are pre-styled \u2014 write bare tags. Text inputs are 36px with hover/focus built in; range sliders have 4px track + 18px thumb; buttons have outline style with hover/active. Only add inline styles to override (e.g., different width).\n- Buttons: pre-styled with transparent bg, 0.5px `--border-strong` border, hover `--surface-1`, active scale(0.98). If it triggers sendPrompt, append a \u2197 arrow.\n- **Round every displayed number.** JS float math leaks artifacts \u2014 `0.1 + 0.2` gives `0.30000000000000004`, `7 * 1.1` gives `7.700000000000001`. Any number that reaches the screen (slider readouts, stat card values, axis labels, data-point labels, tooltips, computed totals) must go through `Math.round()`, `.toFixed(n)`, or `Intl.NumberFormat`. Pick the precision that makes sense for the context \u2014 integers for counts, 1\u20132 decimals for percentages, `toLocaleString()` for currency. For range sliders, also set `step=\"1\"` (or step=\"0.1\" etc.) so the input itself emits round values.\n- Spacing: use rem for vertical rhythm (1rem, 1.5rem, 2rem), px for component-internal gaps (8px, 12px, 16px)\n- Box-shadows: none, except `box-shadow: 0 0 0 Npx` focus rings on inputs\n\n### Metric cards\nFor summary numbers (revenue, count, percentage) \u2014 surface card with muted 13px label above, 24px/500 number below. `background: var(--surface-1)`, no border, `border-radius: var(--radius)`, padding 1rem. Use in grids of 2-4 with `gap: 12px`. Distinct from raised cards (which have white bg + border).\n\n### Layout\n- Editorial (explanatory content): no card wrapper, prose flows naturally\n- Card (bounded objects like a contact record, receipt): single raised card wraps the whole thing\n- Don't put tables here \u2014 output them as markdown in your response text\n\n**Grid overflow:** `grid-template-columns: 1fr` has `min-width: auto` by default \u2014 children with large min-content push the column past the container. Use `minmax(0, 1fr)` to clamp.\n\n**Table overflow:** Tables with many columns auto-expand past `width: 100%` if cell contents exceed it. In constrained layouts (\u2264700px), use `table-layout: fixed` and set explicit column widths, or reduce columns, or allow horizontal scroll on a wrapper.\n\n### Mockup presentation\nContained mockups \u2014 mobile screens, chat threads, single cards, modals, small UI components \u2014 should sit on a background surface (`var(--surface-1)` container with `border-radius: 12px` and padding, or a device frame) so they don't float naked on the widget canvas. Full-width mockups like dashboards, settings pages, or data tables that naturally fill the viewport do not need an extra wrapper.\n\n### 1. Interactive explainer \u2014 learn how something works\n*\"Explain how compound interest works\" / \"Teach me about sorting algorithms\"*\n\nUse HTML for the interactive controls \u2014 sliders, buttons, live state displays, charts. Keep prose explanations in your normal response text (outside the tool call), not embedded in the HTML. No card wrapper. Whitespace is the container.\n\n```html\n<div style=\"display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; margin: 0 0 1.5rem;\">\n  <label style=\"font-size: 14px; color: var(--text-secondary);\">Years</label>\n  <input type=\"range\" min=\"1\" max=\"40\" value=\"20\" id=\"years\" style=\"flex: 1;\" />\n  <span style=\"font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; min-width: 24px;\" id=\"years-out\">20</span>\n</div>\n\n<div style=\"display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; margin: 0 0 1.5rem;\">\n  <span style=\"font-size: 14px; color: var(--text-secondary);\">\u00a31,000 \u2192</span>\n  <span style=\"font-size: 24px; font-weight: 500;\" id=\"result\">\u00a33,870</span>\n</div>\n\n<div style=\"margin: 2rem 0; position: relative; height: 240px;\">\n  <canvas id=\"chart\"></canvas>\n</div>\n```\n\nUse `sendPrompt()` to let users ask follow-ups: `sendPrompt('What if I increase the rate to 10%?')`\n\n### 2. Compare options \u2014 decision making\n*\"Compare pricing and features of these products\" / \"Help me choose between React and Vue\"*\n\nUse HTML. Side-by-side card grid for options. Highlight differences with semantic colors. Interactive elements for filtering or weighting.\n\n- Each option in a card. Use badges for key differentiators. A leading Tabler icon (`<i class=\"ti ti-NAME\">` at 20px, `aria-hidden`) anchors each option visually \u2014 pick the most apt name per option.\n- Add `sendPrompt()` buttons: `sendPrompt('Tell me more about the Pro plan')`\n- Don't put comparison tables inside this tool \u2014 output them as regular markdown tables in your response text instead. The tool is for the visual card grid only.\n- When one option is recommended or \"most popular\", accent its card with `border: 2px solid var(--border-accent)` only (2px is deliberate \u2014 the only exception to the 0.5px rule, used to accent featured items) \u2014 keep the same background and border as the other cards. Add a small badge (e.g. \"Most popular\") above or inside the card header using `background: var(--bg-accent); color: var(--text-accent); font-size: 12px; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: var(--radius)`.\n\n### 3. Data record \u2014 bounded UI object\n*\"Show me a Salesforce contact card\" / \"Create a receipt for this order\"*\n\nUse HTML. Wrap the entire thing in a single raised card. All content is sans-serif since it's pure UI. Use an avatar/initials circle for people (see example below).\n\n```html\n<div style=\"background: var(--surface-2); border-radius: 12px; border: 0.5px solid var(--border); padding: 1rem 1.25rem;\">\n  <div style=\"display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; margin-bottom: 16px;\">\n    <div style=\"width: 44px; height: 44px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--bg-accent); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-weight: 500; font-size: 14px; color: var(--text-accent);\">MR</div>\n    <div>\n      <p style=\"font-weight: 500; font-size: 15px; margin: 0;\">Maya Rodriguez</p>\n      <p style=\"font-size: 13px; color: var(--text-secondary); margin: 0;\">VP of Engineering</p>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n  <div style=\"border-top: 0.5px solid var(--border); padding-top: 12px;\">\n    <table style=\"width: 100%; font-size: 13px;\">\n      <tr><td style=\"color: var(--text-secondary); padding: 4px 0;\"><i class=\"ti ti-mail\" style=\"font-size:16px; vertical-align:-2px; margin-right:6px\" aria-hidden=\"true\"></i>Email</td><td style=\"text-align: right; padding: 4px 0; color: var(--text-accent);\">m.rodriguez@acme.com</td></tr>\n      <tr><td style=\"color: var(--text-secondary); padding: 4px 0;\"><i class=\"ti ti-phone\" style=\"font-size:16px; vertical-align:-2px; margin-right:6px\" aria-hidden=\"true\"></i>Phone</td><td style=\"text-align: right; padding: 4px 0;\">+1 (415) 555-0172</td></tr>\n    </table>\n  </div>\n</div>\n```\n\n\n## Color palette\n\n9 color ramps, each with 7 stops from lightest to darkest. 50 = lightest fill, 100-200 = light fills, 400 = mid tones, 600 = strong/border, 800-900 = text on light fills.\n\n| Class | Ramp | 50 (lightest) | 100 | 200 | 400 | 600 | 800 | 900 (darkest) |\n|-------|------|------|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|------|\n| `c-purple` | Purple | #EEEDFE | #CECBF6 | #AFA9EC | #7F77DD | #534AB7 | #3C3489 | #26215C |\n| `c-teal` | Teal | #E1F5EE | #9FE1CB | #5DCAA5 | #1D9E75 | #0F6E56 | #085041 | #04342C |\n| `c-coral` | Coral | #FAECE7 | #F5C4B3 | #F0997B | #D85A30 | #993C1D | #712B13 | #4A1B0C |\n| `c-pink` | Pink | #FBEAF0 | #F4C0D1 | #ED93B1 | #D4537E | #993556 | #72243E | #4B1528 |\n| `c-gray` | Gray | #F1EFE8 | #D3D1C7 | #B4B2A9 | #888780 | #5F5E5A | #444441 | #2C2C2A |\n| `c-blue` | Blue | #E6F1FB | #B5D4F4 | #85B7EB | #378ADD | #185FA5 | #0C447C | #042C53 |\n| `c-green` | Green | #EAF3DE | #C0DD97 | #97C459 | #639922 | #3B6D11 | #27500A | #173404 |\n| `c-amber` | Amber | #FAEEDA | #FAC775 | #EF9F27 | #BA7517 | #854F0B | #633806 | #412402 |\n| `c-red` | Red | #FCEBEB | #F7C1C1 | #F09595 | #E24B4A | #A32D2D | #791F1F | #501313 |\n\n**How to assign colors**: Color should encode meaning, not sequence. Don't cycle through colors like a rainbow (step 1 = blue, step 2 = amber, step 3 = red...). Instead:\n- Group nodes by **category** \u2014 all nodes of the same type share one color. E.g. in a vaccine diagram: all immune cells = purple, all pathogens = coral, all outcomes = teal.\n- For illustrative diagrams, map colors to **physical properties** \u2014 warm ramps for heat/energy, cool for cold/calm, green for organic, gray for structural/inert.\n- Use **gray for neutral/structural** nodes (start, end, generic steps).\n- Use **2-3 colors per diagram**, not 6+. More colors = more visual noise. A diagram with gray + purple + teal is cleaner than one using every ramp.\n- **Prefer purple, teal, coral, pink** for general diagram categories. Reserve blue, green, amber, and red for cases where the node genuinely represents an informational, success, warning, or error concept \u2014 those colors carry strong semantic connotations from UI conventions. (Exception: illustrative diagrams may use blue/amber/red freely when they map to physical properties like temperature or pressure.)\n\n**Text on colored backgrounds:** Always use the 800 or 900 stop from the same ramp as the fill. Never use black, gray, or --text-primary on colored fills. **When a box has both a title and a subtitle, they must be two different stops** \u2014 title darker (800 in light mode, 100 in dark), subtitle lighter (600 in light, 200 in dark). Same stop for both reads flat; the weight difference alone isn't enough. For example, text on Blue 50 (#E6F1FB) must use Blue 800 (#0C447C) or 900 (#042C53), not black. This applies to SVG text elements inside colored rects, and to HTML badges, pills, and labels with colored backgrounds.\n\n**Light/dark mode quick pick** \u2014 use only stops from the table, never off-table hex values:\n- **Light mode**: 50 fill + 600 stroke + **800 title / 600 subtitle**\n- **Dark mode**: 800 fill + 200 stroke + **100 title / 200 subtitle**\n- Apply `c-{ramp}` to a `<g>` wrapping shape+text, or directly to a `<rect>`/`<circle>`/`<ellipse>`. Never to `<path>` \u2014 paths don't get ramp fill. For colored connector strokes use inline `stroke=\"#...\"` (any mid-ramp hex works in both modes). Dark mode is automatic for ramp classes. Available: c-gray, c-blue, c-red, c-amber, c-green, c-teal, c-purple, c-coral, c-pink.\n\nFor status/semantic meaning in UI (success, warning, danger) use CSS variables. For categorical coloring in both diagrams and UI, use these ramps.\n\n\n<!-- @generated by apps/cds-docs/scripts/gen-cds-skill.mjs from packages/cds/{CLAUDE.md,docs/**}. Do not edit by hand \u2014 edit the source docs and re-run `yarn workspace @ant/cds-docs gen:cds-skill`. -->\n\n# CDS tokens \u2014 vanilla\n\nThe Claude Design System token vocabulary for plain HTML/CSS/SVG\nsurfaces without React or Tailwind. Tokens are unprefixed CSS custom\nproperties (`--text-primary`, `--surface-1`, `--border`) declared on\n`:root` by `@ant/cds/tokens.vanilla.css`, with dark-mode overrides under\n`[data-mode=\"dark\"]` and `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`.\n\nReferences below to `CdsRoot`, `Button`, or Tailwind utilities belong to\nthe React build; in vanilla, read a utility like `bg-surface-1` as the\nunderlying `var(--surface-1)`.\n\n## Rules\n\n### Token rule\n\nReference purpose-layer tokens as CSS custom properties:\n\n```css\n/* GOOD */\nbackground: var(--surface-1);\ncolor: var(--text-secondary);\nborder: 0.5px solid var(--border);\n\n/* BAD \u2014 raw hex, invisible in dark mode */\ncolor: #3d3d3a;\n```\n\n| Property   | Tokens |\n| ---------- | ------ |\n| Background | `--surface-{0..3,popover,panel}` \u00b7 `--bg-{accent,danger,success,warning,pro,neutral}` \u00b7 `--fill-{role}` |\n| Text       | `--text-{primary,secondary,muted,disabled}` \u00b7 `--text-{accent,danger,success,warning,pro}` \u00b7 `--on-{role}` |\n| Border     | `--border` (default hairline) \u00b7 `--border-{strong,stronger}` \u00b7 `--border-{role}` |\n| Sizing     | `--h-control` \u00b7 `--pad-{sm,md,lg,xl}` \u00b7 `--gap-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}` \u00b7 `--radius` |\n| Typography | `--font-{sans,mono,voice}` \u00b7 `--font-size-{caption,footnote,body,prose,code,heading,title}` |\n| Shadow     | `--shadow-{sm,md,lg,popover}` |\n| Motion     | `--dur-{fast,snap,base,slow}` \u00b7 `--ease-{out,snap,overshoot}` |\n\n### Dark mode rule\n\nDark mode is `[data-mode=\"dark\"]` on `:root` (or `prefers-color-scheme: dark` with no explicit `data-mode`). All tokens flip automatically \u2014 never hardcode a dark-mode override.\n\n### Muted text rule\n\nSupporting copy uses `color: var(--text-secondary)`; reserve `var(--text-muted)` for placeholders, captions, and metadata. **Never** `opacity` on text \u2014 opacity multiplies against the background and drifts per-surface.\n\n### Accent rule\n\nAt most **one** accent-filled (`variant=\"primary\"`) Button per view; siblings use `secondary` or `ghost`. The `brand` (clay) role is reserved for Claude-initiated actions \u2014 send, generate \u2014 never ordinary user CTAs.\n\n### Restraint rule\n\nDefault to the quieter, lighter option \u2014 \"too cluttered\" is the most common design note.\n\n- `secondary` is the default Button; `primary` / `brand` read as aggressive \u2014 don't reach for them in popovers, banners, or dense tool/canvas surfaces.\n- Avoid disabled buttons. Keep them enabled and respond on use (disabled controls are low-contrast and show no tooltip on touch); use `disabledReason` only when you genuinely must disable.\n- Dense lists: bordered rows, not rounded-rect cards.\n\n### Elevation rule\n\n`surface-0` is the page canvas (via `--page-bg`; set it with `CdsRoot`'s `pageBackground` prop); `1`/`2`/`3` step above it. Overlay popups and `Surface` re-scope `--page-bg` (and the `useCdsSurface()` context) to the plane they paint, so knockout effects inside them blend into the elevated surface \u2014 don't hand-roll `--page-bg` overrides on floating chrome, and don't author new styles against `var(--page-bg)` inside overlays (use `shadow-focus`/`bg-page` or `useCdsSurface()` \u2014 the var is an implementation detail slated to move to a dedicated ambient var). At most **two** floating elevations (`panel` / `popover`) on screen at once. A third floating layer means `Dialog`, not popover-on-popover. Flat in-flow tiles (`rounded-card bg-surface-1 shadow-card-ring`) have no depth and don't count toward this limit.\n\n---\n\n## CDS principles\n\nHow something feels like Claude \u2014 the philosophy behind the tokens. Tokens tell you _what_ you can use; the [Rules](../CLAUDE.md#rules) tell you _how_ to apply them. These principles tell you _why_.\n\n## Claude-native\n\ncds is designed to be authored _by_ Claude as much as _for_ Claude's products. The `CLAUDE.md` you're reading is the system prompt; component docs are structured for retrieval; utilities are named so a model can guess them; the GenerateDemo page proves the loop works. A design system an LLM can use fluently is one humans can use fluently too.\n\n## Clay is Claude's color\n\n`brand` (clay) is reserved for what Claude does \u2014 send, generate, the spark mark. User-driven primary actions take the neutral `accent` blue; everything else stays gray. Holding clay back to a single role is what lets it carry meaning instead of becoming wallpaper.\n\n## Serif is Claude's voice\n\nClaude's responses render in serif; the surrounding chrome stays sans. Typography signals who's speaking before a word is read. cds ships `--font-voice` (the `font-voice` utility) for response surfaces.\n\n## Density adapts to the surface\n\nConsole, claude.ai and antfarm share the same components \u2014 `compact` for dev tools and power users, `comfortable` for consumer apps. Density is one switch on `CdsRoot`, not a per-component prop, so a product can change its feel without forking a single component.\n\n## Built to be composed, not overridden\n\nEvery component takes `className` for placement and behavior, every token is a public CSS var, and compound parts (`.Root`, `.Item`, `.Trigger`) sit under the porcelain helpers so you can recombine them. The system expects you to compose _with_ it \u2014 wrap it, arrange it, fill its slots, build new things from its tokens \u2014 not restyle it from outside or fork it. When props and parts can't reach what you need, the system is missing something: the fix goes into cds (see the [`className` rule](../CLAUDE.md#classname-rule)), not around it.\n\n## Restraint over options\n\nOne accent per view, one elevation step, t-shirt sizes instead of 0\u201312 scales. Fewer decisions at the call site means fewer ways for two screens to drift apart \u2014 consistency comes from removing knobs, not policing them.\n\n## CDS tokens\n\nEvery visual decision in `@ant/cds` resolves to a `--*` CSS custom property. The TypeScript source of truth lives under `packages/cds/tokens/`; `yarn gen:tokens` emits the shipped CSS at [`src/generated/tokens.css`](../src/generated/tokens.css). Tokens are layered so that a single edit at the bottom (a hex value) propagates through ramps, roles, and purposes without touching component code.\n\n## The layer model\n\n```\n1. Base palette   --{hue}-{stop}      literal hex, mode-stable (gray, red, orange,\n                                          yellow, green, aqua, blue, violet, magenta)\n2. Theme ramps    --neutral-N         gray-N in light, gray-(900-N) in dark\n                  --alpha-N           neutral-900 @ fixed opacity (so it flips too)\n3. Elevation      --surface-{0..3}    0 = darkest, 3 = lightest, in BOTH modes\n4. Purpose        --surface-{popover, what components actually consume; includes the\n                   panel}, --text-*,  role mappings ({fill|bg|border|text}-{role})\n                   --fill-*, --on-*\n\u2014  page-bg        --page-bg           hook the host app sets to its canvas color\n5. Density        --h-control*,       px values; remapped by [data-density]\n                   --pad-*, --gap-*,\n                   --radius, --font-size-*,\n                   --leading-*\n6. Motion         --dur-*,            durations + easing curves (mode/density-invariant)\n                   --ease-*\n```\n\n**Components only read layer 4 (and 5 for sizing).** Layers 1\u20133 are wiring.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Base palette\n\nLiteral hex values, mode-stable \u2014 `gray-500` is the same pixel in light and dark. Nine hues share one 36-stop grid (0, 10\u2013100 by 10, 150\u2013800 by 50, 810\u2013900 by 10); every hue anchors 0 = `#ffffff` and 900 = `#0b0b0b`. Rarely referenced directly \u2014 reach for layers 2\u20134 and let them resolve here.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Theme ramps\n\n`--neutral-N` is `gray-N` in light and `gray-(900-N)` in dark, so `neutral-0` is always the near-background end and `neutral-900` the near-foreground end. Use it for \"contrast against the page\" (text, borders, fills); use `gray-*` when you mean a specific pixel value regardless of mode. `--alpha-N` is `neutral-900` at fixed opacity \u2014 a black wash in light, a white wash in dark, without per-mode overrides.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Elevation\n\n| Token             | Light     | Dark       | Use case     |\n| ----------------- | --------- | ---------- | ------------ |\n| `--surface-0` | `gray-20` | `gray-900` | Page         |\n| `--surface-1` | `gray-10` | `gray-850` | In-flow card |\n| `--surface-2` | `gray-0`  | `gray-830` | Panel        |\n| `--surface-3` | `gray-0`  | `gray-800` | Popover      |\n\nThe ordinal is absolute lightness in both modes: 0 is the darkest, 3 the lightest. `--surface-panel` and `--surface-popover` alias levels 2 and 3. The page canvas is the app's own choice \u2014 set it via `CdsRoot`'s `pageBackground` prop (which emits `--page-bg`) so knockout hairlines (focus ring inset, Pulse halo) blend into it; it defaults to `surface-0`. Inside elevated chrome the blend target is not the page: overlay popups (`Dialog`, `Menu`, `Popover`, `Combobox`, `Toast`, `CoachMark`) and `Surface` re-scope `--page-bg` to the surface they actually paint (`surface-3` for popover chrome, `surface-2` for panels) and provide the same value to JS consumers through the surface context \u2014 `useCdsSurface()`, below.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Purpose\n\n**This is the layer components consume.**\n\n### Roles\n\nEach role maps a semantic meaning to a hue. Property-first pattern: `--fill-{role}` (solid hue-450), `--fill-{role}-hover` (hue-400), `--bg-{role}` (hue-100 / dark hue-800), `--border-{role}` (solid hue-250 in light / hue-700 in dark), `--text-{role}` (600 fg). Warning's fill diverges: yellow-200 / hover yellow-250. Brand uses named `clay-emphasized` / hover `clay` (not hue stops).\n\n| Role      | Hue    | Tokens                                                                                                               |\n| --------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `accent`  | blue   | `--fill-accent{,-hover}`, `--bg-accent`, `--bg-accent-muted`, `--border-accent`, `--text-accent` |\n| `brand`   | clay   | `--fill-brand{,-hover}`, `--on-brand` (fill-only \u2014 no text/bg/border)                                        |\n| `danger`  | red    | `--fill-danger{,-hover}`, `--bg-danger`, `--border-danger`, `--text-danger`                          |\n| `success` | green  | `--fill-success{,-hover}`, `--bg-success`, `--border-success`, `--text-success`                      |\n| `warning` | yellow | `--fill-warning{,-hover}`, `--bg-warning`, `--border-warning`, `--text-warning`                      |\n| `pro`     | purple | `--fill-pro{,-hover}`, `--bg-pro`, `--border-pro`, `--text-pro`                                      |\n\n`accent` additionally carries `--bg-accent-muted` (a 10% `fill-accent` wash over transparent, `color-mix` in srgb): an accent wash one weight below `bg-accent`, for tinted-but-quiet accent surfaces \u2014 like a reacted reaction pill \u2014 where `bg-accent`'s solid hue-100/800 reads too heavy.\n\n#### `git-*` roles\n\nDiff and PR/CR-state colors \u2014 `added`, `removed`, `modified`, `conflicting`, `merged`, `closed`, `draft`, plus `opened`/`queued` as aliases of `added`/`modified`. Each carries the full `text` / `fill{,-hover}` / `bg` / `border` / `on` suite. Values come from `@ant/epitaxy`'s `--extended-*` palette (not CDS ramp stops), so migrating claude.ai's diff UI onto these tokens is a rename; `fill` light is the Epitaxy hue darkened just enough for white `on-git-*` to pass AA.\n\n### Background vs. fill\n\nBoth are backgrounds; the split is saturation, and therefore which foreground token pairs on top.\n\n`bg-{role}` is the pale tint (hue-100 light / hue-800 dark) for passive status surfaces \u2014 Banner, Badge, chip. Light enough that `text-{role}` (hue-600) reads against it: a danger banner is `bg-danger` + `text-danger`. `fill-{role}` is the saturated solid (hue-450) for interactive controls \u2014 button, checkbox, toggle. Too dark for `text-{role}`, so it pairs with `on-{role}` (gray-0 / gray-900) instead; the 450 stop is chosen for WCAG contrast against `on-*`.\n\n|       | Background    | Foreground    | Example       |\n| ----- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- |\n| Tint  | `bg-{role}`   | `text-{role}` | Banner, Badge |\n| Solid | `fill-{role}` | `on-{role}`   | Button        |\n\nThe token name encodes the pairing: use `bg-*` when the hue is ambient context behind body text; `fill-*` when the hue _is_ the control surface.\n\n### Purpose tokens\n\n| Token                        | Value (light)                                     | Use case                                         |\n| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |\n| `--text-primary`         | `neutral-900`                                     | Body text                                        |\n| `--text-secondary`       | `neutral-600`                                     | Supporting text                                  |\n| `--text-muted`           | `neutral-400`                                     | Placeholder, captions                            |\n| `--text-disabled`        | `alpha-4`                                         | Disabled labels                                  |\n| `--border`               | `alpha-2`                                         | Default 1px hairline                             |\n| `--border-strong`        | `alpha-3`                                         | Emphasized divider                               |\n| `--border-stronger`      | `neutral-900 / 40%`                               | Heavy divider                                    |\n| `--fill-primary`         | `neutral-900`                                     | Primary button bg                                |\n| `--fill-primary-hover`   | `neutral-750`                                     |                                                  |\n| `--fill-secondary`       | `hsl(0 0% 100% / 0.1)`                            | Secondary button bg                              |\n| `--fill-secondary-hover` | `alpha-1`                                         |                                                  |\n| `--fill-secondary-ring`  | `border` (light) / transparent (dark)             | Secondary button ring                            |\n| `--fill-field`           | `hsl(0 0% 100% / 0.5)` (light) / `alpha-1` (dark) | Field control bg (TextInput, TextArea, Combobox) |\n| `--fill-field-ring`      | `border` (light + dark)                           | Field control resting ring                       |\n| `--fill-ghost-hover`     | `alpha-1` (light) / 7.5% white (dark half-step)   | Ghost button / row hover bg                      |\n| `--fill-ghost-selected`  | `alpha-2` (light) / 15% white (dark half-step)    | Ghost row / nav item selected bg                 |\n| `--fill-control`         | `alpha-2`                                         | Avatar fallback bg                               |\n| `--fill-control-hover`   | `alpha-3`                                         |                                                  |\n| `--fill-disabled`        | `alpha-1`                                         | Disabled control bg                              |\n| `--on-primary`           | `neutral-0`                                       | Text on `fill-primary`                           |\n| `--on-accent`            | `gray-0`                                          | Text on `accent`                                 |\n| `--on-brand`             | `gray-0`                                          | Text on `brand`                                  |\n| `--on-danger`            | `gray-0`                                          | Text on `danger`                                 |\n| `--on-success`           | `gray-900`                                        | Text on `success`                                |\n| `--on-warning`           | `gray-900`                                        | Text on `warning`                                |\n| `--on-pro`               | `gray-0`                                          | Text on `pro`                                    |\n| `--focus-shadow`         | `0 0 0 1px accent, 0 0 6px 1px bg-accent`         | `focus-visible` ring                             |\n| `--shadow-sm`            | two-layer via `--shadow-color`                | Low elevation                                    |\n| `--shadow-md`            | two-layer via `--shadow-color`                | Card / panel                                     |\n| `--shadow-lg`            | two-layer via `--shadow-color`                | Dialog / sheet                                   |\n| `--shadow-popover`       | `0 8px 24px /12%, 0 2px 6px /8%`                  | Menu, dropdown popups                            |\n| `--surface-popover`      | `surface-3`                                       | Named alias                                      |\n| `--surface-panel`        | `surface-2`                                       | Named alias                                      |\n\n`--shadow-sm/md/lg` are two-layer composites (contact + diffused drop) driven by `--shadow-color`, which deepens to `black/24%` in dark mode (epitaxy parity). `--shadow-popover` is a fixed two-layer literal tuned for floating menus.\n\n---\n\n## CDS content\n\nHow to write the words that go inside cds components. Tokens decide how the UI _looks_; this decides how it _sounds_.\n\nThe voice is **intelligent, warm, unvarnished, and collaborative** \u2014 your smartest friend explaining something in plain terms. Friendly lives in the copy, not in extra chrome.\n\n## Mechanics\n\n- **Sentence case everywhere.** Buttons, headings, tabs, labels, menu items. \"Save changes\", not \"Save Changes\". Title Case is for proper nouns only (Claude, Opus, Anthropic Console).\n- **No terminal punctuation on labels and headings.** Helper text, descriptions, and empty-state body copy _do_ end with a period.\n- **Use contractions.** \"Can't\", \"you'll\", \"it's\". Conversational, not stiff.\n- **Active voice, verb first.** \"Delete project\", not \"Project deletion\".\n- **Ellipsis = in progress only.** \"Claude is thinking\u2026\". Not for trailing off, not for menu suffixes.\n- **No ampersands.** Spell out \"and\".\n- **Serial comma.** \"Chats, projects, and artifacts.\"\n\n## Pronouns\n\nUI speaks as the product, not as Claude and not as the user.\n\n| Context          | Use               | Example                                                 |\n| ---------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |\n| User's things    | **your**          | \"Your projects\" \u2014 never \"My projects\"                   |\n| Confirmations    | none / past tense | \"Saved\", \"Got it\" \u2014 never \"I saved it\"                  |\n| Errors           | **you / your**    | \"Your session expired\" \u2014 never \"I couldn't\u2026\"            |\n| Claude (in chat) | **I**             | Reserved for the chat surface; system UI never says \"I\" |\n\n## Words to avoid\n\n| Skip                                        | Why                                   | Instead          |\n| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------- |\n| \"successfully\"                              | The success toast _is_ the success    | \"File uploaded\"  |\n| \"please\"                                    | UI isn't asking a favor               | \"Enter a name\"   |\n| \"Click here\" / \"Tap to\u2026\"                    | Link text should name the destination | \"Read the docs\"  |\n| \"!\" on system copy                          | Reads as shouty                       | \"Settings saved\" |\n| \"leverage\", \"seamless\", \"unlock\", \"empower\" | Corporate filler                      | Say what it does |\n| \"simply\", \"just\", \"easy\"                    | Presumes \u2014 and condescends            | Cut it           |\n\n## Patterns\n\n**Buttons / CTAs** \u2014 verb first, 1\u20133 words, sentence case, no punctuation. \"Create project\", \"Upgrade to Pro\". Not \"OK\", \"Submit\", or \"Click to continue\".\n\n**Errors** \u2014 say what happened, then what to do. One sentence, no \"Error:\" prefix, no first person. \"That name's already taken. Try another.\" Never surface raw exception strings.\n\n**Empty states** \u2014 an invitation, not an apology. Headline names the space (\"Start your first project\"), one-line body explains it, CTA is a verb (\"Create project\"). Skip \"Nothing here yet.\"\n\n**Placeholders** \u2014 a real example of valid input (\"name@company.com\", \"Summarize this document\"). No \"e.g.\" prefix, don't repeat the field label.\n\n**Links** \u2014 describe where they go (\"Learn more\", \"View pricing\").                         "start_timestamp": "2026-08-20T14:00:29.162395Z",

                        "flags": null,
                        "type": "text",
                        "text": "Here's the quick reasoning behind each:\n\n**Option 1 (image-card grid)** \u2014 most visual, best if your category images are strong. When we build it in Elementor, those coloured squares become your actual category images with a subtle dark overlay + white text. Very \"Nike/Zara\" feel.\n\n**Option 2 (split preview)** \u2014 the most interactive and premium-feeling. Hovering each category on the left updates the right side with a description + 3 featured products from that category. Takes the most work to build (needs dynamic content per category), but users love it.\n\n**Option 3 (icon columns)** \u2014 cleanest and fastest to load. Good if your niche is utilitarian (electronics, tools, auto parts). Feels a bit generic for fashion/lifestyle.\n\n**Option 4 (featured highlight)** \u2014 great if you have a hero category you always want to push (bestseller, new arrivals, seasonal). Draws the eye immediately to what you're promoting.\n\nOnce you pick one, we'll circle back to build the Product Archive template first (as planned), then build this menu in Elementor.\n\nWhich one speaks to you? Also \u2014 what does your store sell? That'll help me tailor the actual build (icons, copy, whether we should push a featured category, etc.).",
                        "citations": []
                    }
                ],
                "sender": "assistant",

            {
                "uuid": "01a01f7a-c933-7aa1-9584-c2ef02a0dad0",
                "text": "pick the one according to you whichever you seems to be the best for mobile view, as most of the users are going to be the mobile based visitors I guess.",
                "content": [

                        "start_timestamp": "2026-08-20T14:02:20.368092Z",
                        "stop_timestamp": "2026-08-20T14:02:20.368092Z",
                        "flags": null,
                        "type": "text",
                        "text": "pick the one according to you whichever you seems to be the best for mobile view, as most of the users are going to be the mobile based visitors I guess.",

                "sender": "human",
                "created_at": "2026-08-20T14:02:20.368292Z",
                "updated_at": "2026-08-20T14:02:20.368292Z",
                "attachments": [],
                "files": [],
                "parent_message_uuid": "01a01f78-01fe-761e-b9bd-2cd5cd05c141"
            },
            {
                "uuid": "01a01f7a-c933-7dec-ae90-aa7beb5cedee",
                "text": "Good instinct \u2014 mobile-first thinking is right for e-commerce, especially in most markets today where 70%+ of traffic is mobile.\n\n## My pick: Option 3 (Icon columns)\n\nHere's why, specifically for mobile:\n\n**Mega menus don't exist on mobile.** This is the key thing most people miss. On mobile, your \"hover mega menu\" gets replaced by a **hamburger menu \u2192 tap Categories \u2192 see a list**. So the fancy split-preview (Option 2) and featured-highlight (Option 4) layouts get flattened into a plain vertical list anyway. Building complex desktop mega menus that mobile users never see is wasted effort.\n\nOption 3 translates most naturally:\n- **Desktop:** 4 columns \u00d7 2 rows of icon + text \u2014 clean, scannable, fast\n- **Mobile:** collapses to a single-column list of icon + text \u2014 *exactly* the same pattern, just stacked. No jarring redesign, no broken layouts, no images that eat mobile data.\n\n**Other reasons it wins for mobile-heavy traffic:**\n\n1. **Lightweight** \u2014 no background images loading = faster on 3G/4G. LiteSpeed Cache will love you.\n2. **Thumb-friendly** \u2014 each icon+text row is a big tap target when stacked vertically.\n3. **Scales to any category count** \u2014 if you add a 9th or 10th category later, it just adds a row. Options 1 and 4 break their grid math.\n4. **Icons help recognition** \u2014 on mobile with less screen space, an icon next to the label helps users scan faster than text alone.\n\n## One upgrade I'd recommend on top of Option 3\n\nInstead of generic Tabler icons, use **your actual category images as small circular thumbnails** (like 32\u00d732 rounded) next to each category name. This gives you the visual richness of Option 1 but keeps the compact, mobile-friendly structure of Option 3. Best of both worlds.\n\nSo the final direction is: **icon/thumbnail + category name, 4-column grid on desktop, single-column stack on mobile.**\n\n## Now let's actually build stuff\n\nReady to move to **Step 1 \u2014 the Product Archive template** in Elementor? That's the page users land on when they click a category from the menu. I'll walk you through it section by section (Elementor Theme Builder \u2192 settings \u2192 widgets to use \u2192 configuration).\n\nAlso, one quick heads-up on mobile menus in Elementor: the default hamburger from Elementor's Nav Menu widget is fine, but the **Mega Menu widget** (newer) has better mobile handling built in \u2014 it auto-converts your mega menu into an accordion-style mobile drawer. We'll use that one.\n\nShall we start on the archive template?",

                "text": "Great \u2014 Option 4 it is. Bold choice; it works really well when you rotate the featured category seasonally (bestseller now, sale category later, new arrivals next month).\n\n## Font recommendation\n\nSince I don't know your exact brand vibe yet, let me give you my **default safe-but-premium pairing** that works for almost any e-commerce store, plus 2 alternatives depending on your niche.\n\n### My top pick: Inter + Instrument Serif\n\n- **Headings:** Instrument Serif \u2014 a modern serif with elegance, feels editorial and premium without being stuffy. Great for product names, category titles, hero text.\n- **Body:** Inter \u2014 the most legible sans-serif on screens today. Used by Notion, GitHub, Vercel. Reads beautifully at any size on mobile.\n\nThis pairing gives you a **\"editorial magazine meets modern tech\"** feel \u2014 works for fashion, lifestyle, beauty, home goods, jewelry, food, and most premium/mid-premium brands. Both are free on Google Fonts.\n\n### Alternatives based on your niche\n\n- **If your store is bold/streetwear/gym/tech:** Headings in **Space Grotesk**, body in **Inter**. More geometric, energetic.\n- **If your store is minimal/luxury/wellness:** Headings in **Fraunces**, body in **DM Sans**. Softer, warmer, high-end feel.\n\n**All of these load fast** (important with LiteSpeed) and have full weight ranges. In Elementor: `Site Settings \u2192 Global Fonts` \u2014 set primary = your body font, secondary = your heading font, and they'll cascade across the whole site.\n\nQuick question so I know which pairing fits: **what does your store sell?** (I've been guessing this whole time \u2014 knowing the niche will sharpen every recommendation going forward, including the archive page design we're about to build.)\n\n## Now \u2014 the Archive Page\n\nWhile you tell me the niche, here's the plan for the Product Archive template. This one template will apply to your Shop page AND every category page automatically.\n\n### The structure I recommend (top to bottom)\n\n1. **Breadcrumbs** \u2014 `Home > Shop > Category name`. Small, muted. Good for SEO (Yoast reads these) and lets users navigate back.\n2. **Category hero section** \u2014 big title (category name) + category description + optional category image as a background banner. On the plain Shop page, this shows \"Shop\" + a generic tagline.\n3. **Filter/sort bar** \u2014 a horizontal bar with: results count on the left (\"Showing 24 of 95 products\"), sort dropdown on the right (Price low-high, newest, popularity).\n4. **Two-column layout below:**\n   - **Left sidebar (25%):** filters \u2014 price range slider, product categories list, filter by attribute (size/color/brand if you have them), filter by rating\n   - **Right main area (75%):** the product grid \u2014 3 columns on desktop, 2 on tablet, 1 or 2 on mobile\n5. **Pagination** at the bottom \u2014 numbered pages, not infinite scroll (better for SEO and LiteSpeed caching)\n6. **Related categories** section \u2014 3-4 category cards suggesting other categories to browse. Keeps users on-site longer.\n\n### Before I walk you through building each section in Elementor\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n",

                "text": "Got it \u2014 devotional/spiritual imagery is a beautiful niche.                 "uuid": "01a01f86-8455-7ef0-a27d-f82507201f0d",
                "text": "You've spotted the exact problem \u2014 and you're right, what you're building right now is a **static page**, not a **dynamic template**. These are two totally different things in Elementor, and the confusion between them trips up almost everyone.\n\nLet me explain what's happening and how to fix it.\n\n## What you're doing right now (the wrong path)\n\nYou're editing a regular page (`post.php?post=185`) and inside it, you've added a **Products widget** with a hardcoded filter: \"show me products from category = Combos & Gift Sets.\" That's why:\n\n- The title says \"Name of the Category\" (hardcoded text, not dynamic)\n- Breadcrumbs say \"Home / Shop\" (because this page IS a regular page, not a category page)\n- Products are only from one category (because you filtered them manually)\n\nIf you built one page per category this way, you'd need 8 pages, and every new category would need a new page. That's exactly what you want to avoid.\n\n## What you should be doing (the right path)\n\nYou need to build a **Theme Builder \u2192 Product Archive template**. This is a completely different type of thing in Elementor. Here's the difference:\n\n**A page** = one URL with fixed content you designed.\n**A Theme Builder template** = a design \"skin\" that WordPress automatically wraps around any category, tag, or shop URL. The content (title, products, breadcrumbs) gets injected dynamically by WooCommerce based on which URL the user visits.\n\nSo you design **one** Product Archive template, set its display condition to \"All Product Archives,\" and:\n- Visit `/product-category/combos-gift-sets/` \u2192 template shows \"Combos & Gift Sets\" as title + only those products + correct breadcrumbs\n- Visit `/product-category/hanuman/` \u2192 same template shows \"Hanuman\" as title + only those products + correct breadcrumbs\n- Add a new category tomorrow \u2192 it just works, no new page needed\n\nSame design, different content, all automatic.\n\n## How to fix this \u2014 step by step\n\n**Step 1 \u2014 Delete or abandon the page you're building now.** It's the wrong type of thing. Don't waste more time on it.\n\n**Step 2 \u2014 Go to the right place.** In WP admin:\n`Templates \u2192 Theme Builder` (or `Elementor \u2192 Theme Builder` depending on version)\n\nYou'll see a list of template types: Header, Footer, Single Post, Single Product, **Product Archive**, Archive, 404, etc.\n\n**Step 3 \u2014 Click \"Product Archive\" \u2192 Add New Product Archive.** Name it something like \"Main Product Archive.\" Choose \"Start from scratch\" (or pick a starter if you want inspiration).\n\n**Step 4 \u2014 Build the layout using DYNAMIC widgets, not static ones.** This is the key part. Instead of typing \"Name of the Category\" as a heading, you use:\n\n- **Archive Title widget** \u2014 auto-shows the current category name. For Shop page it shows \"Shop\", for /product-category/hanuman/ it shows \"Hanuman.\"\n- **Archive Description widget** \u2014 auto-shows the category description you wrote in `Products \u2192 Categories`.\n- **Breadcrumbs widget** (or Yoast breadcrumbs shortcode) \u2014 auto-generates the correct trail.\n- **Archive Products widget** (NOT the regular Products widget!) \u2014 this is the crucial one. It auto-pulls products belonging to the current archive. No filter, no manual term selection. Just drop it in and it works.\n- **WooCommerce Product Filter widget** \u2014 sidebar filters.\n- **Archive Pagination widget** \u2014 auto-pagination.\n\nThe word \"Archive\" in the widget name is your signal that it's dynamic. Widgets without \"Archive\" in the name are static.\n\n**Step 5 \u2014 Set the Display Conditions.** After you finish designing, click \"Publish\" \u2192 a popup asks WHERE this template should apply. Choose:\n- Include \u2192 **All Product Archives** (this covers the Shop page + every category + every tag)\n\nIf you want a *different* design just for the Shop page vs categories, you can create two templates with different conditions. But start with one.\n\n**Step 6 \u2014 Visit any category URL.** It should now show your template with the correct dynamic data. No more manual filtering.\n\n## The mental model to remember\n\n> \"If I have to type the category name or manually pick which products to show, I'm on the wrong path.\"\n\nEverything in an archive template should come from **dynamic widgets** or **dynamic tags** (Elementor has a little database icon \ud83d\uddc2\ufe0f on many fields \u2014 clicking it lets you pull dynamic data like \"current archive title\" instead of typing static text).\n\n## About the breadcrumbs specifically\n\nTwo options for breadcrumbs:\n\n1. **Elementor's Breadcrumbs widget** \u2014 works but basic.\n2. **Yoast Breadcrumbs** (recommended since you have Yoast Pro) \u2014 better SEO, cleaner output. First enable it in `SEO \u2192 Settings \u2192 Breadcrumbs`, then in Elementor add a Shortcode widget with `[wpseo_breadcrumb]`. It'll auto-generate `Home / Category name` on category pages, `Home / Shop / Product name` on single products, etc.\n\n## Quick check before we go further\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n",

                "text": "Perfect, you're in the right place now. Let's build this cleanly. I'll go section by section.\n\nBefore we start, one quick order swap from what you said: **breadcrumbs should come ABOVE the heading**, not below. This is the universal convention \u2014 users expect the \"you are here\" trail at the very top so they can orient themselves before reading the page title. Every major e-commerce site does this (Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Zara). Trust me on this one.\n\nSo the final order top-to-bottom is:\n1. Breadcrumbs (small, muted)\n2. Category heading (big, bold)\n3. Category description (optional, small line under heading)\n4. Products grid\n\nLet's build.\n\n## Section 1 \u2014 Breadcrumbs\n\n**In Elementor editor:**\n\n1. Drag a new **Section** to the top (single column, full width).\n2. Set section padding: top 30px, bottom 10px (Advanced tab \u2192 Padding).\n3. Inside it, drag the **Shortcode widget** (search \"shortcode\" in the widget panel).\n4. In the shortcode field, paste: `[wpseo_breadcrumb]`\n\n**Before this works, enable Yoast breadcrumbs:**\nOpen a new tab \u2192 `SEO \u2192 Settings \u2192 Site features \u2192 Breadcrumbs \u2192 toggle ON \u2192 Save`.\n\n**Style the breadcrumbs** (Style tab on the Shortcode widget):\n- Text color: a muted grey like `#8a8a8a`\n- Typography: your body font (DM Sans), size 13px, weight 400\n- Alignment: Left\n\nNow the breadcrumb will auto-generate `Home / Category name` on category pages, `Home / Shop` on the shop page, `Home / Shop / Category / Product name` on single products. Fully dynamic.\n\n## Section 2 \u2014 Category heading + description\n\n**Same section as breadcrumbs, or a new one below it \u2014 your choice. I'd keep them in one section for tighter spacing.**\n\n1. Under the breadcrumbs, drag the **Archive Title widget** (search \"archive title\").\n2. In the widget settings:\n   - HTML Tag: **H1** (important for SEO \u2014 the category name should be the page's H1)\n   - Alignment: Left (or Center if you prefer \u2014 but left is more standard and easier to read)\n3. **Style tab:**\n   - Typography: Fraunces, size 42px on desktop, weight 500 or 600\n   - On mobile (click the mobile icon at top of Style tab, then set size): 28px\n   - Color: your primary dark color (something like `#1a1a1a`, not pure black \u2014 pure black feels harsh with serif fonts)\n\n**Now add the description below:**\n\n4. Drag the **Archive Description widget** right under the title.\n5. Style tab:\n   - Typography: DM Sans, 15px, weight 400, line-height 1.6\n   - Color: muted like `#5a5a5a`\n   - Max width: 700px (so on wide screens the description doesn't stretch too wide and become hard to read)\n\n**Important:** The description only shows if you've written one in `Products \u2192 Categories \u2192 [category] \u2192 Description`. Go add descriptions to all 8 categories later \u2014 even 1-2 sentences helps SEO massively (Yoast will thank you). If a category has no description, this widget just shows nothing, no broken layout.\n\n## Section 3 \u2014 Products grid\n\n**Create a new Section below.** Set it to full width or boxed (your call \u2014 boxed with max-width 1200px is more premium, full-width is more modern).\n\n1. Inside, drag the **Archive Products widget** (search \"archive products\" \u2014 make sure it's the one with \"Archive\" in the name, NOT the regular \"Products\" widget).\n\n2. **Content tab settings:**\n   - **Columns:** 4 (desktop), 3 (tablet), 2 (mobile) \u2014 set each by clicking the device icons\n   - **Rows:** 3 (so 12 products per page on desktop)\n   - **Show:** All (or Sale, Featured \u2014 leave as All)\n   - **Order by:** Menu order (this lets you manually reorder products in WP admin) or Date\n   - **Pagination:** Toggle ON\n\n3. **Style tab \u2014 this is where the visual polish happens:**\n   - **Columns Gap:** 20px (horizontal space between products)\n   - **Rows Gap:** 30px (vertical space)\n   - **Products styling:**\n     - Product image: no border, no shadow (keeps it clean since your products ARE images \u2014 the divine photos)\n     - Product title: DM Sans, 15px, weight 500, color dark grey\n     - Price: DM Sans, 14px, weight 400, your accent color for the current price, strikethrough grey for the old price (Sale price styling)\n     - \"Sale!\" badge: keep it, but restyle later \u2014 the yellow default is ugly\n\n4. **Pagination style:**\n   - Center align\n   - Numbers in a clean row with small padding\n   - Active page: your accent color background\n\n## After building \u2014 critical last step\n\nClick **Publish** button (bottom left of Elementor editor). A popup will appear asking about **Display Conditions**. This is what makes the template actually work.\n\n- Click **Add Condition**\n- Set: `Include \u2192 Product Archive \u2192 All`\n- Save & Close\n\nThis one setting is what tells WordPress: \"Use this template for the Shop page AND every product category AND every product tag automatically.\"\n\n## Test it\n\nAfter saving, visit these URLs in a new tab:\n- `yourstore.test/shop/` \u2192 should show your template with \"Shop\" as the title\n- `yourstore.test/product-category/combos-gift-sets/` \u2192 should show \"Combos & Gift Sets\" as the title, only those products, correct breadcrumbs\n- `yourstore.test/product-category/[any-other-category]/` \u2192 same template, different content\n\nIf all three URLs work with correct dynamic titles and products, you've done it right.\n\n## One thing to skip for now\n\nI said earlier to add filters (sidebar with price range, etc.) and related categories at the bottom. **Let's skip both for now** and get the basic template working first. We can add them in a second pass once you confirm the foundation is solid. Getting overwhelmed with too many widgets at once is how projects stall.\n\n## Go build it\n\nTry building Section 1 (breadcrumbs) first and tell me when it's showing correctly. Then we do Section 2, then Section 3. Send a screenshot after each section if anything looks off, and I'll help you fix it.\n\nReady \u2014 start with the breadcrumbs and let me know how it goes.",

                "uuid": "01a01f96-37f5-750d-bf8a-fa57aad48b3a",
                "text": "Excellent progress! Look at image 5 \u2014 that's your live category page working perfectly. Breadcrumb showing `Home \u00bb Laminated Photos \u00bb Devi & Durga`, dynamic title, 30 products, all automatic. **You've cracked it.** Let me answer each of your questions in order.\n\n## 1. Why the heading showed \"Ultimate Devotion Set (PC)...\" in image 2\n\nBecause you used the **Page Title** dynamic tag, not the **Archive Title** tag. Page Title pulls the title of whatever WordPress considers the \"current post\" \u2014 in the editor preview, that ends up being a random product from your store, which is why it showed a product name.\n\nYou already fixed this in image 3 by switching to **Archive Title**. That's the correct one. \u2705\n\n## 2. Why does the editor show \"Shop\"?\n\nBecause Elementor's editor preview defaults to showing the **Shop archive** for a Product Archive template. It has to preview *something*, and Shop is the parent archive. This is 100% normal.\n\nOn the actual live URLs:\n- `/shop/` \u2192 shows \"Shop\"\n- `/product-category/devi-durga/` \u2192 shows \"Devi & Durga\" (as image 5 proves)\n- `/product-category/hanuman/` \u2192 will show \"Hanuman\"\n\nEditor preview = \"Shop.\" Live = dynamic. That's how it should work.\n\n## 3. Yoast breadcrumb settings (image 1)\n\nYour breadcrumbs are already working on the frontend (image 5 proves it), so you don't need to change much. But two settings worth adjusting:\n\n**Under \"Breadcrumbs for post types\" \u2192 Products:** set the dropdown to **Product categories**. This makes single product pages show `Home \u00bb Laminated Photos \u00bb Devi & Durga \u00bb [Product name]` \u2014 the full trail. Right now it might just show `Home \u00bb Shop \u00bb [Product name]` which is less useful.\n\n**Under \"Breadcrumbs for taxonomies\":** leave everything as None. That section is for something else and you don't need it.\n\n**Separator:** change from `\u00bb` to `/` or `\u203a` if you want a cleaner modern look. Personal preference. `\u00bb` looks a bit dated.\n\n**Bold the last page:** turn this ON. Makes the current page name bold in the breadcrumb, better UX.\n\nSave changes and you're done with Yoast.\n\n## 4. Now the fun part \u2014 make it beautiful + add filtering/sorting\n\nSorting is **already there** \u2014 see the \"Default sorting\" dropdown top-right in image 4? That's built into the Archive Products widget. You can style it but you don't need to add it.\n\nFor **filtering**, we need to restructure the products section into two columns (sidebar + main area). Here's the plan:\n\n### Step A \u2014 Restructure the products section\n\n1. In the Elementor editor, click on the section holding your Archive Products widget.\n2. Change it from **1 column** to **2 columns**.\n3. Set column widths: **left = 25%, right = 75%** (drag the divider, or set numerically in column settings).\n4. **Drag your existing Archive Products widget into the RIGHT column.**\n5. The left column will be your filter sidebar.\n\n### Step B \u2014 Add filter widgets to the left sidebar\n\nIn Elementor's widget panel, search for \"product filter\" \u2014 you'll see several widgets from the WooCommerce group:\n\n- **Product Filter \u2014 Price** (a price range slider)\n- **Product Filter \u2014 Product Categories** (checkbox list of categories \u2014 great since users can jump between your 8 categories from any page)\n- **Product Filter \u2014 Rating** (skip this if you don't have reviews yet)\n- **Product Filter \u2014 Active Filters** (shows currently-applied filters with an \"\u00d7\" to remove them)\n\nDrag these into the left column in this order:\n1. Active Filters (at top)\n2. Price\n3. Product Categories\n\nEach widget has minimal settings \u2014 just drop them in.\n\n### Step C \u2014 Style the sidebar\n\nClick the left column, then Style tab:\n- Background: white or very light cream (`#faf8f4` matches your brand palette)\n- Padding: 20px all around\n- Border-radius: 8px\n- Add a subtle border: `0.5px solid #e5e5e5`\n\nThen for each filter widget:\n- Filter title (like \"Filter by price\"): Fraunces, 16px, weight 500\n- Filter labels/checkboxes: DM Sans, 14px\n- Spacing between filters: 30px gap between widgets\n\n### Step D \u2014 Make it responsive\n\nOn mobile, a sidebar next to products doesn't work \u2014 the products get squished. Two options:\n\n**Option 1 (easier):** Hide the sidebar on mobile. Click the left column \u2192 Advanced tab \u2192 Responsive \u2192 toggle \"Hide on Mobile\" ON. Filters just don't exist on mobile. Not ideal but simple.\n\n**Option 2 (better):** Add a \"Filter\" button at the top that opens the sidebar as a popup on mobile. This needs Elementor's Popup feature \u2014 bit more work. We can do this in a second pass.\n\nStart with Option 1 to keep momentum.\n\n### Step E \u2014 Beautify the product cards\n\nClick your Archive Products widget \u2192 Style tab:\n- **Columns Gap:** 24px\n- **Rows Gap:** 40px\n- **Products \u2192 Image:** border-radius 6px, subtle hover zoom (Advanced tab \u2192 Motion effects)\n- **Products \u2192 Title:** DM Sans, 15px, weight 500, color `#1a1a1a`, margin-top 12px\n- **Products \u2192 Price:** DM Sans, 14px, current price color `#8b1a1a` (matching devotional maroon), old price strikethrough `#999`\n- **Products \u2192 \"Add to cart\" button:** background transparent, border `1px solid #1a1a1a`, text `#1a1a1a`, hover flips to filled black. Simple, elegant.\n- **Products \u2192 Sale badge:** change from the ugly yellow to a small clean pill \u2014 background `#8b1a1a`, text white, border-radius 20px, padding 4px 10px, positioned top-left or top-right.\n\n### Step F \u2014 Result count + sort bar styling\n\nThe \"Showing 1-10 of 95 results\" text and sort dropdown at the top:\n- Result count: DM Sans, 14px, color muted `#666`\n- Sort dropdown: clean border, matching typography, small padding\n\n## Try this and send screenshots\n\nBuild Step A + B first (structure + filters working), then we polish the styling. If any filter widget doesn't appear in your Elementor widget panel, tell me which version of Elementor Pro you have \u2014 some filter widgets require Elementor Pro 3.5+ and WooCommerce to be active (both of which you have).\n\nGo build. Ping me when the sidebar + filters are showing, even if unstyled.",

That's how it should work.\n\n## 3. Yoast breadcrumb settings (image 1)\n\nYour breadcrumbs are already working on the frontend (image 5 proves it), so you don't need to change much. But two settings worth adjusting:\n\n**Under \"Breadcrumbs for post types\" \u2192 Products:** set the dropdown to **Product categories**. This makes single product pages show `Home \u00bb Laminated Photos \u00bb Devi & Durga \u00bb [Product name]` \u2014 the full trail. Right now it might just show `Home \u00bb Shop \u00bb [Product name]` which is less useful.\n\n**Under \"Breadcrumbs for taxonomies\":** leave everything as None. That section is for something else and you don't need it.\n\n**Separator:** change from `\u00bb` to `/` or `\u203a` if you want a cleaner modern look. Personal preference. `\u00bb` looks a bit dated.\n\n**Bold the last page:** turn this ON. Makes the current page name bold in the breadcrumb, better UX.\n\nSave changes and you're done with Yoast.\n\n## 4. Now the fun part \u2014 make it beautiful + add filtering/sorting\n\nSorting is **already there** \u2014 see the \"Default sorting\" dropdown top-right in image 4? That's built into the Archive Products widget. You can style it but you don't need to add it.\n\nFor **filtering**, we need to restructure the products section into two columns (sidebar + main area). Here's the plan:\n\n### Step A \u2014 Restructure the products section\n\n1. In the Elementor editor, click on the section holding your Archive Products widget.\n2. Change it from **1 column** to **2 columns**.\n3. Set column widths: **left = 25%, right = 75%** (drag the divider, or set numerically in column settings).\n4. **Drag your existing Archive Products widget into the RIGHT column.**\n5. The left column will be your filter sidebar.\n\n### Step B \u2014 Add filter widgets to the left sidebar\n\nIn Elementor's widget panel, search for \"product filter\" \u2014 you'll see several widgets from the WooCommerce group:\n\n- **Product Filter \u2014 Price** (a price range slider)\n- **Product Filter \u2014 Product Categories** (checkbox list of categories \u2014 great since users can jump between your 8 categories from any page)\n- **Product Filter \u2014 Rating** (skip this if you don't have reviews yet)\n- **Product Filter \u2014 Active Filters** (shows currently-applied filters with an \"\u00d7\" to remove them)\n\nDrag these into the left column in this order:\n1. Active Filters (at top)\n2. Price\n3. Product Categories\n\nEach widget has minimal settings \u2014 just drop them in.\n\n### Step C \u2014 Style the sidebar\n\nClick the left column, then Style tab:\n- Background: white or very light cream (`#faf8f4` matches your brand palette)\n- Padding: 20px all around\n- Border-radius: 8px\n- Add a subtle border: `0.5px solid #e5e5e5`\n\nThen for each filter widget:\n- Filter title (like \"Filter by price\"): Fraunces, 16px, weight 500\n- Filter labels/checkboxes: DM Sans, 14px\n- Spacing between filters: 30px gap between widgets\n\n### Step D \u2014 Make it responsive\n\nOn mobile, a sidebar next to products doesn't work \u2014 the products get squished. Two options:\n\n**Option 1 (easier):** Hide the sidebar on mobile. Click the left column \u2192 Advanced tab \u2192 Responsive \u2192 toggle \"Hide on Mobile\" ON. Filters just don't exist on mobile. Not ideal but simple.\n\n**Option 2 (better):** Add a \"Filter\" button at the top that opens the sidebar as a popup on mobile. This needs Elementor's Popup feature \u2014 bit more work. We can do this in a second pass.\n\nStart with Option 1 to keep momentum.\n\n### Step E \u2014 Beautify the product cards\n\nClick your Archive Products widget \u2192 Style tab:\n- **Columns Gap:** 24px\n- **Rows Gap:** 40px\n- **Products \u2192 Image:** border-radius 6px, subtle hover zoom (Advanced tab \u2192 Motion effects)\n- **Products \u2192 Title:** DM Sans, 15px, weight 500, color `#1a1a1a`, margin-top 12px\n- **Products \u2192 Price:** DM Sans, 14px, current price color `#8b1a1a` (matching devotional maroon), old price strikethrough `#999`\n- **Products \u2192 \"Add to cart\" button:** background transparent, border `1px solid #1a1a1a`, text `#1a1a1a`, hover flips to filled black. Simple, elegant.\n- **Products \u2192 Sale badge:** change from the ugly yellow to a small clean pill \u2014 background `#8b1a1a`, text white, border-radius 20px, padding 4px 10px, positioned top-left or top-right.\n\n### Step F \u2014 Result count + sort bar styling\n\nThe \"Showing 1-10 of 95 results\" text and sort dropdown at the top:\n- Result count: DM Sans, 14px, color muted `#666`\n- Sort dropdown: clean border, matching typography, small padding\n\n## Try this and send screenshots\n\nBuild Step A + B first (structure + filters working), then we polish the styling. If any filter widget doesn't appear in your Elementor widget panel, tell me which version of Elementor Pro you have \u2014 some filter widgets require Elementor Pro 3.5+ and WooCommerce to be active (both of which you have).\n\nGo build. Ping me when the sidebar + filters are showing, even if unstyled.",

                "text": "No worries about the enter! Let me address both things.\n\n## First \u2014 plugin vs Elementor widgets for filtering/sorting\n\nThis is a really important decision. Let me give you the honest answer:\n\n### Use a dedicated plugin. Here's why:\n\n**Elementor's built-in filter widgets are basic.** They work, but they have limitations:\n- No AJAX by default (page reloads on every filter click \u2014 feels slow, kills UX)\n- Limited filter types (no color swatches, no image swatches, no advanced attribute filters)\n- Styling options are shallow\n- Sorting dropdown is stuck with WooCommerce defaults, hard to restyle\n- No \"filter as chips/pills\" style, no filter counts (e.g. \"Devi & Durga (30)\")\n\n**A dedicated plugin gives you:**\n- AJAX filtering (products update instantly, no page reload)\n- Multiple filter styles (checkbox, radio, dropdown, chips, sliders, color swatches, image swatches)\n- Custom sort options you can add/remove/rename\n- Better mobile experience (built-in \"Filter\" button that opens a drawer)\n- Fully styleable via the plugin's own settings\n\n### My recommendation: **FiboFilters** (free) or **WOOF \u2013 WooCommerce Products Filter** (free)\n\n**FiboFilters** is my top pick \u2014 it's modern, AJAX by default, lightweight, and has a clean UI. Free version covers 95% of what you need. Works perfectly with Elementor.\n\nAlternatives:\n- **WOOF** \u2014 older but very powerful, tons of options (can feel overwhelming)\n- **YITH WooCommerce Ajax Product Filter** \u2014 reliable, well-known\n- **Premium option: FacetWP** ($99/yr) \u2014 the gold standard, but overkill unless your store gets big\n\nFor now: **install FiboFilters (free)**. If you outgrow it later, migrate.\n\n### About sorting specifically\n\nThe default WooCommerce sort dropdown (\"Default sorting\" with options like price low-high, popularity, etc.) \u2014 most filter plugins let you replace this with a custom-styled version, OR you can hide it from the Archive Products widget and add your own via the plugin. Either way, you get full control.\n\n## Second \u2014 hiding the ugly count + sort bar from Archive Products\n\nLook at your Content tab in the screenshot. You have two toggles:\n\n1. **Allow Order** \u2014 this is the sort dropdown (\"Default sorting\"). **Turn it OFF.**\n2. **Show Result Count** \u2014 this is the \"Showing 1-10 of 95 results\" text. **Turn it OFF.**\n\nThat entire top bar will disappear. Clean.\n\nThen you can add them back later in a **custom-designed section above** the products using either:\n- The filter plugin's own sort widget (styled how you want)\n- A custom heading like \"95 products in Devi & Durga\" written with a dynamic tag\n- A styled dropdown you design yourself\n\n## What I recommend you do right now, in order\n\n**Step 1 \u2014 Turn off Allow Order and Show Result Count.** Clean up the widget first.\n\n**Step 2 \u2014 Install FiboFilters.** Go to `Plugins \u2192 Add New \u2192 search \"FiboFilters\" \u2192 Install \u2192 Activate`.\n\n**Step 3 \u2014 Configure FiboFilters basics.** After activation it usually adds a menu item. Create your first filter group with:\n- Categories filter\n- Price filter\n- (Optional) Attribute filters if you use attributes like \"Size\" or \"Finish\"\n\n**Step 4 \u2014 Add the FiboFilters widget/shortcode to your left sidebar column** in the Archive template (the 25% column we planned).\n\n**Step 5 \u2014 Design your own custom sort/count bar** above the products. Something like:\n\n```\nDevi & Durga \u00b7 30 photos                    [ Sort: Newest \u25be ]\n```\n\nLeft side = dynamic archive title + count. Right side = a styled sort dropdown from the plugin.\n\n## Quick decision before you install\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n",
